News.title: Woman fighting for life after being shot with air rifle as man, 28, and woman, 26, arrested for ‘attempted murder’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

STREET SHOOTING Woman fighting for life after being shot with air rifle as man, 28, and woman, 26, arrested for ‘attempted murder’

COPS have arrested three people after a woman was left fighting for her life after reportedly being shot with an air rifle.

The victim was rushed to hospital with serious injuries following the alleged horror attack yesterday evening.

Police were called to Windsor Street in Thurnscoe, near Barnsley, at around 9.50pm yesterday after reports of a person with a suspected firearm.

It was reported that a woman had been shot with an air rifle.





Officers and ambulance crews raced to the scene and the woman was taken to hospital for treatment.

She suffered serious injuries and remains in hospital in a stable but life-threatening condition.

Cops recovered an air rifle from the scene before launching a search for the suspect.

A 26-year-old woman was arrested at the scene on suspicion of attempted murder.



She remains in custody.

Then today, cops arrested two more people as the investigation continued.

A 28-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

A 37-year-old man was also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.



Both men remain in police custody.

A police scene remains in place on Windsor Street as detectives continue their investigation.

DI Claire Moss, from the Armed Crime Team, said: “The thoughts of all those involved in this investigation remain with the victim and her family in the wake of such a vicious attack.

“I am thankful for the work of the first officers at the scene and emergency services staff who attended the scene and provided essential and immediate medical care to the victim.

“We are carrying out detailed inquiries to get a better understanding of the circumstances which resulted in the victim being seriously injured.



“If you saw what happened yesterday evening, or have any information which may assist our enquiries, please get in touch online or by calling 101, quoting incident number 1076 of 1 September 2026.”

News.title: Burnham urged to stop stitch-up as French promise just 45 more small boat cops on day Bayeux Tapestry displayed in UK
News.content:
Andy Burnham was last night urged to prevent a stitch-up by the French after viewing the returned Bayeux Tapestry.

President Emmanuel Macron will today promise just 45 extra cops for the small-boats crisis.



He and the PM were at the British Museum to see the medieval embroidery depicting King Harold getting shot in the eye with an arrow in 1066.

They then held talks, with Mr Burnham urged to confront Mr Macron over a Dunkirk detention centre that is still incomplete, despite being paid for by the UK three years ago.



It was part of a £1billion package announced under the Tories and extended by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “It’s shocking that it’s not operational. Forget the Bayeux Tapestry, this is a stitch-up.”



No10 will hail a fall in Channel crossings, with this summer seeing the fewest since 2020.

But more than 16,000 migrants have arrived this year amid a change in tactics by gangs, with a record 230 on a mega-dinghy last month.



An extra 45 French cops are to be sent to beaches to help. An intelligence and judicial unit is also rising from 18 to 30 officers.

But Mr Philp claimed he recently witnessed ten armed French cops “standing around doing nothing” as around 100 migrants boarded a boat.

He said: “A gendarme said they had orders not to intervene. The £660million we pay should be withheld until they stop all embarkations in shallow waters.”



Meanwhile, the future of the controversial “one in, one out” returns deal is also said to be under threat. It was extended into autumn, with the Home Office saying more than 1,400 arrivals have been removed.

But French reports say Paris has been pushing for it to be scrapped in the longer term.

The PM insists the latest figures show cooperation is working, but he added: “We cannot be complacent. Smuggling gangs are constantly adapting their tactics, and the UK and France need to respond quickly and stay one step ahead.”



Ms Mahmood said: “We are boosting officer numbers to record highs to crack down on small boat launches and the gangs behind them.”

News.title: Kemi Badenoch pledges £10bn a year to boost defence spending by 2030 – with welfare cuts planned
News.content:
KEMI Badenoch has pledged a £10billion a year boost to defence spending by 2030 — via huge welfare cuts.

The Tory leader’s savings would include £4billion from housing benefit reforms and £3billion by reimposing the two-child benefit cap.



If she wins office, she would also scrap the Chagos Islands deal.

Ms Badenoch has heaped pressure on PM Andy Burnham and his Chancellor John Healey to urgently spell out plans to hit three per cent of GDP on defence by 2030.



She said: “The first duty of every government is defence — and the Conservatives will always put our defence first.

“That’s why we are setting out our plans to reach three per cent on defence spending by the end of this parliament.

“John Healey resigned from Keir Starmer’s government saying Labour weren’t keeping our country safe.

“Now he is Chancellor he should adopt our plans and make sure our armed forces have the funding they need.”

At Mr Burnham’s first Prime Minister’s Questions in the job, Labour MP Tan Dhesi, who chairs the Defence select committee, told the PM “vibes alone are not going to be enough”.

He added that rather than “kicking the can down the road” the PM should commit to three per cent by 2030.



Mr Burnham replied he had “made that commitment very clear”.

But Government sources have pointed to the Chancellor saying this week that the target date would be set out at the spending review in the spring.

Mr Healey quit as Defence Secretary in June during Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership over the Armed Forces spending plan.



Lord Dannatt, the former head of the British Army, told Times Radio last night: “My heart bleeds for John Healey.

“He resigned over Keir Starmer’s unwillingness and Rachel Reeves’ inability to fund defence.

“He now realises the wider financial issues that the Government has got.”

News.title: Footage shows boy racers causing ‘pure chaos’ on roundabout as locals warn someone will be killed weeks after A66 crash
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment thuggish boy racers cause “pure chaos” as they tear around a busy residential roundabout.

Footage shows cars racing at high speed and making dangerous turns as crowds of yobs gather around the road to watch.



The clips were filmed in Dartford, Kent, where residents say groups of predominantly young men regularly gather to race and speed.

Drivers can be seen hurtling around roundabouts while crowds line the roads and entrances to nearby estates.



Locals say they are being “terrorised” by the late-night meets, with fears someone will be killed.

One mum said the meets had turned Friday and Saturday nights, as well as Sundays, into “hell”.

She said: “Everyone weekend, Friday and Saturday nights and Sunday are hell.

“There’s organised meet-ups, with terrible sorting. It’s hell.



“They drift around the roundabouts at high speed.

“The spectators block the entrance to the local estates. It’s a nightmare.

“There’s groups of dozens of them. It’s so disruptive.

“Someone will end up getting killed. They are dicing with death.”

Another mum, Sonia, 32, said: “We’re being terrorised. It’s pure chaos.”



The issue has now been raised in Parliament, with Dartford MP Jim Dickson comparing the behaviour to the circumstances surrounding the deaths of two police officers and five teens.

PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, were killed in a horror crash on the A66 near Middlesbrough last month.

The two officers were in a marked armed response vehicle when it was hit head-on by a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way along the road.



Five young men travelling in the Passat also died in the devastating collision on August 22.

They were named as Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.

The tragedy has renewed fears over the dangers posed by reckless driving and illegal racing on Britain’s roads.

In Parliament, Mr Dickson said Dartford residents had experienced “very similar” incidents involving racing and speeding.

He told MPs: “My constituency of Dartford has experienced very similar, deeply antisocial and incredibly dangerous experiences of racing and speeding on our roads.



“Groups of predominantly young men gathering along our roads, watching cars, speeding down those busy roads as content is filmed to be posted on social media.

“This activity is clearly dangerous for other road users, really disruptive for local residents.

“Would the Home Secretary agree with me that we must do absolutely everything we can to tackle this lawlessness.”



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood thanked the MP for bringing the issue to her attention.

The Dartford footage comes amid a series of devastating road tragedies involving dangerous driving.

Just days before the A66 crash, five teenagers were killed in a separate wrong-way motorway smash in Ireland.

The teenagers were travelling in a stolen BMW the wrong way along the M9 in County Kildare after police tried to stop them.

The BMW then smashed into a Hyundai carrying innocent members of a family.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Three sisters and a seven-year-old boy were seriously injured in the devastating collision.

Now Dartford residents fear it is only a matter of time before reckless driving at the late-night meets ends in another tragedy.

News.title: Major motorway closed overnight as jack-knifed HGV blocks lanes after serious crash between two lorries and car
News.content:
A STRETCH of the M25 will remain shut overnight after a horror lorry crash saw a truck “jack-knifed” and diesel spilled everywhere.

The huge lorry ended up sideways across the anti-clockwise carriageway at junction 27 for the M11 near Epping, Essex.



Its fuel tank ruptured in the smash, sending diesel leaking across the road and sparking a major emergency response.

Essex Police, Essex Fire and Rescue and National Highways crews all rushed to the scene in the height of rush hour.



Drivers face a nightmare with the motorway set to remain closed overnight while the carriageway is resurfaced.

National Highways said: “No serious injuries were reported from the collision.

“However, one of the lorries has ‘jack-knifed’ and is sideways across all lanes.

“The fuel tank of this lorry has ruptured, resulting in its diesel leaking over all lanes.”

An Essex Police spokesperson added: “We are currently at the scene of a collision involving two lorries and a car on the anti-clockwise carriageway of the M25, close to junction 27/ junction 6 of the M11.

“The collision was reported at about 4.35 pm – we are attending with colleagues from the ambulance and fire services and National Highways.



“A road closure is in place while emergency services work at the scene, and we thank you for your patience.

“Drivers should check before they travel and plan their journeys accordingly.”

Traffic from the M11 northbound or southbound joining the M25 anti-clockwise is not affected.

However, other traffic approaching junction 27 is being diverted.

A diversion is in place via the M11 southbound to the A406 westbound, then the A10 northbound to rejoin the M25 at junction 25.



National Highways has advised drivers to allow extra time for their journeys and consider alternative routes.

A spokesman added: “If this closure impacts on your planned route, please allow extra journey time.

“Plan ahead, you may wish to re-route or even delay your journey.”

The diversion route is as follows: Exit the M25 at J27 onto the M11 southbound and continue to J4.

Exit the M11 onto the A406 headed westbound and continue for approx. 6 miles to the junction with A10.

Take the A10 headed northbound to re-join the M25 at J25.

News.title: Tributes pour in for ‘caring and selfless’ woman, 19, who died when car crashed into tree as driver, 23, arrested
News.content:
IMMEASURABLE VOID Tributes pour in for ‘caring and selfless’ woman, 19, who died when car crashed into tree as driver, 23, arrested

TRIBUTES have poured in for a “beautiful and selfless” teenage girl who died following a horror car crash – as cops arrest the driver.

Harriet Boyles, 19, suffered serious injuries after a Ford smashed into a tree in Armitage, Staffordshire.

Police and emergency crews raced to reports of an accident at 1:35am on Lichfield Road.



Harriet was badly wounded and rushed to hospital on Saturday, August 22 – but tragically succumbed to her injuries four days later.



The teen had been elected as Head Girl at her school and was due to start an apprenticeship in finance.

In a heartbreaking tribute, her family wrote: “Harriet was a beautiful young woman whose kindness, warmth and caring nature touched everyone who knew her.

“Family meant everything to Harriet. She treasured every moment spent with her loved ones and brought joy, laughter, and comfort wherever she went.

“Her caring personality and selfless nature made her a devoted daughter, sister, relative and friend, and she will be deeply missed by all who had the privilege of knowing her.”

The teenager had also been an organ donor with her family noting that even in her passing Harriet’s “generosity and selflessness continued to shine”.

“Through the gift of organ donation, she helped to save and transform the lives of others by donating six organs.”

Police have arrested a 23-year-old man from Newcastle-under-Lyme on suspicion of driving offences.



He has been released on bail while a probe into Harriet’s death continues.

Officers are appealing to the public for dashcam footage of the night on Lichfield Road on 22 August to help with investigations.

News.title: Kemi had Andy Burnham beetroot red at PMQs… but it’s Britain’s finances that should leave us blushing
News.content:
OH God, Kemi Badenoch, the Leader of the Opposition, wasn’t trying to flirt with Andy Burnham at his first Prime Minister’s Questions, was she?

Bad news, it looked like she was — and Kemi wanted to congratulate him on: “His stamina.”



“Three hours he lasted, yesterday,” she continued, while all the time the cost of borrowing was rising and rising and rising.

At which point the PM’s face turned beetroot red — the exact reaction Kemi wanted.



Her sweet-talking was, of course, nothing but a political trap.

“And in all that time, can he name a single spending request for which he answered ‘No’?”



Burnham started to bluster: “Well, what I can say to the Right Honourable Lady is…”

So we’ll take that as “no” then, because Burnham is an old-school socialist fool who could no more turn down a spending request and lower taxes than he could cycle off the end of Brighton pier and land in France.

The PM looked nervous and out of his depth in his new job, which was evident by the number of times his hands fidgeted and he mentioned his comfort blanket “Manchester”.

It would be less worrying if he understood basic economics and could talk himself out of trouble.



But Burnham can do neither and was so rattled by Kemi’s advances on spending and tax that, at one point, he came dangerously close to calling her “my lady”.

Kemi’s problem is she’s inextricably linked to past Conservative failures — a point made by the man who wants to “end cheap political point-scoring”.

“The Leader of the Opposition is on record saying ‘Liz Truss is 100 per cent right’.



“What other thing can I say, Mr Speaker, than God help us?”

Indeed, God help us all.

News.title: What else have you got, Nige? Immigration isn’t the only problem we have – but it’s all Reform will talk about
News.content:
“Labour On Course To Win General Election.”

Wait, what? This notification on my phone makes no sense.



Labour can’t possibly win the next election because Reform UK are nailed-on champs, right?

I mean, Nigel’s lot have been streets ahead in the polls for months.

He’s assembled the, er, cream of the crop of UK politics ready to ride into Downing Street: Braverman, Yusuf, Jenrick, Anderson . . . and Prue Leith’s lad, Danny what’s-his-chops.



Zia Yusuf is already measuring up the curtains in Number 11. (“Sod off Jenrick, I’m having it!”)

Well, it looks like Reform might need to put the Champagne — sorry, English sparkling wine — on ice as a new “poll of polls”(!) has them in second place behind . . . hold each other tight now . . . Labour.

That’s right, Our Andy is predicted to get 26 per cent of the vote, knocking Reform and the Tories into second and third with 24 per cent and 20 per cent respectively.

Oof! What a difference a few weeks makes, eh? Of course, it is easy to dismiss this poll as just a stab in the dark from an erratic polling industry famous for its clangers (although another poll from More In Common 24 hours later had Reform in third place).

But scratch the surface and I think there’s something here, something that tells us where this merry band of upstarts find themselves.



Because even before these polls, Reform UK had started to look like a party coming unstuck.

The “vote for us, we’re better than these clowns” vibes that saw them soar to 35 per cent in one poll last September are fizzling out.

New, much less auspicious, vibes have taken their place. Indeed, in recent weeks Reform have been in the headlines for all the wrong reasons.



Like Farage’s £5million “gift”, rotting round his neck like a putrid albatross and putting off more voters than he cares to accept.

Or Yusuf’s nasty branding of former Army captain Sir Ben Wallace as a “moron” and “traitor to Britain”, spiteful remarks that even his famously blunt boss thought were “too strong”.

Then on Friday, Danny Kruger (that’s the fella!) pissed everyone off by suggesting we should scrap postal voting and therefore cancel our holidays if they happened to clash with an election.

(First rule of life, Danny Boy: don’t f**k with someone’s holiday.)

Of course, like much of Reform’s policies, it was all wrapped up in other punchy ideas addressing Britain’s chronically soft-touch immigration racket. Which is fair enough.



Immigration is the No1 issue on the doorstep. Foreigners sucking at the teat of our broken benefits system and the incessant small boat arrivals (albeit mercifully down by nearly half since last year) are issues that have become so charged they’ve spawned a new right wing party, Rupert Lowe’s batshit Restore Britain.

A more robust approach to immigration is clearly needed.

But Britain’s problems do not start and end with migrants.

Stopping the boats and reducing the number of foreigners granted indefinite leave to remain are no panacea for our crippling cost-of-living crisis.

Reform must convince those still sceptical about a party many view as a one-trick pony that they can tackle the other big issue: Fixing the economy.



So far they have offered little in the way of reassurance as Britain’s national debt hits £3TRILLION.

Eye-catching policies like no income tax until you earn £20,000 have already been binned as a manifesto proposal to make £90billion in tax cuts was scrapped for not being “sensible”.

Few alternative big ideas have materialised. So, beyond some minted backers, it’s no wonder Reform are struggling to attract the support of big business. (Their biggest business backer is crypto boss Christopher Harborne, the man behind Farage’s iffy £5million.)

This time last year, Reform were in Birmingham hosting a party conference that crackled with excitement as pint-wielding delegates in Reform FC football shirts put the world to rights.

Here was a party with their finger on the pulse, a new political force with the world at their feet.



Today they will traipse back into the same NEC halls a lot more battle weary.

The faithful will offer a warm welcome as they raise a glass of IPA to their hero Nigel Farage.

Yet while he drinks in the applause, he will be painfully aware that he needs more than their adulation or that of those spending £3,000 for “platinum” tickets.

If Reform UK are to deliver the Britain they are promising, Farage must speak to everyone outside the walls.

To the huge swathes of undecided voters — like me — eager to know: What else have you got?



X Factor reboot? Get the Crankies

Things must be bad at ITV if they’re even thinking of rebooting the X Factor with cranky old loonies Sharon Osbourne and Louis Walsh on the panel.

Well that’s what I thought when I first read the news in Monday’s Sun.

And then I saw who might be on the panel instead.



Painfully woke stars like Yungblud and Raye might make sense for TikTok, but I can’t imagine for one second they would spew out the kind of bile that Shazza and Louis used to.

It would be all soft soap blah about how great everyone was, so as not to trigger anyone or damage their mental health.

Nah, X Factor only works if the jumped-up acts are cut down to size by the sharpest tongues in the business.

Anything else is just wallpaper.



KEIR AS PM SO STUPID So farewell then, Keir Starmer MP. After 11 years serving the country he was once so passionate about improving, he’s thrown in the towel. I can’t say I’m that surprised he fled the Westminster bear pit so soon after his defenestration. Screw all those backstabbers, time to make some real money from anyone daft enough to give it to him (and there will, inexplicably, be plenty). Of course the truth is he should never have got involved in politics in the first place. He was catastrophically bad at it, as his hopeless tenure in No10 proved. He wasn’t “evil” as some of the more swivel-eyed members of the online right insisted. But he suffered from too much ambition and far too little ability. Labour were stupid to give him the top job. It sounds harsh to say good riddance. But good riddance.

Smaxx of bad smell

Just when I thought Gen Z had maxed out on all their “maxxing” bollocks, along comes another ludicrous phenomena, straight off the red-eye from the good ol’ USA, natch.

This one is called “pheremone-maxxing”, which sees blokes not bothering to shower or wash their hair so they smell like God intended.

The theory, claim aficionados, is simple: Allowing one’s natural pheromones to run riot unimpeded by the aromatic straightjacket of Lynx Africa will help you get more females with whom to mate.

Unsurprisingly, this hogwash is not supported by science.



As dermatologist Dr Shereen Teymour put it: “Not showering isn’t pheromone-maxxing . . . it’s bacteria-maxxing.”

Ladies, form an orderly queue . . .

ARGIE ENZO'S AN OIK Typical Man City stumping up £125million for that Argie spanner, Enzo Fernandez. It may have been nearly two months, but I still can’t get the image of him taunting our fans after he scored against us at the World Cup out of my mind. What a ghastly oik he is. So I feel nothing but pity for all those City fans having to cheer for this arrogant pleb. They’d better get used to all the boos from their opponents’ fans. My vocal cords are primed and ready for when the Manchester derby rolls round in ten days’ time. Why can’t he have been sold off to some godawful Saudi club so we’d never have to see him again?

Traditionalists are frothing over brewer Timothy Taylor’s new “hipster” dude on its classic Landlord ale.

Out goes the fella who always looked to me like a retired Wales scrum-half now running his local boozer in the Mumbles, and in comes a perky bearded chap.



The issue seems to be the new mascot’s facial fuzz, which is something of an irony given many real ale drinkers famously don’t own a razor.

And the suggestion it’s some kind of Gen Z rebrand is obviously daft.

Our anxious young folk would rather sup a protein shake than anything with alcohol in it.

A kick in the teeth

Dyson has “reinvented” another common electrical device in order to charge the earth for it.



Fresh from screwing £480 out of ladies for its Airwrap hair curler, it’s now conjured up a toothbrush for £420 (plus a £9.99 tube of paste to go with it).

It promises to use AI to spray the gaps in your teeth with water jets as you brush, to blast that hard-to-reach plaque

Right, so it’s a water flosser (£20 on Amazon) combined with an electric toothbrush (also £20).

Of course, Dyson insists its CameraJet is far superior than anything else on the market.

But unless it turns my knackered gnashers into Brad Pitt’s mega-watt grin after one brush, I’ll pass.

News.title: Burnham pressed on economy at first PMQs as borrowing costs surge
News.content:
Andy Burnham said his government would be "grounded in fiscal responsibility" as his first Prime Minister's Questions took place against a backdrop of rising UK borrowing costs.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called on Burnham to say where spending would be cut and how he would deal with the UK's increasing debt, after the cost of borrowing for the UK reached a new 18-year high on Wednesday.

He blamed the previous Tory government, saying the "turbulence on global markets are because of that exposure that they left behind".

Burnham took over from Sir Keir Starmer in July before Parliament's summer recess, meaning Wednesday was the first time he had faced Badenoch at PMQs.

Burnham sought to stress his administration's fiscal responsibility and said ministers were taking steps to reduce debt.

He told MPs: "This will be a government grounded in fiscal responsibility. It will stick to the fiscal rules, but at the same time, we will help reduce cost-of-living pressure on our constituents, and that's the approach that we will take."

Interest rates on government bonds have been going up, with the yield on a 10-year bond at its highest level since 2008, while the yield on a 30-year bond is at its highest since 1998.

This means it costs the government more to borrow over the long term and could constrain its spending choices as the 28 October Budget approaches.

Burnham's PMQs debut came after he used the summer recess to tour the UK, announcing a series of eye-catching policies mainly aimed at tackling the cost of living.

On Wednesday, Badenoch said the prime minister had set out plenty of spending plans but no detail of how he would be paying the bill.

"The markets are clearly worried that we now have a spendthrift prime minister who wants to say yes to everyone but cannot tell us where the money is coming from," she said.

"He needs to pay for all his new promises and he has a choice - higher taxes, more borrowing, or spending cuts.

"Yesterday he said change begins with honesty, so will he be honest and tell us: is he preparing to raise taxes again, yes or no?"

Burnham had earlier said he had already cut taxes, including VAT on energy bills and a cut in business rates for hospitality.

"I've already indicated my first moves were to cut tax, but I'm not going to do what any prime minister has done and write the budget here," he said, adding he and Chancellor John Healey had agreed on an earlier date for the Budget to reduce speculation.

In the Commons, Badenoch also raised comments from economist and cross-bench peer Lord Jim O'Neill, who had been tipped to become Burnham's chief economic adviser, but who ruled out joining Burnham's government.

Speaking to the BBC, Lord O'Neill had praised the PM for "a great first five weeks" which he said had helped lift consumer and business confidence; adding the current spike in market interest rates for government debt would force Labour to start "dealing with the triple lock" on the state pension, and "excessive" welfare spending.

Badenoch pointed to a warning from Lord O'Neill that the prime minister's tone during his Tuesday Commons debut would have unsettled investors, although the peer had also said that spike was mostly mirroring US market upheaval concerning the Iran conflict.

News.title: Faisal Islam: Why bond market wildfire is keeping world leaders up at night
News.content:
The biggest factor pushing up rates is the credibility of the borrowing plans set out by major countries. The increase is not based on fears about countries "going bankrupt".

But it is based on the brutal market equation that if a country wants to borrow more, and to do so without a credible plan, especially if there are doubts over the stability of a given government, it should expect to pay a higher rate.

Influential economists lean on different factors. Mohamed el-Erian told me the AI competition in bond markets was the biggest new factor.

Lord Jim O'Neill, says the recent action has been caused by uncertainty about US policy, and in particular efforts by the US Government to try to manage down surging yields.

This brings us to the UK. The profound and rolling instability of multiple prime ministers, chancellors, policy U-turns and the seeming inability to push through major structural change in this country over the past decades, has attracted a premium.

It was part of Sir Keir Starmer's strategy to try to take on boring reforms and offer markets stability in a bid to lower borrowing costs.

It was a shock to many in the markets that despite a landslide majority, Labour could not push through plans to cut Britain's welfare bill. This added to the ups and downs in the gilt markets - the trade in British government debt.

Actually, there are signs of green shoots in the underlying economy. Economic growth has been faster than peers so far in 2026, despite the energy price spike.

Measures of consumer confidence have ticked back up again. The PM is hoping to build on these signs to help rebuild the economy.

But the ongoing rout in global bond markets raises serious questions about the coherence and detail of Burnham's broader plans.

"More public control" and more support for those struggling with the cost of living sounds like a plan for more spending, while the former could turn off potential investors looking at the country.

Burnham's former economic adviser, Lord O'Neill, told me yesterday that the PM's 10-year plan, expected in November, needs to set out how he will tackle "excessive spending".

Lord O'Neill believes showing investors he can be decisive on the state pension or the welfare bill will give him breathing room to focus on his favoured infrastructure investments.

As interest rates tick up, the trade offs facing the prime minister only get more difficult.

News.title: King hails 'unprecedented' Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London
News.content:
The King and Queen, Macron and his wife Brigitte, and Burnham and his wife Marie-France van Heel were given the chance to see the historic embroidery in the atmospheric darkness of the British Museum.

It's displayed in a long glass illuminated cabinet, with the figures remarkably vivid for something almost a 1,000 years old, and visitors file along, following the story of the Norman invasion.

The royal visitors had a close look at key scenes in the tapestry, including the Coronation of King Harold and his death in battle.

It's filled with details of medieval life and the King commented on Normans pulling a cart with "an enormous amount of wine".

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said the final scene, showing King Harold with an arrow in his eye, was what she found the most dramatic.

"We've just been talking to all the schoolchildren, and that's the bit that they really liked and really registered with them," she said.

"And it's amazing actually that a tapestry that is 1,000 years old can still inspire people to feel such emotion and capture such drama after all this time."

Nandy said she was inspired by the way this epic depiction of conflict had "come to symbolise probably the biggest act of friendship on behalf of the French nation".

Sending the tapestry to the British Museum was announced by Macron during a state visit to the UK in July 2025, as an emblem of the strong partnership between the countries.

There had been fears that moving the fragile tapestry could risk causing damage, but French government sources said display conditions at the British Museum were "ideal".

The French authorities welcomed the way that visitors in London would see the tapestry lying flat, rather than upright, with this believed to be better for the conservation of the fibres.

It also allows viewers to get a clearer view of all the animals, plants and often bawdy images sewn around the margins of the main narrative.

It is believed the final scenes of the tapestry have been lost or destroyed, as it has not always had such careful owners. In the 18th Century, during the French Revolution, it was rescued from being cut up to make covers for soldiers' carts.

News.title: Protests in Spain over government's handling of Ceuta migrant crisis
News.content:
Thousands of people have protested in cities across Spain over the government's handling of the influx of migrants to the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on the north African coast.

Spanish opposition parties accuse Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez of abandoning the residents of Ceuta, while the government says right-wing parties are exploiting the crisis.

On Wednesday a police report said Moroccan security forces had displayed "total permissiveness" during the unprecedented influx, days after SÃ¡nchez insisted Morocco was not responsible.

He has blamed trafficking gangs and misinformation on social media for encouraging people to cross the border. Morocco has denied orchestrating or being involved in the mass crossing.

At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July and although most have returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or scattered across the city's streets or on the beach - leading to unrest in the autonomous city in North Africa and a crisis for SÃ¡nchez.

There have been near-daily protests by locals, with demonstrators calling for the migrants to be sent back to their countries of origin or redistributed across Spain.

Wednesday's rallies were called by city councils across Spain where opposition parties - the conservative Partido Popular (PP) and the far-right Vox party - govern or have significant popularity.

Demonstrators called on SÃ¡nchez to resign.

PP leader Alberto NÃºÃ±ez FeijÃ³o was at the rally in Madrid, where more than 50,000 people gathered, according to government figures.

"A Spanish city has been invaded, occupied and, unfortunately, this happened with the knowledge of the Government of Spain," he said.

Vox leader Santiago Abascal meanwhile said SÃ¡nchez was "at the service, like a lackey, of the Moroccan regime".

There was also a major rally in Ceuta itself, with participants chanting: "Ceuta is not for sale, Ceuta must be defended."

"The response has been inadequate, late and, to top it all, has involved a complete dereliction of duty on the part of the government," 45-year-old teacher David Hernandez told Reuters.

"We cannot be second-class citizens, and our border must not be sidelined."

Pressure on SÃ¡nchez's government has intensified after Spanish media said the report submitted by the National Police's National Immigration and Borders Centre (CENIF) to the National Court pointed to the involvement of Moroccan gendarmes in the migrant crossings.

The police report claimed that the Moroccan police deployment around the border "was clearly smaller than usual" and cited migrants who spoke of a "passive attitude" as the crossings happened.

However the report did not categorically accuse Morocco of being behind the influx.

News.title: ‘I'd be the last to know’: Stars of The Gentlemen react to Meghan reports
News.content:
It has been almost two weeks since reports emerged that the Duchess of Sussex was in talks for a role in The Gentlemen.

At the world premiere for series two of the Netflix show on Wednesday night, stars including Maya Jama, Hugh Bonneville and Theo James remained tight-lipped about the prospect of Meghan joining the cast.

âItâs fascinating to watch, but ultimately itâs a lot of rumour,â James told BBC News, while Jama said: âIâd be the last person to know!â

The showâs executive producer said he didn't want to say yes or no to the reports about Meghan, but added they were looking forward to âmore energy and surprisesâ to come.

The Gentlemen, a comedy action series about a duke turned drug baron, created by Guy Ritchie, was a major hit when it first dropped in 2024.

The show has officially been greenlit for a third series. Talks with Meghan are understood to be in the early stages, but the details of the discussions and any role she might be offered have not yet been revealed.

News.title: Farage tells BBC 'we live in a complainants' society' after questions over Reform funding
News.content:
Asked if he knew whether or not money donated by Fiona Cottrell had come from her son George, Farage said he was not "involved in the transactions".

However, he added that he "had been told it's her money". Reform has insisted it has always complied with donations rules.

He added: "The point is, we live in a complainants' society. If you complain about me, automatically that triggers an investigation."

He said that political parties were "constantly writing to all the authorities", meaning Reform was "under investigation every day for virtually everything we do".

"There's a big picture here. The old two-party system that has dominated since the end of the First World War feels for the first time it faces an existential threat.

"There is a whole ecosystem with a century of development around this. And we come along from virtually nowhere and threaten the whole thing.

"So I think what you're seeing is the establishment, in a very co-ordinated way, fighting back."

Pressed on what he meant, he added: "I'm talking about normal human behaviour.

"People who hold positions of power, influence and money don't want new kids on the block succeeding. It's the whole ecosystem, it's everything."

Farage said he expected it "won't be too long" before he is interviewed by Parliament's standards commissioner Daniel Greenberg as part of his probe into whether he should have publicly declared the Â£5m he received from Harborne.

He continued to insist the sum, which he says was a personal gift, did not require registration under Commons rules.

He added he had "no questions" about Greenberg's impartiality, but hit out at the "political composition" of the standards committee that will recommend what action should be taken on his findings.

The 14-member panel includes seven MPs from Labour, the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats, but none from Reform UK.

He added: "Have you seen who's on the committee? I think we know the outcome already. I'm not going to say anything more than that."

"To be judged by members of Parliament by other political parties who you're fighting against in by-elections or general elections, I think that raises a question, I really do," he added.

News.title: Four in court over murder of baby stabbed to death
News.content:
Two men and two women have appeared in court charged with murdering a baby girl who had been repeatedly stabbed at a house in Sheffield.

The newborn - referred to as Baby S in court - was found at a property in Holywell Heights, in the Wincobank area, on Sunday, having suffered 33 wounds from 15 separate stabbings.

Andrea Skopova, 20, formerly of Robey Street, Sheffield, and Peter Horvath, 19, Nina Horvathova, 37, and Peter Horvath, 38, all of Holywell Heights, appeared at Sheffield Magistrates' Court.

The four Slovakian nationals have been charged with murder, causing or allowing the death of a child and perverting the course of justice by taking steps to conceal the killing of an infant.

A fifth person, a 15-year-old girl, who cannot be named for legal reasons, also appeared in the same court charged with perverting the course of justice.

All five defendants were remanded into custody to appear at Sheffield Crown Court on Thursday.

News.title: 'Nothing but mud and silt' - the village swept away by deadly floods in Nepal
News.content:
After the catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border a week ago, more than 1,000 people have died and nearly 4,000 more are missing, according to Nepal's disaster agency.

The BBC has travelled to the district of Betrawati in Nepal, as some people return to their homes to see the devastation caused by the floods.

South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri spoke to a local, who is still waiting for his his wife's body to be retrieved as rescue efforts continue.

More on this story.

News.title: Letby 'boyfriend' doctor named as court order lifted
News.content:
Letby - who has always maintained her innocence - is serving 15 whole life prison terms. The Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) is conducting a review of Letby's convictions.

At her criminal trial - the longest murder trial in UK history - Deakin gave evidence in relation to several babies. He was granted special measures as well as anonymity. These allowed him to give evidence from behind a screen so that Letby, the public gallery, and the media were prevented from seeing him.

Deakin's evidence provided detail of some of the emergency calls and resuscitations which he and Letby were jointly involved in. Their long nights of text messaging were laid bare and many of the messages shown to the jury.

When he was sworn in, on the first occasion he testified, Letby burst into tears, in what was the first display of emotion from her during the trial.

During her cross-examination, Letby was forced to deny that Deakin was her boyfriend, though she did accept that they had gone on a trip to London together.

The prosecuting barrister, Nick Johnson KC, said Letby "tried to get out the back of the dock" when the doctor first came to the witness box.

Letby said: "Yes, because I felt unwell."

Johnson said: "No, it's because you didn't like hearing your boyfriend giving evidence, did you?"

Letby said: "That's unfair."

Prosecutors also went through a WhatsApp message exchange between Letby and a friend who had teased her for being "flirty" with Deakin.

Johnson said: "She knew you were sweet on Mark, didn't she?"

Letby said: "What do you mean, sweet?"

Johnson said: "That you had a crush on him."

"No," said Letby.

"There was nothing between me and that Mark."

Johnson told the court that Letby told her friend she had received a "strange message" from the doctor.

Her colleague responded: "Did you? Saying what? Go Commando [laughing face emoji]."

While some media reports have described him as "a key witness", Deakin was one of many former colleagues of Letby's whose joint testimony helped to build the prosecution case against her, and none of the convictions rested solely on his evidence.

Correction: The original version of this story was published with an incorrect picture which has since been amended

News.title: London mayor's untaxed car conviction withdrawn
News.content:
The DVLA has said a criminal prosecution against mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan will be withdrawn after he was convicted of not taxing a 24-year-old Nissan Micra.

The Labour politician, 55, was found guilty of keeping an unlicensed vehicle by a magistrate last month in a criminal prosecution brought by the DVLA.

Court documents show letters addressed to the mayor about the unpaid tax bill were sent to Gordon Ramsay's east London restaurant and the car did not belong to the mayor.

A spokesperson for the mayor said: "This is a scam, which is a crime. It's not the first time the mayor has been victim of a scam involving people falsely stating that Sadiq is the owner of a vehicle."

The mayor's adviser told BBC London earlier that the DVLA was "urgently" looking into reopening the case and withdrawing the prosecution.

The DLVA said the withdrawal had been accepted but it needed to be formally reopened and withdrawn, which will be done at a hearing at Hereford Magistrates' Court on Thursday.

The DVLA will also investigate the false registration, the adviser said.

The magistrate, sitting in a private hearing of the Single Justice Procedure in Herefordshire, previously convicted Khan in his absence and ordered that he pay a Â£220 fine, Â£85 in costs, and settle the Â£35.84 bill for unpaid tax on the Micra.

After the mayor expanded the Ultra Low Emission Zone (Ulez) to cover the whole of London he faced a wave of protests, including from motorists who said they planned to register their car in his name - supposedly to make him liable for the Â£12.50 daily charge.

News.title: Four arrested over woman's murder 32 years ago
News.content:
Four people have been arrested on suspicion of perverting the course of justice in the case of a woman who was murdered 32 years ago.

Doreen Morris, 64, was stabbed to death with a fork after disturbing a burglary at her home, Penrhyn Uchaf, on Anglesey, in 1994, according to a 2023 inquest.

Joseph Carl Westbury denied breaking into Doreen's bungalow and was found not guilty of her murder in 1995. He took his life in May 2016.

North Wales Police said a man and three women, all from north Wales, were arrested on Wednesday morning.

The force said advances in forensic science and a review of evidence had led to the development and the Morris family had been told.

Mark Pierce, senior review officer, said: "Forensic results, combined with a detailed review of witness evidence, have provided grounds to interview four people on suspicion of perverting the course of justice."

He appealed for anyone with information about the case to get in touch.

News.title: About 700 prisoners to be freed on 1 October under revised early release plans
News.content:
About 700 eligible offenders will leave jails in England and Wales on the morning of 1 October and some 2,550 will have been released by the end of the year, the government's revised early prison release plan shows.

The new plan, signed into law and published online, shows Andy Burnham's government kept the promised original schedule of how and when offenders will leave jail, aside from delaying the start date by a month and excluding specific offences from the programme.

Under the original plan, offenders serving sentences of up to 19 months would have been eligible from 2 September to walk out of jail after serving a third of that time.

In the Commons on Wednesday, Burnham said he understood the "anguish" of victims and "listened to what they were saying".

"I came in and asked for changes to the early release scheme, and we excluded rape, grooming, and child sex offences," the prime minister added.

Prisoners will now qualify for their earlier release from 1 October and officials estimate that around 700 will walk out of the prison gates that day.

From 13 October, governors will release a second tranche of 650 prisoners who have been serving sentences of between 19 months and two years and five months.

Prisons in England and Wales are running at 97% capacity, with the latest Ministry of Justice figures showing the number of available spaces across the male prison estate at its lowest this year, with about 1,500 free spaces.

Under the original plan, prisons and probation services had almost six weeks to prepare this second group following the first releases, but they now have less than a fortnight.

The rest of the estimated 4,500 releases will then be phased in following the dates below. Some 1,400 more offenders were due to be released under the original plans before revisions made after certain offences were excluded.

The estimated numbers are Ministry of Justice calculations:

From 10 November, 650 offenders serving up to three years and two months

From 8 December, 550 offenders serving up to four years and three months

From 12 January 2027, 600 offenders serving up to five years and nine months

From 9 February, 500 offenders serving up to seven years and six months

From 9 March, 200 offenders serving up to nine years

From 13 April, 200 offenders serving up to 10 years

From 11 May, 250 offenders serving up to 12 years

From 9 June, 250 offenders serving more than 12 years.

The offenders serving the longer sentences, which do not become part of the scheme until next year, include more dangerous criminals who would have previously expected to spend two-thirds of their sentence behind bars.

News.title: Woman died of heatstroke climbing Yr Wyddfa, inquest hears
News.content:
A 35-year-old woman died of heatstroke on Wales' highest mountain, an inquest has heard.

Sophie Goodyer-Bird, from Birmingham, was climbing Yr Wyddfa - also known as Snowdon - on 10 July, a few days after her birthday.

On Wednesday, an inquest opening at Caernarfon Coroners' Court heard Goodyer-Bird became increasingly tired while coming down the mountain.

Near the end of the walk, she became unresponsive, and was confirmed to have died shortly afterwards.

Coroner Kate Robertson said emergency services were called and attempted CPR, but were unable to revive her.

A provisional cause of death was given as exertional heat stroke.

The inquest was adjourned to a full hearing, which will take place at a later date.

Following her death, an online fundraiser was set up to raise money for her 12-year-old son.

News.title: Man found guilty of killing his dad in pub garden
News.content:
A man who pushed over and killed his newly-discovered father in a pub garden on Christmas Eve has been found guilty of manslaughter.

Martin Greensmith, 37, only learnt Steven Shevels, 61, was his biological father shortly before their encounter behind The Queen's Head in Willington, County Durham, on 24 December, Teesside Crown Court heard.

Greensmith said he only "gently" pushed Shevels after the victim "intimidated" him, but prosecutors maintained he had caused his death during a fit of anger.

The defendant, who told jurors he was "very remorseful" and wanted to apologise to the victim's family, will be sentenced on 21 October.

Judge Jonathan Carroll remanded Greensmith into custody on the grounds of the "likely sentence" that would be imposed.

Jurors reached their verdict after almost six hours of deliberation, with 10 of the cohort of 12 finding him guilty.

Speaking after the verdict, Shevels' sister, Angela, said her brother was "the victim of an unprovoked act of violence that took his life far too soon".

His death had "left a hole in all our hearts" and a "future forever changed for all of his family, friends, and everyone who knew him", she added.

News.title: Nottingham attacks families not told 'stalker' had violent past
News.content:
Families of the Nottingham attacks victims said police did not tell them a man who had taken an interest in them had a history of violence when he attempted to visit them.

Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates were fatally stabbed by Valdo Calocane, who had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020, on 13 June 2023. He tried to kill three others.

Grace's father, Dr Sanjoy Kumar, said he was told in 2025 that a man had visited his GP surgery in London. Emma Webber, Barnaby's mother, said he had also travelled to Somerset, but neither were informed of the man's history of mental ill health.

Nottinghamshire Police said it had received a complaint and referred the matter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

The IOPC confirmed it had received a referral of a complaint from Nottinghamshire Police in relation to information the force allegedly withheld from the families of Calocane's victims about a potential witness who had tried to contact them.

News.title: Family of murdered Stacy Hunter say new misogyny bill would not have protected her
News.content:
The family of Stacy Hunter has called for immediate action to protect victims of domestic abuse, after plans for a misogyny bill were announced by the Scottish government.

First Minister John Swinney announced plans to recognise misogyny as a "distinct form of prejudice and abuse" during his programme for government, external on Tuesday, alongside a public health campaign to target toxic male behaviour.

Stacy was murdered by her estranged husband, Jim Mair, at her home near Houston in Refrewshire in July. He was on bail for attacking her. His body was found nearby.

Her family is calling for tougher action on offenders.

Speaking on BBC Radio Scotland's Mornings programme, Stacy's brother said some aspects of the proposals were important but they are not "anywhere near good enough".

Some hockey fans will find their favorite teams games exclusively streaming on Amazon Prime starting this season.

Amazon announced on Wednesday that Prime Video and the National Hockey League have reached a multi-year deal that gives Prime Video the exclusive local streaming rights for six NHL teams starting in the 2026-2027 hockey season.

The Carolina Hurricanes, Anaheim Ducks, Columbus Blue Jackets, Dallas Stars, Minnesota Wild, and St Louis Blues will have their games exclusively streamed on Prime Video for fans living in the teams' regional territories.

The streams will include the games plus pre- and post-game shows and other team programming, according to Amazon. Each of the participating teams will announce the specific details of their streaming packages and subscriptions for their respective territories.

"Fans want an easy way to find and follow their favorite teams, and this agreement with Prime Video gives Clubs the flexibility to meet that demand as the market evolves," NHL Chief Media Officer and Senior Executive Vice President David Proper said in a statement.

Amazon's Prime Video and the NHL announced that local games for six teams — the Carolina Hurricanes, Anaheim Ducks, Columbus Blue Jackets, Dallas Stars, Minnesota Wild and St. Louis Blues — will be exclusively streamed on the Prime Video platform ( Getty )

He told the Sports Business Journal that the NHL ultimately took a variety of deals to the participating teams and said they opted to go with Amazon's offer.

“We talked to a whole bunch of different people, and everybody had good proposals and a lot of good partners,” Proper said. “At the end of the day, we negotiated all of them as far as we could and then took them to the clubs, and the clubs opted for the Amazon opportunity.”

Prime Video already carries a number of local sports team coverage. The Seattle Kraken, MSG Networks, CHSN, NESN, Peacock NBC Sports Network RSN's in Boston, Philadelphia, and the Bay Area, SNY, YES Network, and Marquee Sports Network are already on the service, and more are reportedly going to be added in the future.

Amazon's sports offerings can be watched on all compatible devices, including on browsers and Prime Video apps across devices.

Fans who aren't in local markets can still watch games via NHL Center Ice.

In addition to the Kraken, Amazon now has the exclusive local streaming rights for seven NHL teams.

A new team of 45 officers will be deployed on French beaches in the coming weeks, specifically tasked with stopping “mega dinghy” launches along the coast.

The additional boots on the ground will bring the total number of French officers battling to stop small boat launches to nearly 1,050, the government has announced.

The move comes as French president Emmanuel Macron meets with prime minister Andy Burnham in London on Wednesday.

Small boat crossings to the UK have fallen by 23 per cent year-on-year, data up to the end of June 2026 shows, mirroring similar trends across Europe.

French police teams funded by the UK prevented 185 small boat crossings between 27 April and 2 August, the Home Office said this week.

open image in gallery A mega dinghy with a record 230 people abroad travelled to the UK last month ( SNSM )

The UK is paying France around £662m over the next three years to fund policing of the northern French beaches. Around £160m of this money has been earmarked for new tactics, such as policing to stop “taxi boats” picking up migrants offshore, and is conditional on the success of the French operation.

While the number of migrants arriving to the UK on small boats is going down, the number of people that smugglers are cramming onto the flimsy dinghies has been rising.

Last month, a record 230 migrants arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel in a single boat.

open image in gallery French President Emmanuel Macron is in the UK for talks with prime minister Andy Burnham ( Reuters )

The “mega dinghy” was seen “buckling” in the water and could have led to tragedy, according to French rescuers. The number breaks the previous record from July when 165 people successfully made the crossing.

In a move to clamp down on the super-sized boats, the team of 45 officers has been tasked with stopping the launches.

A specialist French intelligence and judicial unit will also be expanded from 18 to 30 officers, with the team focussing on disrupting the people-smuggling networks that organise the illegal trade.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK ‘cannot be complacent’ despite falling numbers of small boats crossing the Channel ( PA Wire )

Prime minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday: “The progress we have seen this summer shows what can be achieved when the UK and France works together.

“But I am clear that we cannot be complacent. Smuggling gangs are constantly adapting their tactics, and the UK and France need to respond quickly and stay one step ahead of the criminals facilitating the dangerous crossings.”

Home secretary Shabana Mahmood said the work was “bearing fruit”, adding: “We are boosting officer numbers to record highs to crack down on small boat launches and the gangs behind them.”

News.title: Accused Penn State drug ringleader who called himself ‘the Godfather’ granted bail
News.content:

Agostino Abbatiello, a former student from Pennsylvania State University who is accused of leading a cocaine trafficking ring out of two fraternities, has been granted bail.

A Pennsylvania judge set bail for Abbatiello, who called himself “the Godfather,” at $250,000 at a Wednesday hearing in nearby Bellefonte, despite prosecutors' claims that he threatened witnesses, according to local reports. Abbatiello’s lawyers called the allegation “outrageous,” WTAJ reported.

As part of the bail conditions, Abbatiello, a 24-year-old from Westbury, New York, can not have contact with witnesses and must live with his parents.

Philip Masorti, a lawyer for Abbatiello, said he was “happy with the way things went today,” per CBS News Pittsburgh. "My client's gonna be posting bail soon."

Abbatiello was one of 14 people, mostly college students, who were charged in connection with the drug ring bust. He, along with Thomas Robinson, Mohammed Hurabi and Lars Zeepvat, face the most serious charges, including felony corrupt organizations, conspiracy and dealing in proceeds of unlawful activity.

open image in gallery Agostino Abbatiello, a former student from Pennsylvania State University who is accused of leading a cocaine trafficking ring out of two fraternities, has been granted bail at $250,000 ( AP )

open image in gallery Abbatiello, a 24-year-old from Westbury, New York, can not have contact with witnesses and must live with his parents ( AP )

Abbatiello and Robinson, a 23-year-old from Churchill, Pennsylvania, were the main suppliers of the operation, which ran from 2023 to 2024, making regular trips to Philadelphia and New York for large amounts of cocaine, according to prosecutors.

The cocaine was then allegedly cut and packaged, mainly at the Delta Upsilon and Sigma Chi fraternity houses, and distributed to Penn State students. Abbatiello was a Sigma Chi brother and Robinson was a Delta Upsilon brother — both went to Penn State until 2024.

“According to the evidence uncovered, cutting and packaging cocaine was, for some pledges, an indoctrination into the fraternities,” Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday said when the charges were announced on August 17.

Zeepvat, a 24-year-old from Mendham, New Jersey, who allegedly sold cocaine for Abbatiello, testified Wednesday that Abbatiello, whom he said called himself “the Godfather,” sold the drugs “for money and popularity,” CBS News reported.

open image in gallery Abbatiello and Thomas Robinson, a 23-year-old from Churchill, Pennsylvania, were the main suppliers of the operation, which ran from 2023 to 2024, prosecutors say ( Pennsylvania Attorney General's Office )

Robinson testified Wednesday that he and Hurabi, a 22-year-old from Secaucus, New Jersey, started buying drugs from Abbatiello by August 2023, interactions that were set up through Snapchat, WTAJ reported. He and Haraibi then allegedly packaged and sold the drugs.

The drug buys would continue until at least November 2024, with the last purchase costing $22,000, according to Robinson.

Robinson said they only bought the drugs through Abbatiello and would mostly sell them to his fraternity brothers. He also testified that he got other fraternity brothers, such as Zeepfat, to help sell the drugs.

Paul Robinson, Robinson’s father and a prominent Pittsburgh attorney, was one of the 14 people charged in the case. He was charged with tampering with evidence and hindering the investigation.

The Independent has reached out to Masorti for comment

Elliot Page is waiting for Hollywood to give him a call.

The Oscar-nominated actor, 39, admitted in a new interview that he has yet to find his next role after playing Greek soldier Sinon in Christopher Nolan’s smash hit adaptation of Homer’s epic The Odyssey.

During his appearance Tuesday on the On Film... With Kevin McCarthy podcast, Page laughed in response to McCarthy’s suggestion that the performer would be flooded with calls and offers after joining stars like Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron and Tom Holland on the big screen.

“No, Kevin, I’m not,” he said. “So, if someone wants to call me.”

Page, who is transgender, went on to joke: “I know I get some pushback for being… Canadian. I don't know what it's about.”

open image in gallery Elliot Page says he has not received many offers since 'The Odyssey' ( Getty )

According to Page’s IMDb page, he has nothing officially in the works after finishing production as the voice of Dusky in forthcoming animated action film Naya Legend of the Golden Dolphin.

The Odyssey reunited the actor and director after Page starred as Ariadne in Nolan’s Leonardo DiCaprio-led science-fiction heist movie Inception in 2010, ten years before transitioning in 2020.

Speaking about working with Nolan again, Page recalled that he had been “uncomfortable” while filming Inception because it had been before his transition.

“I don't know if this is weird or too personal, but when you do ask me about [Inception], I had such a great time being in that movie,” he said on the podcast. “I had such a great time working with [Nolan], but I was also personally really uncomfortable.”

However, he said about filming 2007 romance Juno, “I was able to feel more comfortable and embodied or something like that.”

open image in gallery Elliot Page played Greek soldier Sinon in Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ ( Universal Pictures )

Page continued: “But I feel now, because that's removed, and I don't have to deal with that when I'm acting in my performances, I am like… I feel like I could maybe do some of my best work now.”

He went on to say that it felt like a “full circle moment” filming The Odyssey with Nolan because he now feels comfortable in his own skin, which led to him breaking into tears after wrapping the movie.

“I think that just feeling more embodied and connected, that's what weirdly lets you let go more, you know?” he said. “Knowing yourself more and embodying yourself more, weirdly, lets you let go more.”

The Odyssey passed Nolan’s previous record and became the filmmaker’s highest-grossing film with more than $1.5 billion globally.

Joey Logano has won 71 NASCAR races and three Cup Series championships during his illustrious career.

But the driver of the No. 22 Penske Racing Ford said nothing would make him appear cooler in the eyes of his five children than securing a cameo in the upcoming sequel to “Days of Thunder,” which will star Tom Cruise and Anne Hathaway and is set for release in 2028.

“Yeah, are you kidding me — that's like wicked cool dad points to be in ‘Days of Thunder,’” Logano said Wednesday at the NASCAR playoff media day.

Logano isn't the only driver pushing for a role in the follow-up to the 1990 movie starring Cruise as fictional NASCAR driver Cole Trickle.

Chase Briscoe wants in, too.

“Absolutely, I would love to be,” Briscoe said. “I would think they are going to use some of the drivers. Maybe our car will just be in it, but I would love to be in there.”

Kyle Larson thinks it would be cool to be around while the movie is in production, but joked, “I’m not an actor, so I don’t want to make the film worse.”

Filming is scheduled to begin early next year.

Logano said he has watched “Days of Thunder” numerous times, often alongside his children, who love the movie.

NASCAR drivers Richard Petty, Rusty Wallace, Neil Bonnett and Harry Gant all appeared in “Days of Thunder,” so Logano is hopeful he might be able to pull some strings and get a small part in the sequel.

“Hopefully that happens,” Logano said with a laugh. “I wouldn’t say no, that's for sure. Absolutely I'd do it.”

Cruise surprised drivers last weekend when he showed up for the Cup Series race at Daytona International Speedway, emerging from a black Chevy Suburban and attending the drivers' council meeting.

He and some of the screenwriters spoke to drivers and team owners to get a feel for their routines and how the sport has changed since the original movie's debut 36 years ago.

“It was really neat,” Briscoe said. “All of a sudden, Tom Cruise walked in and none of us knew that was happening. And he’s just sitting there and talked with us for like 20, 25 minutes about his goal of what to do with the movie and how he wants to paint us out to be.”

Briscoe described Cruise as “super nice.”

Charlotte-based Hendrick Motorsports had an instrumental role in the first movie, helping build, prepare and repair the stock cars used during the production. Trickle’s primary car included a sponsorship from City Chevrolet, a real-life car dealership owned by Rick Hendrick.

It's unclear at this point if Hendrick Motorsports will be involved again, but Larson is hoping it works out.

There is a good chance it will.

Four-time Cup Series champion Jeff Gordon, now vice chairman at Hendrick Motorsports, openly lobbied for Cruise to make a “Days of Thunder” sequel. Over the years, Gordon and Cruise have developed a friendship, with Cruise showing up at a 2015 NASCAR banquet to honor the retiring Gordon.

Larson said meeting Cruise was cool, and he can't wait to learn about the moviemaking process.

“He’s a celebrity like I’ve never met before in my life,” Larson said. “You could tell he was different from the rest of us, in a cool way, like really, really cool. He kind of already knows a little bit about us, so I thought that was neat.”

___

AP Sports Writer Mark Long in Jacksonville, Florida, contributed to this report.

Republican Senator Thom Tillis called on President Donald Trump to fire Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over his “inept management” of the military.

The North Carolina lawmaker, who previously served on the Senate Armed Services Committee, lambasted Hegseth Wednesday following the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, who had reportedly clashed with Hegseth over the ouster of top military leaders.

Tillis commended Driscoll for being the “right man at the right moment to lead our Soldiers and Army civilians,” before launching into a tirade against Hegseth.

“I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country. He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense and the health and well-being of our fighting force,” Tillis wrote on X.

Tillis, who in January last year cast a key vote to confirm Hegseth’s appointment in a 51-50 vote, added, “I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it.”

open image in gallery Senator Thom Tillis called on President Donald Trump to fire Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth following the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll earlier this week ( Getty )

He also accused Hegseth, a former Fox News presenter, of “creating a leadership void at the top of our military ranks” by pushing people like Driscoll out of their roles.

Other senior military officials who have vacated their jobs under Hegseth’s leadership include former Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Charles Q Brown Jr.; Adm. Lisa Franchetti, the first female member of the Joint Chiefs; U.S. National Security Agency Director Tim Haugh; Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin; Lt. Gen. Jeffrey Kruse, who led the Defense Intelligence Agency; Navy Secretary John Phelan; Gen. Christopher Donahue and the top U.S. Army commander in Europe and former Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George.

Tillis, who has become a frequent critic of Trump before he is set to retire at the end of his current term, has previously been outspoken against Hegseth, telling CNN in May that his mistakes regarding the war in Iran “make Kristi Noem look like a five-star recruit.”

open image in gallery Tillis, pictured center with Trump and Hegseth at a dignified transfer for four U.S. military personnel in June, has become a frequent critic of the president and his team ( Getty )

However, with Driscoll’s resignation Monday, reports emerged of tensions hitting a boiling point between the Army Secretary and Hegseth.

No official reason was provided for Driscoll’s departure, which comes after CNN and Reuters reported he had been getting into arguments with Hegseth for several months.

Sources told The Atlantic this week that Driscoll had “brought up concerns with the administration surrounding Army transformation and readiness and Hegseth’s blocking those efforts specifically by firing the generals who were responsible,” but wasn’t successful in addressing those concerns.

open image in gallery Former Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll is the latest Army official to announce their departure amid efforts by Hegseth to reshape the Defense Department ( Getty )

Trump was also left “surprised and concerned” over the number of cuts to the Army, as well as the seniority of those who have resigned from their roles, according to The Atlantic report.

The Army now has fewer generals than any point in recent history, according to the report.

Driscoll, an Iraq War veteran and former advisor to Vice President JD Vance, whom he befriended at Yale Law School, was lauded as being “highly effective,” by the White House following his resignation.

open image in gallery A handful of high-ranking military leaders have been fired or have quit under Hegseth’s leadership ( AFP/Getty )

“Secretary Driscoll has been highly effective in advancing President Trump’s agenda to Make America Strong Again at the Department of the Army by providing outstanding leadership during historic military operations, restoring an emphasis on readiness and lethality, assisting with negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, and more,” White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said in a statement.

“The United States Army is more powerful than ever thanks to his work alongside the commander-in-chief and secretary of war.”

The Independent has asked the Defense Department for comment.

The Metropolitan Police are investigating allegations Chinese embassy guards brandished illegal electroshock batons at protesters.

The government has also been urged to take action after the alleged incident.

Videos appeared to show security staff at both the current Chinese embassy in Portland Place and the proposed new embassy at Royal Mint Court, near the Tower of London, wielding the weapons in two separate incidents in recent months, the i Paper have reported.

Electroshock weapons are banned in the UK.

The Met said officers are reviewing evidence, “including video footage supplied by witnesses”.

Downing Street officials said the matter has been raised with the embassy directly and warned that foreign diplomats must abide by British laws.

The Chinese embassy described the claims about its security staff at Portland Place as “nothing but fabrication and defamation” by “Tibetan independence elements” who “attempted to force their way into the embassy premises”.

The Prime Minister’s official spokesperson said he would not “get ahead” of the police investigation but added: “If there’s evidence a crime has been committed, we won’t hesitate to act.

“Any attempts by a foreign state to coerce, intimidate, harass or harm individuals on UK soil will never be tolerated.

open image in gallery Videos appeared to show security staff wielding the weapons in two separate incidents in recent months ( PA )

“We expect all foreign diplomats in the UK to abide by our laws, in the same way we expect all UK diplomats to do so when posted overseas, and we’ve raised this incident directly with the Chinese embassy.”

Shadow national security minister Alicia Kearns urged the government to take more action, describing the police investigation as a “dead end” that was unlikely to result in prosecution because of international protections for embassy premises.

She said: “Nine weeks after the incident, with evidence of prohibited electroshock weapons on more than one Chinese site, the Government has done nothing but ‘raise’ the incident with the embassy.

“The Chinese Communist Party has broken British law, and potentially the Vienna Convention, and yet rather than respond to the threatening of peaceful vigil holders with illegal weapons, ministers are hiding behind a dead-end Met investigation they know won’t end with prosecutions.

“If the Government won’t act when laws are broken, and people are threatened on British soil, it is inviting the Chinese Communist Party to test them again.

“The Government needs to deter future threats, but that requires them to act, now.”

A Met Police spokesperson said: “On Friday 3 July at around 1800hrs, police were called to reports of a protest outside the Chinese Embassy on Portland Place, W1B.

“Officers attended the scene. Two protesters alleged that embassy staff had pointed a Taser towards them. No injuries were reported and officers left the area once the protesters had dispersed on their own accord.

“No arrests have been made at this stage. The investigation continues as officers review evidence, including video footage supplied by witnesses.”

The Met urged anyone with information to call police on 101, quoting CAD7335/03JUL26.
