Dollywood has shared how it plans to honor "dreamer-in-chief” Dolly Parton after her death at the age of 80.

Raised in rural Sevier County, Dolly Parton helped transform the theme park into the area's top employer and a major tourist destination.

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, park officials announced plans to introduce a new character named the Dream Maker, inspired by Parton's Imagination Library. A chapel located inside the park will also feature a new waterfall and stained glass windows reflecting her deep faith.

Visitors will be able to leave messages about Parton at designated kiosks, while further additions are coming to The Dolly Parton Experience, a multibuilding space containing exhibits dedicated to her life and career.

open image in gallery Fans will have new ways to show their love for the iconic singer and songwriter ( AP Photo/Camden Hall )

Situated in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains in east Tennessee, Sevierville is also installing markers throughout the city to establish a self-guided walking tour of locations that held significance for the singer, actor and philanthropist.

Dolly Parton’s family announced her death in an emotional Instagram video on August 25. Her representatives later confirmed that she died following a “brief battle with cancer.”

She was laid to rest at a private funeral, in line with her wishes. Dolly had made it clear before she died that she wanted a “small, private service” for immediate family, the singer’s team said.

Her service was held at Woodlawn Memorial Park and Mausoleum in Nashville, where she was buried next to Carl Dean, her husband of 60 years who died in March 2025.

“I wanted to wait until after my granny was laid to rest yesterday before I tried to put any of this into words,” Dolly’s niece, Lainey Parton, wrote in a touching tribute after the service.

“From the time I was little, my granny always had a way of making me feel like I was enough. She never made my dreams feel too big or made me feel like I couldn’t do something. She believed in me before I even knew how to believe in myself.”

News.title: Burnham risks Truss moment, warn bond traders
News.content:
Andy Burnham risks a Liz Truss-style market meltdown unless he presents a credible plan to pay for his agenda, bond traders have warned.

Investors said the Prime Minister faces further spikes in borrowing costs unless he outlines tax rises or spending cuts to fund his major policies.

UK borrowing costs have surged to multi-decade highs this week amid a global bond market sell-off. However, investors are particularly concerned about Mr Burnham’s fiscal agenda before his first Budget next month.

Al Cattermole, a portfolio manager at Swiss private bank Mirabaud, said investors were “unclear” about the Prime Minister’s plans and how he would pay for them.

He said: “If you have a lack of credibility about your spending plan and how that will be funded, then you would get spikes in yields similar to [what] we saw during the Liz Truss episode.

“That was about unfunded fiscal spending. And if you get that again, then there is concern about that.”

Mr Burnham refused to rule out increasing borrowing during his first Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday despite recent market turmoil.

Jim Athey, a portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment, said: “Spending cuts are the thing the market wants to hear.

“It would go a long way if this Government were to recognise that it is a challenge that needs addressing – that the path we are on in terms of welfare spending is completely unsustainable.”

He added: “The market knows that, and the market wants to hear that the Government understands that.”

Lord Jim O’Neill said earlier that the Prime Minister must “get real” and cut public spending in order to ease pressure in the bond market.

The cost of long-term government borrowing hit its highest level since 1998 on Wednesday, increasing the strain on the public finances as John Healey, the new Chancellor, prepares for the Budget.

The 10-year gilt yield – a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money – has risen to its highest point since 2007.

News.title: H5N1 hits US mink farms, sparking calls for an urgent cull
News.content:
H5N1 has been detected on a US mink farm for the first time, igniting fears the infected animals could present a human pandemic risk.

The bird flu virus, which has “jumped” from birds to numerous mammal species and infected hundreds of people in recent years, was detected in at least six mink on a farm in Utah in mid-August, according to a notification from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) released over the weekend.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms gives invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate. Mink also have strikingly similar respiratory systems to humans, which greatly increases the human risk.

The animals are farmed for their fur, which is then typically exported to fashion manufacturers in China, Hong Kong, and Russia and used in items like coats and scarves.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 acquires the ability to spread efficiently between people, it could trigger a human pandemic.

“Avian influenza viruses tend to replicate pretty poorly in humans and don’t really have the right sort of properties that allow them to transmit from person to person.

“If H5N1 were to cause a pandemic, it would need to make quite a lot of changes, and there’s a real concern that mink, particularly farmed mink, have a lot of the features that could drive the evolution of H5N1,” Dr Tom Peacock, a virologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

News.title: Collapsing child vaccination in South Africa ‘a public health emergency’
News.content:
Plummeting child immunisation rates are now a public health emergency in South Africa and risk causing outbreaks of preventable but potentially deadly childhood diseases, the government has said.

The proportion of children under one who have received no vaccinations has trebled in the past decade to nearly a third of infants in South Africa.

Mistrust of vaccines and growing ignorance about the benefits of childhood immunisations risk undoing years of progress made by one of the continent’s most effective health systems.

Outbreaks of measles, diphtheria and whooping cough this year have all been linked to poor immunisation rates and are evidence that herd immunity is breaking down, officials warned.

An alert from the department for health said the proportion of unvaccinated infants had hit 36.3 per cent in the first four months of 2026, up from 12.1 per cent in 2017.

The department warned the jump was “effectively tripling the number of completely unvaccinated children and leaving hundreds of thousands of infants at risk of life-threatening illnesses”.

Coverage of the six-in-one hexavalent infant vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, meningitis, and hepatitis B declined from 87 per cent to 60.5 per cent over the same period.

Officials said the shortfall was caused by a lack of people coming forward to bring their children for jabs and was not due to any shortage of vaccines.

Dr Nonhlanhla Ndlovu, deputy director general of South Africa’s health department, told the state broadcaster that parents had a poor understanding of the public health benefits of childhood jabs.

She said: “The second one that comes out is the issue of public trust, in terms of the safety of the vaccines, but also the trust in terms of our systems.”

“Theses vaccines are very safe and we have seen the gains that we have had in our years before and now that is changing.

“The benefit of vaccines far outweigh anything we can talk about in public health. We need them to come back and bring the children for immunisation.”

News.title: Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer
News.content:
It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

Julian Alvarez to Barcelona… or Arsenal

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Lamine Camara to Chelsea

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

Ismaila Sarr to Liverpool

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Sports.title: Chelsea and Tottenham leave Arsenal and Man Utd in their wake as winners and losers of summer transfer window revealed
Sports.content:
IT was the maddest, biggest, most astonishing summer transfer window of all time.

Record-breaking sums and huge squad overhauls, with the drama extending to two hours after the deadline as Everton’s big striker signing changed his mind after the last minute.



As the dust settles, the debates on who were the Prem winners and losers will intensify.

SunSport sifts through the chaos to identify those with something to smile about. And those left with scowls.



WINNERS

Chelsea:

Even by Stamford Bridge standards, this has been a stunning summer of shifting sands.

But while midfield depth may be an issue – given the injury records of Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and Reece James and the collapse of the deal for Monaco’s Lamine Camara – new boss Xabi Alonso seems to have all his other ducks in a row.

Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival has already paid off alongside Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer, Maxence Lacroix is utterly at home at centre-halves, while Blues fans like the look of full-backs Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria.

Even the signing Chelsea did not want to make, before Robert Sanchez’ failings made the move for Emi Martinez a no-brainer, has boosted the squad.

Hull:

The Tigers had two options after their unexpected promotion.

They could have taken the easy way out, spent a few bob, accepted their fate, used the guaranteed £220m over the next three years to give them a platform to come back stronger.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Instead, it’s a copy of the playbook that saw Sunderland exceed all expectations last summer – and then some.

In total, 18 new players and the third-highest net spend in the Prem. They even let the bloke who scored their winner at Coventry on Saturday go out on loan on deadline day. Full marks for ambition.

Liverpool:

Bradley Barcola’s £123m arrival was the landmark deal of the Anfield summer – but Andoni Iraola putting his foot down to keep Cody Gakpo might be equally important.

Spaniard Victor Munoz has already made a good impression, winning the penalty that earned a point at Newcastle on the opening weekend before scoring the leveller against Forest on Saturday.

Young Frenchman Jeremy Jacquet could be the partner to keep Virgil van Dijk fresh for the fight at the back, while there are doubts about both full-backs.



Yet if Alexander Isak can profit from the men on either flank, Liverpool could be back in the title mix.

Manchester City:

Life after Pep was always going to be different, yet few could have imagined quite how different.

Overhauling the entire midfield – at a cost of just £327m – was a signal of City’s laser focus on giving Enzo Maresca the chance to get off to a trophy-winning start.

But while City have lost the experience of Rodri, they look to have plenty of goals in them – as long as Erling Haaland stays fit.



Enzo Fernandez will add midfield goals, Iliman Ndiaye something different to the mix, while Rayan Cherki already looks in the mood to make this a launchpad season.

Tottenham:

Well, they should be, anyway, after an unprecedented summer splurge in North London.

This is “Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham”, in every sense, all 10 new recruits bearing the manager’s mark.

Now the onus is on the Italian manager to turn the ingredients he put in the pot into something tasty – although there has been a distinct lack of seasoning so far.

Spurs fans have reason to be demanding and that will put pressure on Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Omar Marmoush in particular.



De Zerbi must make sure they aren’t “N17th” again.

LOSERS

Arsenal:

The expectation was that the champions would improve from a position of strength.

Instead, while Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes add to the previous strong points of Mikel Arteta’s side, his forward options look weaker.

For all the efforts to land Vinicius Jr, Arsenal look like they were played by the Brazilian and his representatives, leaving Greek winger Christos Solis as the only attacking reinforcement.

Meanwhile, Arsenal allowed Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Reiss Nelson to leave, with Gabriel Martinelli Saudi-bound as well.



Fans are asking big questions of sporting director Andrea Berta. It is hard to argue Arteta has a better squad than he ended last term with.

Aston Villa:

It might look very different in May but for now Unai Emery appears to have been asked to undertake a massive job in building almost an entirely new side from scratch.

Losing six of the 11 players who started the Europa League final feels like a seismic change, even if Emery loves a challenge.

Villa have been slow starters in the past, only to pick up the pace quickly and end up as a potent force in both the Prem and Europe.

This time, though, they need all the new recruits to get up to speed quickly, in the most competitive league in the world.

You’ve got to feel sorry for Pierre Sage, whose spirits are unlikely to be lifted by parsley, rosemary or thyme.

The new Palace boss inherited a side that had lost two of its three star assets last term, with Eberechi Eze leaving for Arsenal and Marc Guehi at Manchester City.

While he did keep Adam Wharton – surely a January target for someone – Sage saw wing-back Daniel Munoz join predecessor Oliver Glasner at Forest and Lacroix’s switch to Chelsea, while Jean-Philippe Mateta unsuccessfully asked Fifa to rip up his contract and Ismaila Sarr is in a right old huff.

Even the Holmesdale Massive are hacked off. Nobody looks to be “glad all over” at Selhurst.



Everton:

The joke was biting, but fair.

Everton – the only team with more stadiums than strikers. And left-backs. And right-backs.

Over the space of three days, the Toffees moved for Richarlison, Joshua Zirkzee, and Folarin Balogun but were rejected by all of them.

And while few Evertonians will mourn the departure of Beto, selling Iliman Ndiaye to take a punt on Jack Grealish’s second loan spell is hardly a bet you’d put more than a fiver on.

Fans are in uproar – even after making the club backtrack over the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong – and the mood is beyond dark.



You wonder how much longer David Moyes will put up with being ordered to fight with both hands tied behind his back?

Manchester United:

Yes, a new-look midfield – although Carlos Baleba is still injured and Andrey Santos was dropped after one game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But other than that, United are pretty much exactly the same as they were, which has left Old Trafford fans wondering what the club is playing at.

Deadline day efforts to find a back-up – or replacement – for Luke Shaw were too little and too late, Diogo Dalot is hardly the ideal choice on the right, while they looked vulnerable to pace through the middle even while beating Ipswich on Sunday.

Sports.title: Tottenham misfit Richarlison lined up for sensational Mo Salah strike partnership as Trabzonspor target late transfer
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM striker Richarlison has emerged as a shock target for Turkish side Trabzonspor.

The Brazilian has been left in limbo after turning down the chance to join Everton before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.

Richarlison hinted he wanted to stay at Spurs via a bombshell statement that said “no one will ever again decide my future”.



But Tottenham are now braced for a formal approach from Trabzonspor, who want to sign a striker this week.



The Turkish transfer window does not close until on Friday and West Ham striker Pablo is another player on their radar.

Richarlison is thought to be open to the idea of moving to Trabzonspor, but agreeing a fee with Spurs may prove tricky.

Tottenham were set to bank £35million by selling the Brazil forward to Everton before the deal collapsed.



Trabzonspor would be able to offer hefty wages, as shown by the contract that Salah penned with them.

The Egyptian signed a two-year deal in August that is worth £363,000 a week – AFTER TAX.

Club president Ertugrul Dogan was behind Trabzonspor’s push to sign Salah and is expected to play a leading role in the pitch to Richarlison.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

If Richarlison were to depart, he’d join Luka Vuskovic, Cristian Romero and Djed Spence among the big name departures.



Should he remain, he has a fight on his hands to find a role in the team with Spurs signing Savio, Omar Marmoush and Mykhalo Mudryk in attacking positions.

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer window ranked as Xabi Alonso strikes gold with Morgan Rogers but could be left short in key area
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans were one decision away from a seemingly perfect transfer window.

And that decision was not one of their own but one made by AS Monaco, after pulling out of a deal for midfielder Lamine Camara at the final hour, who was supposed to replace Enzo Fernandez.



Still, the Blues’ first window with Xabi Alonso at the helm is something to be marveled at in terms of incomings, but especially in terms of outgoings.

The signing of Morgan Rogers looks to have given them one of the most dangerous forward lines in the Premier League, with Maxence Lacroix enforcing their defence, and Emiliano Martinez replacing the inconsistent Robert Sanchez in goal.



Those three were joined by the incomings of Marco Palestra, Danny Welbeck, Jordan Henderson, Pep Chavarria, Valentin Barco, Honest Anahor, Geovany Quenda, and Dastan Satpayev.

If they had have replaced the outgoing Fernandez with Camara they would total 12 new players who all bring vastly different qualities.

MORGAN ROGERS – 9

£117m from Aston Villa

Rogers’ signing from Aston Villa has started very brightly, and got everyone talking about Chelsea‘s ‘JP Morgan’ or ‘CPR’ front three.

He has a great relationship with Cole Palmer, who also seems to be back on track and boosted by Rogers’ signing, and has scored and assisted in the Prem already.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

It’s a hefty fee, which makes him the most expensive English player of all time, but so far he looks to be proving his worth.

So far, signing him looks a very smart move from The Blues, and one that could even propel them to the title if things work out.



EMILIANO MARTINEZ – 8

£7.5m from Aston Villa

For such a cheap fee, it’s hard to argue that this will be a bad signing for Chelsea.

Robert Sanchez was incredibly error prone, and Martinez is a proven top-level goalkeeper who has won numerous trophies and individual awards, as well as being a leader and adding experience to the side.

However, he is just as, if not more mistake-prone than Sanchez – and it will be a waiting game to see how much that impacts Chelsea and the value of his signing.

MAXENCE LACROIX – 8

£52m from Crystal Palace

Perhaps a little pricey, but undoubtedly what Chelsea needed at the back.



A Premier League proven defender who is comfortable in a back three system, with recovery pace to burn and of a good age profile for what this Chelsea team need.

The Frenchman has been exceptional so far, and especially strong against Fulham where he bagged an assist.

Admittedly, the Blues defence still looks particularly shaky even with him in it, but the missing Moises Caicedo won’t be helping that one bit.

MARCO PALESTRA – 7

£43m from Bologna

The Italian wingback has already been dubbed the ‘next Marcos Alonso‘ at Stamford Bridge.



Problem with that being, he was great going forward, but had obvious shortcomings in defence – something Palestra seems to share with him,

For £43m, the upside to his signing certainly outweights the potential downside, and he looks a promising signing from pre-season despite picking up an injury that has seen him miss the opening two matches of the Premier League.

DANNY WELBECK – 7

£5m from Brighton

What Welbeck brings to this team is obvious, experience and goals.

He will be a good, much-needed leader for Alonso, and has already bagged his first goal in blue in the Carabao Cup.



JORDAN HENDERSON – 7

Free from Brentford

The midfielder is yet to really do anything since joining Chelsea, given his overhanging injury from the World Cup.

That said, he has been taking up something of a coaching role under Alonso and will have a good impact on the dressing room.

Having signed on a free it’s hard to give him a bad mark, and he might even get some minutes in the absence of Fernandez.

VALENTIN BARCO – 8

£33.6m from Strasbourg

Wasn’t given much of a chance by fans when he first signed, but actually already looks a very astute signing.

He’s versatile, and can play as a full-back or a midfielder, shining in the Carabao Cup arguably more than any other player – dubbed a mix of Kevin De Bruyne and N’Golo Kante.



If he turns out to be anywhere near as good as either of those, he will be a success.

PEP CHAVARRIA – 7

£16.3m from Rayo Vallecano

Compared mostly to Cesar Azpilicueta, Chavarria has been solid when he has played for Chelsea so far.

He seems like largely a backup option on the left to the likes of Jorrel Hato and Marco Palestra, but a solid one nonetheless when he has played, and again is the right age profile for what Chelsea needed in this window.

GEOVANY QUENDA – 7

£44m from Sporting

A very, very exciting winger who can also play wingback under Xabi Alonso.



He is versatile and looks fresh in the same way Estevao did when he was breaking onto the scene at Stamford Bridge last season.

When he has played he looks direct and willing to take on his man, and you would imagine he is someone that if Chelsea do ever need to offload that they will profit on.

DASTAN SATPAYEV – 8

£3.5m from Kairat Almaty

Is spending the season on loan at Burnley, but it’s hard to imagine the Blues’ ‘baby Aguero’ not at least turning them a profit in the future.

He has also looked promising when he has actually played under Alonso, scoring a goal in pre-season.



HONEST ANAHOR – ?

£40m from Atalanta

Is supposedly the next best defender to come out of Serie A, and will spend this season at Crystal Palace before joining Chelsea in 2027.

£40m is a lot of money for a centre-back who will need to impress at Palace this season.

OVERALL RATING: 8/10

Xabi Alonso has been given the ‘manager’ title at Stamford Bridge, and it shows.

He has addressed almost every problem area in the squad, apart from the central midfield position where the late departure of Enzo Fernandez has left a hole.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A new goalkeeper in Emi Martinez and the additions of Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers address issues from qualitative depth to a lack of experience from last season, and seem to suit Alonso’s system nicely.

Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson should provide experience and squad depth, while Chelsea have also sold brilliantly and still brought promising youth in the form of Anahor, Quenda and Satpayev, who will likely make them a profit or become superstars themselves.

Sports.title: Why Man Utd struggle to sell players – one legend departed for ‘peanuts’ and serial winners have left for cut-price fees
Sports.content:
THIRTY-ONE years ago, Manchester United sold three first-teamers and did not make a single signing.

If social media existed in the summer of 1995, the internet might have crashed. Paul Ince, Andrei Kanchelskis and Mark Hughes, integral to Alex Ferguson’s first great side, each had a unique bond with the fanbase.



United banked £14million for the trio, an enormous sum three years after the Premier League’s inception. They have not had many summers like it since.

Ideally, United would have jettisoned a midfielder, a winger and a forward this summer, too. Manuel Ugarte, Marcus Rashford and Joshua Zirkzee were unshiftable.



For a club that received a world record fee for Cristiano Ronaldo in 2009, United are historically bad sellers.

They gave David Beckham away for “peanuts” to Real Madrid at the height of the Galactico era. Anthony Martial, Paul Pogba and Jadon Sancho signed for deals worth a combined £219.9m within a six-year period and were released.

There is no short answer to why United are bad at selling. You could write a hefty tome or record a podcast series on their poor record and why they struggle to fetch fees for senior players.

It was not even 18 months ago that United suffered their worst season in 51 years. So their current squad is not teeming with sellable assets and hardly anyone is capable of raking in a profit.

Altay Bayindir, loaned to Celta Vigo, is renowned for letting in goals. Joshua Zirkzee, the subject of a desperate loan enquiry from Everton on Tuesday evening, is renowned for not scoring goals.

Of all Everton’s window missteps, selling Beto and moving for Zirkzee should spark sackings. Beto scored five times as many goals as Zirkzee last season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The extravagant salaries United have put players on made them no-goes. Marcus Rashford is only still at the club as no elite European side was prepared to foot his wage bill of £325,000-a-week.

Casemiro saw out his contract as he was immovable. United are bound to encounter the same issue with Mason Mount, into the final two years of his deal and on £250,000 a week.

Jaap Stam, Cristiano Ronaldo, Daley Blind, Chris Smalling and Daniel James would be an obscure five-a-side team. They are also the only players United bought and sold at an eight-figure profit.

Ronaldo, James, Beckham, Angel di Maria, Romelu Lukaku, Scott McTominay, Mason Greenwood, Alejandro Garnacho and Rasmus Hojlund are the only United players to leave for £25m or more.

Of those nine players, four came through the club’s academy. That was the only source of United’s transfer income negotiated this summer, via Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek.



Garnacho, valued north of £85m in 2024, left for £40m in 2025. The most senior sale in the window that just closed was Collyer, starter of three games against Barnsley, Rangers and Steaua Bucharest. The last of those was in January 2025.

United trumpeted the overall £7.6m fee West Brom agreed to pay, with £3m up front. A source said it is “unlikely” the add-ons will be triggered.

The academy sells as United have produced talented professionals for the best part of a century. Andreas Pereira (£10m), James Garner (£15m), Dean Henderson (£20m), Anthony Elanga (£15m) and Garnacho all moved to Premier League clubs before Collyer and Vitek dropped down to the Championship.



In the summer of 2022, United’s only sales were Pereira and Garner. They had been out on loan, so were not damaged by the cataclysmic season with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and then Ralf Rangnick in the dugout.

Although Ferguson rarely drove a hard bargain, he did not struggle for willing takers. In 2007, Ferguson’s friend Sam Allardyce, had just been installed at Newcastle, who signed Alan Smith for £6m

Roy Keane could barely stomach sharing the same oxygen as Ferguson after United sacked him but still signed five players from his former club during his two-and-a-half years as Sunderland manager.

Steve Bruce, also at Sunderland, gave Wes Brown and John O’Shea a new home in 2011. David Moyes was a sucker for a United reject at Everton.

There were no domestic or Uefa financial rules to comply with back then, either. That was largely the case when Ed Woodward regularly misread a player’s market value.



The die was cast in the summer of 2014. New manager Louis van Gaal was decisive in identifying which players’ faces did not fit, so Woodward sanctioned several sales with little or no negotiating.

Shinji Kagawa left for roughly half the price United paid for him in 2012. Michael Keane and Wilfried Zaha were both flogged for £3m with no sell-on clauses inserted. £16m for Danny Welbeck was, in hindsight, low.

The squad purge continued in Van Gaal’s second summer: £4.25m for Nani, £6m for Jonny Evans and £7.3m for Javier Hernandez. Serial winners sold at a cut price amid mismanagement.



So a precedent was set: United sold on the cheap. Keane moved from Burnley to Everton for £30m in 2017. West Ham bought Hernandez in the same summer for more than double the £7.3m Bayer Leverkusen paid United. Evans was wanted by Manchester City at one stage.

Morgan Schneiderlin (£24m) and Memphis Depay (£21m) left for impressive fees in January 2017. The difference then was United were a resurgent force under Jose Mourinho and the players were cut loose after 18 months, so had suffered little reputational damage.

United banked good fees for Blind (£18.5m) and Sam Johnstone (£10m) in July 2018. Their reputations were enhanced by association with Mourinho and, in Johnstone’s case, emerging from the United academy.

But United regressed in the seller’s market after finishing sixth in 2018-19. Ander Herrera ran down his contract and Lukaku was sold at a minor loss to Inter Milan.



United had a decent 2024 as the majority of their outgoings were academy talents as part of Ineos’s attempts to use it as a cash cow.

There was an obvious market for Aaron Wan-Bissaka, a right back with six-and-a-half years of Premier League experience.

Coming 15th and trophyless in 2025 demanded outgoings. Ruben Amorim’s ‘bomb squad’ made certain players’ positions untenable, though United sold Antony at a considerable loss and failed to obtain a higher fee for Garnacho.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There was never going to be a fire sale this summer and Michael Carrick’s nature meant anyone ‘for sale’ had a squad role if they stayed.



Ugarte is no Ince and Zirkzee is no Hughes. Rashford has trumped Kanchelskis, though.

Sports.title: Inside Enzo Fernandez’s love life, from brief split with childhood sweetheart to Wanda Nara slipping into his DM’s
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ has joined Man City in a joint British record transfer.

The Argentine midfielder, 25, swapped Stamford Bridge for the Etihad on transfer deadline day for £125million.



The move will see Enzo uprooting his family, from London to Manchester, as he settles in to his new club.

Away from the pitch, the World Cup winner is in a longterm relationship with stunning influencer, Valentina Cervantes.



The high school sweethearts share two children, Olivia and Benjamin.

However, there was trouble in paradise when Enzo and Valentina briefly split in late 2024.



They reconciled in 2025, but then he found himself in an alleged love triangle with Wanda Nara.

And Valentina was also said to be charmed by an unnamed Argentina international.

Enzo’s love life has certainly been complicated in the last few years.

Young love

Valentina and Enzo met in 2018 and soon became love struck teenagers in Buenos Aires.



She said: “I met Enzo when he was 16, and at 17 we moved in together. We’re both from San Martín, we have a group of friends in common.

“He used to go on vacation to Mar del Tuyú, and in 2018 I went there with my family, and that’s when I really got to know him.

“We’d see each other on the beach, we talked that summer, and it wasn’t until the end of the year that we actually got together. For our first date, he invited me to the nephew’s country house, which was for his birthday.”



Olivia, their first born, arrived in 2020, and they soon became young parents.

She revealed: “When Olivia was born, we were living in a studio apartment in Urquiza, which Enzo’s agent paid for.

“During the pandemic, the three of us were there, and I was working at a call centre, while he didn’t have a salary yet. At that time, we bought our daughter’s used clothes on Facebook Marketplace.

“We used to take the bus; Enzo would get off at General Paz and catch another one to River, and I’d keep going to the Urquiza station because I worked downtown at an empanada shop, and later at the call centre near the Obelisk.”

In 2022, Enzo moved from River Plate to Benfica. Valentina and Olivia uprooted to Lisbon to start a new life.



But, they weren’t there long. Some five months after he made his debut for the Portuguese giants, Enzo was transferred again.

This time, it was Chelsea calling in a then British record £107million deal.

Valentina and Olivia followed once more, before they could catch their breath in Portugal.

In October 2023, Enzo and Valentina welcomed a son to their brood, when Benjamin was born.



On the surface, they seemed to be the happiest of families. But, underneath the surface, cracks were beginning to show.

A brief split

In November 2024, Enzo and Valentina had parted ways.

Argentine journalist Julieta Argenta claimed that Fernandez told her he wanted to “live alone”.

She added context in a social media post, writing: “They’re still family, but he feels the need to experience the stage he skipped by choosing family early on.”



Valentina admitted she was blindsided by the break-up in an interview with Paparazzi magazine.

She said: “Everything was fine and suddenly one day he told me that he didn’t want to be anymore. There are things that I still have to process, but that’s it, I accepted it.”

Valentina confessed that she cried for five minutes when Fernandez told her about the breakup, but her background of being the daughter of separated parents shaped her perspective.



It got complicated

Barely three months after they went their separate ways, Enzo seemingly had a change of heart.

They were seen walking around London kissing and holding hands, and it seemed their romance was back on

But, reports in Argentina claimed that he moved to repair his relationship, after finding out an unnamed Argentina international team-mate had tried to seduce Valentina.

In an explosive claim about the midfielder’s apparent decision to backtrack on his decision, journalist Daniel Fava revealed it was linked to a move by another member of Argentina’s winning World Cup squad on Enzo’s long-time partner.

Fava said on TV show A la tarde in January 2025: “In the last few hours there’s been a reconciliation with his ex-partner Valentina Cervantes. They’re giving things another go.”



He added: “The information I have is that Enzo Fernandez is desperately trying to win her back because he’s heard that a fellow world champion is sniffing around her.”

The Argentine journalist offered no further clues about the identity of the mystery player he was pointing the finger at, or whether he even knew his name.



After a colleague interrupted to say: “What you’re saying is that he prefers to get back with her than see another man jumping in,” he said of Valentina: “Today she’s prettier than ever.

“Since the separation she has gained a new sex appeal and energy” before making a second bombshell claim “more than one footballer” had contacted her over social media since the shock split.

A fly in the ointment

Not long after Enzo and Valentina had rekindled their romance, it was claimed that blonde beauty Wanda Nara had slipped into his DM’s.

Wanda hosts Celebrity Masterchef in her homeland, and back in October 2025 Valentina was a contestant on the show.

Reports in Argentina said Wanda and Valentina appeared frosty with each other, and apparently for good reason too.



According to La Nacion, Wanda sent Enzo a flirty message that read: “I just saw you around the neighbourhood, write to me if you want.”

It’s claimed that, rather than respond, he immediately showed the message to Valentina.

And this is allegedly what annoyed Wanda.



Valentina blasted reports of alleged messages between her man and Wanda.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “Yes, I saw it. No, as far as I know, I haven’t seen any messages.

“No, no, Enzo never spoke to me about anything. No, he never spoke to me about any of that.”

Sports.title: Man Utd, Chelsea and Arsenal’s wage changes revealed after huge summer transfers as Tottenham see startling payday rise
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE clubs set a new spending record in the summer transfer window.

Tuesday’s deadline brought about the end of the PRICIEST window in Prem history.



The 20 clubs in England’s top flight spent over £3BILLION reinforcing their respective squads.

Manchester City were the biggest spenders, dropping a whopping £427MILLION in a spree which saw them sign Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez for £116m and £125m respectively.



The duo, 23 and 25 respectively, will no doubt be on monster pay packets that will have driven up City’s wage bill.

But the Sky Blues aren’t top of the Prem pile when it comes to increased player wages.



Following the closure of the transfer window, Research by BOYLE Sports football odds calculated the estimated annual wage changes for clubs during the transfer window.

And it emerged that Tottenham Hotspur had the BIGGEST increase in wages thanks to their summer splurge, in which they signed Sandro Tonali, Savio and Matheus Fernandes for a combined £270m.

They have also taken on the wages of Chelsea outcast Mykhailo Mudryk, which have contributed to a whopping £79.3M increase in annual player salaries at the north London club.

They partially offset that outlay by knocking off £39.1M of wages off their books, which equalled a net change of £40.2M



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The newly promoted sides round off the top four, with Hull City, Ipswich Town and Coventry City sitting in second, third and fourth place respectively.

Hull had a net change of £29.8M, having taken on £33.8M in wages and getting rid of £4M worth of player salaries.

Ipswich had a net change of £24.9m, having taken on £34.4M worth of wages and selling players with a combined annual salary of £9.5M.

Coventry City had a £21.6M net change as they got rid of £2.7M worth of salaries, although they took on £24.3M worth of wages.



The bottom three in the list makes for surprising reading.

Despite being the biggest spenders of the window, City are rock bottom of the table.

They took on £44.2M worth of wages, but got a whopping £99.4M off the books. That led to a net change of -£55.2 for the Citizens.



Chelsea are 19th in the table with a net wage change of -£19M.

The Blues have taken on £50.6M worth of wages while getting rid of players who had a combined annual salary of £69.6M.

Newcastle round out the bottom three with a net change of -£17.6.

The Magpies took on £27.8M worth of wages while offloading combined annual salaries of £45.4M

Manchester United are 17th in the table with a net change of -£13.6M after taking on £20.6M worth of wages and offloading players with a combined annual salary of £34.2M.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

And defending Prem champions Arsenal’s net change of -£3M, which they racked up by picking up £31.4M worth of wages and getting £34.4M off their books.

With the window now closed and the season in full swing, fans will be praying their teams’ respective dealings in the transfer window bear fruit.

Sports.title: Patrick Vieira called me an ‘idiot’ – but I was having a word in Emmanuel Petit’s ear trying to get him to bite
Sports.content:
TIM SHERWOOD has recalled the time Patrick Vieira called him an IDIOT – however he was having a word in his Arsenal team-mate Emmanuel Petit’s ear at the time.

Former England international Sherwood is co-hosting The Sun’s brilliant new show Greatest Of All Teams, brought to you by Sun Vegas.



And in the latest episode he recalls a moment in the tunnel before a North London derby between Tottenham and Arsenal.

Sherwood tells of Vieira: “One of the best. He could do everything.



“When I was at Tottenham, I used to try and gain an edge in the tunnel, even before the game started.

“Just verbals, really. ‘Here they come, look at them coming out.’

“I used to go in Emmanuel Petit’s ear and he used to bite back, used to give me some back.

“And I remember Patrick just staring forward and saying to Manu, ‘Just ignore that idiot.’”

Also in the latest episode, Sherwood told the brilliant tale of how Zinedine Zidane and Christophe Dugarry almost ended up in Lancashire – three years before they won the World Cup for France.

Sherwood captained Rovers to their 1994-95 Premier League triumph.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

New manager Ray Harford tried to build on the success by strengthening the squad.

But owner Jack Walker was not convinced they needed Zidane – because they already had Sherwood in midfield.

Sherwood said: “It was a huge change after we won the league. It was almost like a relief that we’d got over the line.



“Arsenal got over the line after finishing twice on a couple of occasions.

“You see what they’ve done, they’ve bought players. We didn’t do that.

“There was an opportunity to sign Dugarry and Zidane. I remember them coming to the Blackburn training ground.

“Jack Walker said, ‘Why do we need Zidane? We’ve got Tim Sherwood.’

“Zidane… I’m a little bit embarrassed even now thinking about that.



“Jack used to like a drink, to be fair. And that day, he might have liked it a little bit more than usual.

“Zidane could have sat on a bench a few times, watched me perform, learned the Premier League. I could have told him the best boozers to go to in Blackburn.

“But I have to put a caveat on it. That’s not the Zidane he grew to be. He was a young Zidane.

“But you’re the champions of the Premier League, a huge league. Everyone started wanting to come there. They still do want to come.

“You’ve got to put the foundations in. If you’ve got an opportunity to sign superstars like that at a time from France, they should have turned it around.”



Manchester United fan and content creator Flex joined co-hosts StevoTheMadman and Sherwood in The Sun’s G.O.A.T studio.

Sports.title: Boulter blown away by Muchova at US Open
Sports.content:
Katie Boulter suffered a nightmare US Open exit in a punishing straight sets defeat to Karolina Muchova in under an hour at Flushing Meadows.

The British No 1 was broken in all seven of her service games in a chastening 6-1 6-0 defeat inside 58 minutes on Louis Armstrong Stadium.

Boulter traded breaks with Muchova at the start of the first set only for the 2026 Wimbledon finalist to pull clear and put on a clinic for her beleaguered opponent.

Boulter double faulted eight times and produced 22 unforced errors in a nightmare, error-strewn performance that left her hopes of progressing in tatters.

'All-round Muchova can do anything'

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman:

"It was a tough day at the office for Boulter, and that is where Muchova deserves so much credit. She is such an all-round player. The focus was definitely on Muchova rather than what Boulter didn't do.

"The highlight reel from the match was outstanding. There were so many incredible shots and great rallies. She's got the variation, using the little short chip cross-court, following the ball in and knocking off volleys at the net. She can do anything.

"She has reached the French Open and Wimbledon finals and is great on hard courts. If she can stay healthy, she has the experience, mentality, confidence and belief to win one of these tournaments one day."

Image: Katie Boulter failed to hold serve once in a chastening US Open exit to Karolina Muchova

'Bad day at office for Boulter'

Sky Sports Tennis' Laura Robson:

"You've got to focus on the positives, and that was how well Muchova played.

"She showed us every trick in the book. She has so much in her repertoire. She's playing with a lot of confidence for something who hasn't played a lot since Wimbledon.

"Not a good day at the office for Boulter."

Muchova in mix for maiden Grand Slam?

Sky Sports Tennis' Jonathan Overend:

"Karolina Muchova has yet to win a Grand Slam in her career but played some exceptional tennis. On that evidence, she has brilliant potential in this tournament.

"A day to forget for Katie Boulter. She just wasn't there and lost her serve seven times out of seven. That does not give you a chance."

Choinski four-day first-round run brought to end

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Botic Van de Zandschulp vs Jan Choinski from the US Open

Britain's Jan Choinski made it to day four at the US Open, but was still a first-round casualty.

The towering German-born 30-year-old was beaten in straight sets by fellow beanpole, Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp.

Getting to the first Wednesday at Flushing Meadows is usually a notable achievement for a British player.

But Choinski's stay at the tournament was only extended after his first-round match was pushed back by the rain in New York.

A handful of players were already through to round three by the time Choinski took to the court, but he was soundly beaten in the big-serving battle 6-3 6-1 7-6 (5) in just under two hours.

Choinski is coached by his girlfriend Sophia, who was shouting encouragement from his players' box.

He said: "She always tries to help me, tries to keep me positive, for sure.

"In the first set it was quite good, I had some chances but from that point it got tough.

"The guy was playing aggressively and she just keeps me fighting and motivated. But in a match like that it's quite tough."

Sports.title: Walsh winner helps send Chelsea through in Women’s Champions League
Sports.content:
Chelsea booked their spot in the Women's Champions League league phase after a 1-0 win over Real Sociedad in the second leg of their third qualifying round tie.

The Blues sealed a 6-2 aggregate victory during a lacklustre match in Spain, which saw Keira Walsh score the only goal of the game in the 54th minute.

The England midfielder's strike subsequently secured Chelsea's place in Friday's draw for the league phase of the competition.

Blues boss Sonia Bompastor made four changes to the side that won 5-2 in London last week, with Lucy Bronze, Kadiesha Buchanan, Lexi Potter and Wieke Kaptein all starting.

Ellie Carpenter caused problems in the early stages of the first half by sending a series of teasing crosses into the box.

Lauren James blasted the ball past the post and Walsh latched onto another brilliant cross from Carpenter, but Julia Arrula easily saved before being called into action to deny Carpenter.

With the score goalless at half-time, Giulia Dragoni was introduced after the break to make her Chelsea debut.

Aggie Beever-Jones had the best chance of the game 53 minutes in after being played through by Carpenter and her strike was palmed away by Arrula.

However, from the resulting corner Chelsea suddenly opened the scoring from a short routine which reached Walsh outside the box and the midfielder curled the ball home.

Hannah Hampton pushed Ainhoa Marin's strike behind for a corner as Sociedad enjoyed a brief threatening spell.

Nelly Las dragged a shot wide for Chelsea, who comfortably navigated the closing stages of the match to reach the league phase.

Sports.title: Wrexham earn first win of the season at Millwall
Sports.content:
Wrexham got their first win of the Championship season in style as Millwall were swept aside 3-0 at the New Den.

Alex Neil's home side were coming off the back of a chastening 5-1 thrashing by Southampton on Saturday and their formerly steadfast defence suffered another horror show as their hopes of repeating last season's promotion push were dealt a blow.

After starting with two clean sheets in victories over Bristol City and Norwich, it is now eight goals conceded in two games after Wrexham put them to the sword with some clinical finishing.

Defender Zak Sturge was unfortunate in turning Issa Kabore's effort past his own goalkeeper in the first half, but there was nothing lucky about the goals scored by Phil Parkinson's side after the break as Kieffer Moore and Jacques Ekomie provided excellent finishes to hoist the visitors into the top half of the table.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kieffer Moore doubles Wrexham's lead against Millwall.

It means the Welsh side finally got their campaign going after drawing with Cardiff and Watford before losing at home to Birmingham.

They were better team throughout. Mark Sykes drilled an effort narrowly wide of the post for Millwall after 11 minutes, the only time they truly threatened.

At the other end, Max Cleworth's header from a deep Matty James free-kick sailed harmlessly wide, as neither side offered much in the opening 25 minutes.

There was an element of fortune about the opening goal in the 28th minute. Moore played a through ball to send Kabore clear inside the area. His strike hit Sturge and spun out of the reach of goalkeeper Max Crocombe to hand the visitors the lead.

Lyndon Dykes fired wide on the half-volley in stoppage time at the end of a first half in which the home side carried little threat and rarely troubled Anthony Patterson.

Lewis O'Brien was guilty of a dreadful miss at the start of the second half, leaning back and scooping the ball over the crossbar after being played in eight yards out by Moore.

But Wrexham would not have long to wait for their second goal and it arrived a minute later. Moore picked up the ball in space 20 yards out and was given time to move it on to his right foot, take aim and send a perfectly placed drive into the bottom corner.

The game was over as a contest with just over 20 minutes to go. Substitute Danny Imray got free down the right and pulled the back to near the penalty spot where Ekomie was waiting, evading the attentions of Jake Cooper to sweep a finish into the corner and wrap up the win, as home supporters began to stream out of the stadium.

Sports.title: Burrell double steers QPR to victory
Sports.content:
Rumarn Burrell scored both QPR goals as they beat Cardiff 2-1 at Loftus Road to continue their impressive start to the Championship season.

Rangers produced a fine attacking display and were deserved winners, but had to endure a somewhat anxious finish after Perry Ng pulled a goal back with a thumping strike.

Julien Stephan's side are second in the table with 10 points from their opening four matches - and the two points dropped came in a goalless draw against Bolton in which they did everything but score.

They went ahead via Nicolas Madsen's right-wing corner after 36 minutes. The ball struck Jimmy Dunne, Cardiff were unable to clear the danger, and Burrell finished from close range.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rumarn Burrell is on a hat-trick as his clinical finish doubles QPR's lead against Cardiff.

The goal came shortly after Cian Ashford had missed a great chance to put Cardiff ahead, meekly heading wide of the target after being found unmarked at the far post from Ollie Tanner's cross.

Rangers had chances before the opener as well - Dunne headed wide from Harvey Vale's corner and Alfie Lloyd blasted over after being set up by Burrell's flick-on.

Burrell, who scored 10 goals last season before suffering a hamstring injury in January, was too hot for the Bluebirds' defence to handle, and scored again eight minutes into the second half.

Ronnie Edwards did superbly, winning the ball in his own half, riding a challenge and then threading a perfect through-ball to release Burrell, who sprinted towards the Cardiff box and showed fine composure to steer his shot beyond goalkeeper Nathan Trott and into the far corner of the net.

QPR continued to dominate and had they taken one of a number of chances to score a third, they would have enjoyed a much more comfortable end to the game.

After Lloyd's shot was saved by Trott, Glen Kamara moved the loose ball on to Koki Saito, who sliced horribly high and wide of the target, before the fit-again - and hugely impressive - Tariq Lamptey fired a shot straight at Trott.

Burrell had a couple of opportunities to complete his hat-trick, dragging an effort wide and seeing another deflected off target.

Stephan then made a quadruple substitution, either replacing or moving three of his back four, and his team lost some momentum.

Fortunate to still be in the game, Cardiff were given a lifeline when Ng unleashed an unstoppable thunderbolt into the top corner from long range on 74 minutes.

Substitute Joel Colwill had a chance to equalise but was unable to get a finishing touch to a cross from former QPR man Chris Willock.

Sports.title: Carse left out of England squad for third Pakistan Test
Sports.content:
Brydon Carse and Matthew Fisher have both been left out of England's 15-man squad for the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

England are chasing a 3-0 series sweep, live from September 9-13 on Sky Sports, having thrashed the tourists by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley before claiming a 194-run victory at Lord's.

Carse was withdrawn from the squad for the second Test, after the Cricket Regulator initiated a probe into an incident that saw the Durham player briefly arrested outside a Derby nightclub on August 22.

Image: Brydon Carse has been left out England's squad for the third Test

Derbyshire Police are looking into "allegations of assault" against the 31-year-old, with right-armer Sonny Baker retaining his place in Joe Root's squad as Carse's replacement, while Fisher misses out after being unused in the first two Tests.

Carse was also left out of Durham's squad for their County Championship match against Northamptonshire, which began on Wednesday, due to 'pre-arranged workload management", despite finishing with match figures of 4-95 in their previous win over Gloucestershire.

Image: Carse featured in the County Championship for Durham last week

Speaking at Lord's last week, England captain Joe Root described himself as "hacked off" by the growing number of alcohol-related stories around the team, adding: "I've spoken to Brydon and when I first found out my first concern was him as a person.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gave his reaction to the latest incident involving an England player at a nightclub, after video footage emerged of Brydon Carse in handcuffs on Saturday night

England's interim head coach Marcus Trescothick has indicated a preference to field his strongest possible side in pursuit of a 3-0 scoreline, rather than ring the changes.

That means Baker and Sam Cook may be kept on the sidelines, unless it is decided that any of the in-form pace attack of Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Atkinson need to be rested.

An inexperienced Pakistan outfit have been skittled for under 200 in all four innings so far, only batting beyond 50 overs once, with the relentless accuracy of Robinson - who finished with match figures of 8-35 in the second Test, backed up brilliantly by England's other seamers.
