As well as Whittaker, Israel international forward Sayed Abu Farchi has also completed a move to Colorado for a $6m (£4.4m) fee.

3 Herrington was a high-profile departure from the Colorado Rapids this summer, and has since made his Premier League debut for Hull Credit: Getty

MLS sides are allowed to sign a maximum three designated players - a rule that allows franchises to sign up to three players considered outside their salary cap.

And Whittaker's anticipated arrival will see to become the Rapids' club second DPs, alongside Aaronson.

Colorado have enjoyed a solid season so far, and currently sit seventh in the Western Conference with 31 points after 22 matches.

Sports.title: Clippers stripped of FIVE first-round picks and slapped with $30m fine as NBA rules on Kawhi Leonard secret payment scandal
Sports.content:
The NBA is stripping the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round picks, issuing a $30 million fine to billionaire owner Steve Ballmer and suspending the former Microsoft CEO for one year following an investigation into improper payments to All-Star Kawhi Leonard, the league announced Wednesday.

'The investigation found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules,' read the league statement.

Leonard will pay $700,000 restitution for improper benefits he and his uncle/representative Dennis Robertson received from the Clippers and other organizations. However, the 35-year-old Leonard will not have any contracts voided by the league as a result of the NBA investigation.

Robertson, meanwhile, has been banned from any business dealings with the NBA.

Additionally, Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has been suspened without pay for six months while president of business operations Gillian Zucker got a one-year ban.

According to the a summary report prepared by law firm Wachtell Lipton, the Clippers violated NBA rules by 'initiating off-court income opportunities between Mr. Leonard and four companies doing business with the team.'

The NBA is stripping the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round picks, issuing a $30 million fine to billionaire owner Steve Ballmer

Kawhi Leonard came out of the year-long investigation with his earnings nearly intact

Those companies include Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance.

Additionally, the Clippers are accused of facilitating endorsement deals, inducing companies to enter into these agreements by offering other business with the team, and personal expenses on behalf of Leonard and his representatives.

Lastly, the team failed to report improper solicitations made on Leonard's behalf by Robertson.

Leonard and Robertson are accused of violating NBA rules by ‘pressuring the Clippers to assist [Leonard] in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses,’ according to the statement.

The Clippers recently agreed to trade Leonard back to Toronto, where he won an NBA title in 2019, but the deal with the Raptors was placed on hold as the league investigation continued over the summer. It remains unclear where Leonard will be playing in 2026-27.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from Leonard's agent and Clippers spokespeople.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver's predecessor, the late David Stern, similarly stripped the Minnesota Timberwolves of five first-round picks after discovering the team had circumvented the salary cap to pay star forward Joe Smith in 2000. However, the Wolves were fined only $3.5 million at the time.

The allegations first surfaced on Pablo Torre's podcast nearly one year ago. Since then, NBA has been investigating the Clippers and Ballmer for allegedly facilitating an under-the-table side deal for Leonard that allowed the team to add other stars, such as Paul George. The team has repeatedly denied the accusations, while Ballmer stated he had no knowledge of Leonard's alleged $21 million 'no-show' endorsement deal with the doomed financial services firm, Aspiration.

Torre made the claim against the Clippers by citing a 2025 bankruptcy filing that names the team and a company owned by Leonard under the list of creditors for Aspiration QFZ, LLC, a subsidiary of fintech and sustainability brand Aspiration Partners Inc.

Torre claimed to have contracts showing Aspiration QFZ, LLC entered into a $28 million 'no-show' agreement with Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, and later claimed - following a report from the Boston Sports Journal - that Leonard also received a separate $20million 'side deal' from Aspiration.

Ballmer invested $50million in Aspiration.

Daily Mail obtained a federal bankruptcy filing showing unsecured claims of $30 million and $7 million for the LA Clippers and Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, respectively

The bankruptcy filing from federal court in Delaware, obtained by the Daily Mail, also shows unsecured claims of $30 million and $7 million for the Clippers and Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, respectively.

And while Ballmer said he was 'embarrassed' that he didn't pick up on any financial trouble from Aspiration, he defended his and the Clippers actions and said they 'weren't involved' in the company's deal with Leonard.

Aspiration Partners Inc. co-founder Joe Sanberg pleaded guilty to two counts of wire fraud in 2025 for what authorities described as a $248million scheme to defraud investors.

The team, as it pointed out in a statement, 'ended its relationship with Aspiration years ago, during the 2022-23 season, when Aspiration defaulted on its obligation.'

Furthermore, as reported by Torre, Aspiration QFZ's alleged payments to KL2 Aspire were sent to Robertson, Leonard's uncle and advisor, who was previously investigated by the NBA in 2019 for allegedly requesting impermissible benefits for his nephew and himself.

That 2019 investigation did not find any impermissible benefits going from the Clippers to Leonard or anyone working on his behalf.

A year later, a self-described acquaintance of Leonard and Robertson named Johnny Wilkes sued the Clippers, claiming he was still owed $2.5 million from the team for helping them to sign the former Spurs and Raptors star.

Wilkes, a self-described acquaintance of Robertson, claimed in the lawsuit that Ballmer would 'fund a $100,000,000.00 marketing campaign for Kawhi Leonard' and the uncle would get his own Southern California home if the All-Star forward agreed to sign with the Clippers.

That lawsuit was ultimately dismissed and neither the Clippers nor Robertson admitted to any wrongdoing.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez risks wrath of Chelsea fans with claim he 'dreamed of joining a big club' after sealing £125m Man City move - as he joins Enzo Maresca in refusing to refer to Blues by name
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez risks wrath of Chelsea fans with claim he 'dreamed of joining a big club' after sealing £125m Man City move - as he joins Enzo Maresca in refusing to refer to Blues by name

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Fernandez has risked the wrath of Chelsea fans after claiming it was a dream to play for a club 'as big' as Man City after his £125million move, while only referencing the Blues as his 'previous club'.

Fernandez completed his transfer to Man City on deadline day, with the deal equalling the British transfer record fee paid by Liverpool to Newcastle for Alexander Isak last summer.

The Argentine had previously angered Chelsea supporters by flirting with a move to Real Madrid last season, leading to him being suspended by the club for two matches.

Fernandez had tried to explain his departure to Chelsea fans on social media by stating he had not been in a 'good place'.

'Life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I've said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart,' Fernandez wrote.

'But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.'

Enzo Fernandez declared he 'always dreamed of being at a club as big as Man City'

Fernandez comments are likely to anger Chelsea fans, as he also referred to the Blues only as his 'previous club'

Fernandez had followed Enzo Maresca as not referring to Chelsea by name after joining City

Despite the sentiments, Fernandez followed Enzo Maresca in avoiding Chelsea by name after completing the move, with the Italian having referred to them as a 'different club' after joining Man City.

Fernandez also spoke of his dream of playing for a 'big club'.

'I'm really happy to be here,' Fernández said. 'I always dreamed of being at a club as big as City.

'I'm grateful for the opportunity. It's a very emotional moment for me and my family, to take this step at 25 years old, in a football career that I always dreamed of.

'I'm so happy to be here, enjoying these first few hours I've had at the club. I can already see just how big it is and, we will enjoy ourselves and win lots of things together.

'Manchester City have to win every trophy they compete for,' he said. 'In every competition we play in, we have to compete and win, because this club's history demands that.

'To be honest, from the first day they believed in me and called me to say they wanted me to join the club, I didn't hesitate for a second.'

When speaking about linking up again with Maresca, Fernandez added: 'He is a top manager, honestly, I had him at my previous club.'

They were incredible moments. I learned so much with him.

'I'm also grateful because he was very important in bringing me here. So it's a huge pleasure for me to work alongside him and enjoy it.

'To be honest, we were both very eager for it to happen, because it wasn't easy for me to be here today.

'But I know he also made a big effort, speaking to the club, and I'm grateful that he did that.

'It was a long few days, but in the end I'm here and I'm very happy to be joining this club.'

Sports.title: Bizarre moment US Open tennis star is handed CASH by a fan after winning her match
Sports.content:
Italian tennis star Jasmine Paolini was handed a bizarre good luck charm after her victory on Court 5 at the US Open on Wednesday.

In the early morning session on the outer court, Paolini managed to easily handle her fellow countrywoman Lucrezia Stefanini in straight sets, 6-4, 6-1.

After the match, Paolini was signing autographs and greeting fans when she was approached by a blonde woman wearing sunglasses.

The woman then produced a $2 bill, which Paolini initially thought was something she wanted signed. Instead, the spectator explained: 'It's for you. It's a $2 bill, they're rare, and they represent good luck.'

Paolini then thanked the fan, who advised the Italian to keep it in her bag the rest of the tournament.

It appears that some sort of good luck message was inscribed on the bill for the 19-seed in the women's singles bracket, who then held it up to the camera with a surprised look.

Italian tennis star Jasmine Paolini was gifted a strange good luck charm by a fan

A woman handed Paolini a $2 bill, noting that they're 'rare' and a token of 'good luck'

Paolini beat countrywoman Lucrezia Stefanini in straight sets to book a third-round spot

While not exactly rare – with 1.7billion $2 bills active in the United States – they're not commonly seen among the 55.6billion paper bills in circulation.

'I thought it was a nice gift and she told me this was the lucky one,' Paolini told the New York Post.

'[She said] 'keep it for yourself.' I was like, okay. I put it in the bag and it [will] stay with me. We'll see if it's going to work. That's the important thing.'

Paolini cruised to a victory in the second set after a close first frame which the 30-year-old won when Stefanini returned a serve into the net.

The world No. 21 has only gone as far as the Round of 16 at Flushing Meadows, which was accomplished back in 2024 – the same year she reached the final at both Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

With a spot in the third round secure, Paolini faces 16-seed Sorana Cîrstea of Romania.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods strikes deal and pleads no contest to reckless driving... after arriving at court with doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tiger Woods has pleaded no contest reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test after striking a deal with prosecutors in the wake of his DUI arrest.

The golf legend was suited-and-booted as he arrived at court with girlfriend Vanessa Trump on his arm, looking stoic while wading through photographers outside the Martin County Court shortly after 8am on Wednesday.

Woods was pictured in the courtroom moments later, where he stood in front of a judge and changed his plea. He was originally charged with driving under the influence but has now pleaded no contest to a lesser charge of reckless driving.

As part of the deal, Woods will have his license suspended for five years.

The 15-time major champion was found at the scene of the crash in Jupiter, Florida, with two opioid tablets in his pocket, on March 27.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but had not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving at a hearing in Florida on Wednesday

Woods appeared puffy-eyed as he left the court alongside doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump

Vanessa led him back to a car after he had pleaded no contest and had his license suspended

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

He was able to crawl out of the car without any injuries before later admitting to officers he was looking at his phone and changing the radio at the time of the collision.

A Breathalyzer test did not reveal any alcohol in Woods’s system, but he refused a urine test, according to police.

The Sheriff’s report obtained by the Daily Mail said deputies found opioids in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment.

A previous hearing was held on August 4, following a July ruling that allowed prosecutors to obtain Woods' hospital records that were connected to the crash.

Martin County circuit court judge Darren Steele approved an agreement between the State Attorney's Office and Woods' legal team that allowed prosecutors to request records from the hospital that treated the PGA legend following his crash.

Back in May, Steele approved a similar agreement granting prosecutors access to Woods' prescription medication records from his Palm Beach pharmacy between January 1 and his March crash.

Prosecutors and Woods's attorney have agreed to a protective order that limits the release of any hospital or prescription records to the State Attorney's Office, law enforcement, state experts and the defense.

Woods appeared puffy-faced as he arrived for his change-of-plea hearing in Florida

Vanessa was front and center inside the court as Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving

Woods in the back of a police cruiser after being arrested on suspicion of DUI in March

Woods was closing in on a return to golf and was widely expected to compete at The Masters in the days before the crash.

He hasn't competed since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon in Scotland and has since undergone surgery to repair a torn Achilles as well as a seventh back procedure.

Woods' legal problems have since been put into perspective by Vanessa's cancer diagnosis. She revealed her bout with an unspecified form of breast cancer back in May.

The March crash marked the fourth major driving-related incident of Woods's adult life.

Five years earlier, when Woods rolled another SUV down a steep embankment in California, he did not face any accusations of driving under the influence. Instead, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department claimed Woods was driving at around 80mph, nearly twice the legal limit, at the time of the crash.

Witnesses told TMZ that Woods appeared agitated and impatient while leaving a golf tournament parking lot in the moments before the crash.

Woods after his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) in Jupiter, Florida, on May 29, 2017. He later pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Woods changed his original not guilty plea in the wake of his DUI arrest back in March

Vanessa with him and her 19-year-old daughter Kai back in March

Woods was never charged in 2021, but he wasn't so lucky in 2017, when he was found by Jupiter police about 15 miles from his home. Officers said they found him unconscious in his Mercedes-Benz, which was parked awkwardly on the roadside at around 3am.

Upon closer inspection, they noticed damage to his vehicle.

Woods didn't have any alcohol in his system, but later tests found the active ingredient for marijuana, two painkillers - Vicodin and Dilaudid - the sleep drug Ambien and the anti-anxiety drug Xanax.

He later claimed he had been self-medicating for pain caused by his fourth back surgery and insomnia. Woods did not specifically address the marijuana issue and he wasn't found with the drug in his possession.

Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving and received a year of probation, a $250 fine and was ordered to undergo 50 hours of community service. He was also banned from drinking alcohol during the probation.

In July 2017, Woods completed a private program to address his dependency on painkillers.

Woods stands alongside his lawyer to face County Judge Darren Steele on Wednesday

In April the Daily Mail broke the news that the golfer would leaving the country 'imminently'

The golf great flipped his Land Rover clean onto its side during his accident in Jupiter

'I will continue to tackle this going forward with my doctors, family and friends,' he tweeted at the time. 'I am so very thankful for all of the support I've received.'

Woods' most notorious car crash took place in 2009, when he rammed his Cadillac Escalade into a fire hydrant, tree and several hedges near his home.

He was treated for minor injuries and received a ticket for careless driving, but while he thanked his then-wife Elin Nordegren for getting him out of the car, there were lingering doubts about the story. After all, it was only days earlier that the National Enquirer claimed he'd had an affair with Rachel Uchitel, a 9/11 widow and New York nightclub manager.

The alleged details of the November 27, 2009 crash were ultimately included in the best-selling biography by Jeff Benedict and Armen Keteyian, titled Tiger Woods.

Sports.title: Custom kits, $400,000 jewellery and battling online trolls: How Naomi Osaka and Aryna Sabalenka's eye-catching fashion statements are helping them transcend tennis
Sports.content:
For Naomi Osaka, preparations on the eve of this year’s US Open were a little unorthodox.

As well as hitting the practice court and allowing time for rest and recovery, the four-time Grand Slam champion prowled a deserted Billie Jean King National Tennis Center looking for backdrops for a series of glamorous high-fashion photoshoots. Dressed by Hollywood superstar Zendaya's stylist Law Roach, Osaka posted on Arthur Ashe, by concession stands, and, most improbably, in the creaky media workroom.

All of this was building to the ultimate spotlight. As she has done at this year’s Australian Open, Roland-Garros, and Wimbledon, Osaka walked out for her first-round match in a custom ensemble designed for the Grand Slam, this one inspired by basketball legend Allen Iverson and also styled by Law. Although she secured the necessary win, the match wasn’t nearly as memorable as the outfit, a sleeveless hoodie embroidered with burnt press clippings, over a full tulle ballgown skirt.

With her walk-on outfits this season, variously inspired or compared to jellyfish, the Eiffel Tower, Lucy Liu in Kill Bill, and the Japanese art of paper-cutting, Osaka has created a feverish atmosphere around the moment she steps onto court. Loved or loathed, the walk-on outfits have become part of Osaka’s package, as questioned and dissected by the media and online as her forehand - or maybe more.

But Osaka isn’t alone in using fashion to distinguish herself from her peers off the court. World No1 Aryna Sabalenka played her first round match wearing a staggering $400,000-worth of jewels on her neck, wrist, and ears. The ‘Silhouette’ suite was made for her by her jewellery sponsor Material Good, and is the fourth of four specially-designed sets made for Sabalenka to wear at each of the Grand Slams. Wimbledon’s, naturally, featured emeralds.

For players at the very top of the game, tennis is not the only thing fans are looking for on-court at the majors.

Naomi Osaka honoured NBA legend Allen Iverson, with her dramatic on-court ensemble at the US Open on Monday night in New York

Osaka donned Iverson's famed arm sleeves and headband as part of her latest fashion statement, which is distinguishing her off the court as well as on it

Osaka is not alone in delivering a fashion statment on court, with world No1 Aryna Sabalenka having been dripping in coloured gemstones as she stepped onto court in New York

The set is worth over £295,000 ($400,000) and reflects New York City's multicultural heritage

The headline-catching choices that both Sabalenka and Osaka have made are increasingly allowing them to transcend tennis, crossing into the mainstream with fashion and pop culture fans dissecting their tournament-specific looks on social media. They’re ripe for the water cooler too: tennis lovers in mothballs might clutch their pearls, but people are tuning in, with passing interest, to see what Osaka is wearing this time, or leafing through articles about Sabalenka in Vogue, TIME, or Vanity Fair.

Osaka has a particular platform for making sure she stands out on court, as the only active Nike player with a unique deal that affords her custom tennis kits. So exclusive that they’re not always for sale, her Australian Open dress sold out in the blink of an eye. Sabalenka, while given a one-of-one colour choice, isn’t so lucky, as she found out at this year’s Roland-Garros. After debuting her kit on TikTok in a splashy reveal for her followers, she was pipped to the court when world No93 Oksana Selekhmeteva wore the black and red mesh ballet-style dress in her defeat to Marta Kostyuk, purchased off the rack.

‘Let’s wait for 2027, because that will be sick!’ Sabalenka teased when asked about not having exclusive looks at the 2025 WTA Finals. For another year then, she must grin and bear it.

Of course, fashion statements do not solely benefit those wearing the clothes. Coco Gauff is an ambassador for Italian high-end fashion brand Miu Miu, who pounced on the opportunity to partner with her kit sponsor New Balance on a number of custom outfits since 2025 - a move that might have Gucci ambassador Sabalenka wishing Nike was a little less stringent in its aversion to partnerships. The American star wore one of these at this year’s Wimbledon, landing her on a raft of ‘best dressed lists’, with fellow player Jelena Ostapenko telling Daily Mail Sport it was her favourite of the tournament. More pertinently, it boosted Miu Miu’s visibility and ties to a sport which is only growing in popularity and cultural prominence.

Traditional sponsors are also leaning in to the power of a unique fashion moment can have for a growing star. Nike has singled out rising Filipina talent Alexandra Eala for special recognition, as she quickly becomes one of the most famous faces in her region as the first player from the Philippines to break into the top 20 and make the fourth round of a major. At Wimbledon last year, she was given a white hair accessory in the shape of a sampaguita - her country’s national flower - to wear for her Centre Court debut. In New York this week, she stepped onto court to play an exhibition match during Fan Week wearing trainers customised with a tag which commemorated her first WTA title, which she won at the start of the month in Washington.

Even the men’s tour are getting in on the action. World No14 Lorenzo Musetti was the picture of Italian elegance when he admirably sported a white leather Bottega Veneta bomber jacket for his Wimbledon walk-on as temperatures hit 35 degrees in south London. German outfitter Hugo Boss looked to outdo this the following year by providing Taylor Fritz with a full white suit to step onto court in, the Roger Federer throwback only a little dented by the fact that the trousers were Velcro tear-off for ease. There are still teething problems on that side of the draw, with Matteo Berrettini’s Boss outfit banned by Wimbledon for being the wrong shade of cream.

Osaka made a fashionable run-up to the tournament with a series of photoshoots around the Billie Jean King National Tennis Centre, including improbably in the media workroom

Osaka has garnered attention with a series of daring outfits at Grand Slams, starting with one some fans compared to a jellyfish with its billowing veil at the Australian Open

Osaka was inspired by the Eiffel Tour for Roland-Garros, while she was able to get creative with Wimbledon's strict dress code

Coco Gauff's Wimbledon outfit, a custom one produced by her sponsors Miu Miu and New Balance, was lauded

Sabalenka had to defend her US Open outfit which was branded 'trashy' by critics online, but appeared in a different version for her first round match

But as anyone making a fashion statement knows, execution can be hit or miss and the online fashion police are unafraid of twisting the knife. In New York, Sabalenka has had to stand firmly by her night-session dress, which was dubbed ‘trashy’ by critics online.

‘I love that it’s different. I love that this outfit is bold,’ Sabalenka said before the start of the tournament. ‘Whatever people saying on Internet, I heard they probably didn't like it.

’It’s like it's funny for me, because when Nike was pretty simple and standard, they were complaining. When Nike went really cool and fun and trying to get back, they always complain.’

Either way, people are talking about it. In 1989, Andre Agassi was mocked for taking part in a Canon advert where he declared ‘image is everything’. No one’s laughing now.

Sports.title: Revealed: The first stunning images of Newcastle's new £190m state-of-the-art training ground - including an 'energy centre', 'members' club' and 'war room' - spread across 260-acre site
Sports.content:
These are the stunning images of Newcastle United’s new £190million state-of-the-art training ground.

The pictures, obtained by Daily Mail Sport, are part of a brochure produced by architects Populous, who are set to lead the ambitious project on a 260-acre site near Newcastle Airport.

It was confirmed last month that the club had purchased the land at Woolsington, owned by former chairman Sir John Hall and his family.

Chief executive David Hopkinson said it was a ‘landmark moment’ for the club and the development would create ‘the world's best performance environment for our teams’.

And, as our images show, the plans are spectacular. Architects’ drawings include an ‘energy centre’, ‘health village’, ‘members’ club’ and ‘war room’, as well as a breathtaking hub named ‘The Stables’ looking out onto a walled garden. There are 17 full-size pitches, to be used by the first team and academy.

These are the stunning first images of Newcastle's new state-of-the-art training ground

The images are part of a brochure produced by architects Populous, who are set to lead the ambitious project on a 260-acre site near Newcastle Airport

Building a new training ground has long been part of the vision for the club's Saudi owners

The build is expected to cost the club a staggering £190m

The designs could still be modified and are all subject to planning approval

The club are hoping that the project will be completed by 2029

Architects’ drawings include an ‘energy centre’, ‘health village’, ‘members’ club’ and ‘war room’, as well as a breathtaking hub named ‘The Stables’ looking out onto a walled garden

There are 17 full-size pitches, to be used by the first team and academy

The designs, which could still be modified, are all subject to planning approval, with an intended completion date of the summer of 2029.

Newcastle have recently completed a £10m extension of their current training ground, but the announcement of the new facility is a show of intent from the club’s owners, at a time when the commitment of PIF was being questioned.

Hopkinson said: ‘We'll develop purpose-built facilities that are geared towards developing sustainable success in the future, where players, coaches and staff can perform at their very best every day.

‘We will be submitting a detailed planning application that not only demonstrates our vision, but also how we will preserve and enhance an historic estate, its biodiversity and wildlife habitats, and how we'll be a great neighbour.’

Brad Miller, the club’s chief operating officer, said: ‘Woolsington Hall will be a magnificent location for our new training complex, so we are delighted to have finalised our agreement to acquire the land.

‘We are finalising hugely exciting plans for the estate, which include renovating and enhancing listed structures and parkland and retaining them as key elements in our designs. Our aim is to carefully and thoughtfully develop world-class facilities for our players and staff, while bringing out the beauty of the location and preserving it for generations to come.

‘It is a highly complex project. We have a rigorous planning process ahead of us, but we will demonstrate how we intend to build something iconic that the club, fans, community and region can be proud of.

'We look forward to engaging with planners, our supporters and interested parties about our exciting plans. Our aim is to sustainably and responsibly move the project forward, delivering a facility that the city and region can be immensely proud of.’

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe 'kidnap' plot busted: Real Madrid superstar targeted by French gang along with 25 other celebrities - as man is arrested
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe 'kidnap' plot busted: Real Madrid superstar targeted by French gang along with 25 other celebrities - as man is arrested

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe was among high-profile figures targeted in a kidnapping plot by a French gang, French authorities have revealed.

The plot reportedly targeted 26 celebrities, including footballers, rappers and wealthy businessmen.

French newspaper Le Parisien reported the plot was allegedly orchestrated by an 18-year-old, named as Clement L.

The gang leader had already been jailed for armed robbery, after being identified as one of two men involved in an attack on a watchmaker in Paris.

It was discovered Clement L had already been on pre-trial detention for pimping, as well as organised robbery.

The gang leader was detained but was then discovered to have been sending orders from his cell via two mobile phones on Snapchat under the alias Lester Z.

Kylian Mbappe was among 26 wealthy individuals targeted in a kidnapping plot in France

A source close to the case told Le Parisien that the addresses of 26 wealthy individuals, including Mbappe, had been discovered on the phones.

The star was among a list including a Chinese businessman, jewellers and a Turkish meat trader.

'Two phones were seized by prison guards, and their contents were highly revealing,' the source said.

'He also wanted to go after a rapper and the footballer Kylian Mbappe.'

When questioned, the teenager claimed he was not the mastermind of the plot and had requested he be let out of solitary confinement.

He revealed he had dropped out of school while studying for a vocational qualification in cooking but wants to resume studying and become a chef.

Despite his request, it was ruled he remain in solitary confinement while the investigation continues.

Sports.title: Trabzonspor fail with approach for Richarlison as wantaway Tottenham star pushes for move ahead of Turkish transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Trabzonspor fail with approach for Richarlison as wantaway Tottenham star pushes for move ahead of Turkish transfer deadline

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Richarlison has agreed terms with Trabzonspor as the wantaway Tottenham forward looks to secure a move ahead of the Turkish transfer deadline.

Daily Mail Sport understands Richarlison wants to move, with the Brazilian liking the prospect of a new challenge and is keen to play alongside Mohamed Salah.

Richarlison, however, fears his soured relationship with Tottenham could put a deal at risk.

Tottenham had been keen for him to move to Everton with clubs having been in talks over a £35million deal, with Spurs having been looking to pay £60m for Iliman Ndiaye, who eventually joined Manchester City.

Trabzonspor are said to have offered £20million for Richarlison but Tottenham say they are yet to receive a bid.

The Turkish transfer window is open until Friday.

Richarlison is understood to have agree terms with Trabzonspor, as he looks to leave Tottenham

RIcharlison had shared a post this week on Instagram which read: 'I am the villain of many poorly told stories' amid uncertainty over his future

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi had revealed after Saturday's defeat to Newcastle that Richarlison, 29, was one of three players to have told him they wanted to leave the club.

Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr, who were also named by De Zerbi, joined Sunderland and Juventus on deadline day.

Richarlison had shared a social media post earlier this week declaring that he had 'decided that no one will ever again decide my future for me'.

In a separate post he had also shared a photograph of a wall with red and black text on it reading, in translation: 'I am the villain of many poorly told stories.'

The Brazilian was Tottenham's top scorer last season, scoring 11 goals in the league and 12 in all competitions.

Should Richarlison leave, it would continue a remarkable trend of Tottenham's top scorers leaving the club.

Harry Kane, Son Heung-min and Brennan Johnson have top scored in three of Tottenham's last four seasons before leaving.

Richarlison's prospective new club Trabzonspor have endured a difficult start to the season, winning one of their opening three league games, despite the high-profile signing of Salah.

Trabzonspor were knocked out of the Europa League after a 5-0 aggregate defeat to Ferencvaros in their play-off, which led to their manager Fatih Tekke announcing his resignation.

Despite initially blocking Tekke's resignation, Trabzonspor have now agreed to part ways.

Sports.title: Liverpool considered 8 wingers in summer transfer window before landing Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool considered 8 wingers in summer transfer window before landing Bradley Barcola

Liverpool made Bradley Barcola their final signing of the summer after sealing a £123million deal with Paris Saint-Germain but the Reds had a number of alternatives to the French winger

View 2 Images Liverpool eventually sealed a deal for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool had as many as eight alternatives to Bradley Barcola in the summer transfer window, including England’s Anthony Gordon and Real Madrid star Endrick.

‌



The Reds came into the window needing additions out wide following Mohamed Salah’s exit. They eventually signed Barcola in a £123million deal after a summer-long search followed by drawn-out negotiations with former side Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



But it is well known that the Frenchman was not the only player that Liverpool chiefs had in mind. Former RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande was a high-profile target, albeit Real Madrid swooped in to seal his services instead.

‌



And that appears to have been the theme with a host of their potential attacking targets. Former Everton and Newcastle man Anthony Gordon was an early possibility but he instead moved to Barcelona for £69m after the Spanish side chose not to activate their permanent £26m option for Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Liverpool were also left frustrated as their attempts to sign Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh ended without a positive result. Brighton received bids of £50m and £60m for the Gambian but chose to turn them down.

While Minteh eventually stayed where he was, the same cannot be said of the rest of Liverpool’s shortlist. Matias Fernandez-Pardo had emerged as an option following his standout performances for French side Lille, with Newcastle sealing a late deal worth £51m for his services.

Lyon wideman Malick Fofana was also eyed by Liverpool, but he too opted for a move to the north east, having sealed a deadline day switch to Sunderland.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool were previously interested in Anthony Gordon (Image: Getty Images)

Away from Barcola, Liverpool also had another PSG winger in mind in their search for attacking reinforcements. Ibrahim Mbaye was eventually on the move to the Premier League but signed for Aston Villa.

Their final two options were Real Madrid’s Endrick and Koln’s Said El Mala, but they eventually stayed with their current clubs.

‌



That left Liverpool pursuing a deal for Barcola, who is keen to lift silverware at Anfield. He said: "I hope to achieve very big thingsFirst of all, winning the Premier League – it's one of my biggest dreams in my life.

"It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that's why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.

"It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy. It took a long time but I'm really happy to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play."

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Man Utd deal announced, Arsenal double move, Folarin Balogun bombshell
Sports.content:
Latest transfer news from Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and more - as Premier League clubs break summer window record with £3.2billion spend

After a major summer of spending, the Premier League's summer transfer window drew to a close at 11pm on Tuesday evening. It was a record-shattering couple of months across the UK, with a total exceeding £3.2billion exceeded through deals.

Manchester City and Chelsea agreed a £125m deal for Enzo Fernandez, with the wantaway midfielder finally leaving Stamford Bridge after months of speculation regarding his future. The Cityzens also welcomed Iliman Ndiaye to their ranks in a £65m move, further bolstering Enzo Maresca's choice.

Sunderland's approach of Malick Fofana also dominated the headlines on Tuesday, with what should have been a straightforward move turning into quite the saga when Crystal Palace threatened to hijack the Black Cats' move.

With Kyril Louis-Dreyfus flying to Lyon to persuade the 21-year-old winger to join his project at the Stadium of Light, Fofana gave Sunderland the green-light to put the wheels in motion on a move, forced to submit a dealsheet to ensure a transfer due to the last-minute nature of his decision.

In West London, AS Monaco also knocked back Chelsea's £47m move for Lamine Camara in dramatic fashion. Everything had been agreed between the two clubs, when Monaco pulled the plug with just minutes to go until the deadline - with Everton's endeavours of securing Folarin Balogun having a knock-on effect.

Chelsea were reportedly left fuming with the incredibly unprofessional last-minute decision. And Balogun's deal didn't go through anyway, with Monaco's sporting director sensationally claiming it was the striker who walked away from the deal after 'feeling mistreated' during his medical.

Mykhailo Mudryk also joined Tottenham Hotspur on a season-long loan, with both clubs hopeful that the Ukrainian is able to reacclimate to the pace of the Premier League after a two-year lay-off.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho career lifeline emerges as ex-Man Utd ace eyed for free agent offer
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jadon Sancho career lifeline emerges as ex-Man Utd ace eyed for free agent offer

EXCLUSIVE: Jadon Sancho was left without a club this summer, but a lifeline for the former Manchester United ace could soon present itself

View 3 Images Jadon Sancho is currently without a club (Image: 2026 UEFA)

Ambitious Dubai side Arabian Falcons are preparing a pitch for former Manchester United star and free agent Jadon Sancho to join them.

‌



The Falcons are managed by ex-Liverpool and England ace Jonjo Shelvey, and have Leicester City Premier League winner Danny Simpson as a player-coach. When the transfer window slammed shut, Sancho was left without a club having been released by United at the end of June.

‌



Aston Villa opted not to make his loan move permanent, after signing him temporarily last season. It means Sancho is currently stuck in the wilderness of free agency, five years after signing for United from Borussia Dortmund for £72.9m.

‌



Fast forward to the present day, the Falcons are preparing to reach out to Sancho and other big name free agents without a club.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Mirror Football understands the Emirati football club are plotting an ambitious pitch to sway the likes of Sancho towards the club. They have already convinced one former United prodigy Ravel Morrison, who signed last summer and was recently made the captain of the side, to move to the Middle East.

‌



Sancho was linked with moves to Fiorentina and Roma, although neither club opted to sign him. He has also been linked with a surprise move to Brazilian side Palmeiras.

The former England international, who scored three goals in 23 international caps for the Three Lions, has played for four clubs in the last three seasons, including the appearances he made for United in the 2023-24 campaign

View 3 Images Shelvey is now in charge of Arabian Falcons (Image: Arabian Falcons FC)

‌



He had an emotional return to Dortmund on loan in the 2024 January transfer window and even played in the Champions League final at Wembley Stadium, which the German heavyweights lost 2-0 to Real Madrid.

After Dortmund opted not to sign him permanently, he spent a season on loan at Chelsea, where he won the Europa Conference League. A permanent move to Stamford Bridge not only didn't transpire, the Blues paid a £5m penalty fee to United to pull out of an obligation to sign him for £25m.

Villa were the next club to take him on loan, but he struggled to carve out a regular starting place in Unai Emery's team. He only contributed one goal and three assists in 39 appearances, although he did finish the campaign with a Europa League winners' medal.

‌



View 3 Images Jadon Sancho was last with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

The Falcons are hoping the prospect of living in Dubai, which also offers tax-free earnings, and the club's top quality facilities may be enough to sway the likes of Sancho. The forward has a history with the popular Emirati city, having previously flown out there to recover from injuries in the past.

He is not the only big-name player who is without a club. Former England team-mate Raheem Sterling also failed to find a new team in the summer, as did ex-United colleague Paul Pogba and many others.

Sports.title: Argentina star hints at retirement after FIFA's brutal ban - 'We'll talk and see'
Sports.content:
Argentina star hints at retirement after FIFA's brutal ban - 'We'll talk and see'

Leandro Paredes was at the centre of attention for all the wrong reasons during the World Cup

View Image Leandro Paredes could retire from international football with Argentina (Image: Getty Images)

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes has hinted he could walk away from international football, just days after Lionel Messi announced his own decision to step aside. His comments come in the wake of a chaotic World Cup final, where Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain and Paredes became embroiled in a mass post‑match brawl.

‌



The Boca Juniors man was seen trading blows at full‑time before shoving Spain's Gavi to the turf. FIFA's disciplinary committee has since issued a 10‑match ban and a £66,000 fine, while defender Nahuel Molina received a seven‑game suspension and the same financial penalty.

‌



Following an appeal from the Argentine FA, FIFA agreed to soften the impact of Paredes' punishment, allowing the suspension to be served across Class A friendlies as well as competitive fixtures.

‌



Argentina star slapped with 10-MATCH ban as FIFA announce World Cup punishments READ MORE :

Argentina World Cup fate decided after calls to ban finalists from next tournament READ MORE :

Yet he has suggested he has no plans to serve the lengthy suspension and is prepared to hold talks with Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni about his future.

"It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team," he admitted. "Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

"I haven't discussed it with the coach yet, but we'll talk and see what decision I make."

‌



Messi announced his retirement from international football last month in an extensive statement saying goodbye to Argentina, with his final outing coming in the World Cup final defeat to Spain.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury losing patience over Anthony Joshua fight - 'You're a coward!'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury losing patience over Anthony Joshua fight - 'You're a coward!'

Fury, 38, and Joshua, 36, signed separate contracts to fight each other earlier this year but Joshua's deal included the stipulation that the clash must take place in the UK

View Image Tyson Fury speaks out (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury has branded Anthony Joshua a "coward" as the row over the venue for their fight rumbled on.

‌



Fury, 38, and Joshua, 36, signed separate contracts to fight each other earlier this year. Joshua's deal included the stipulation that the clash must take place in the UK with Wembley the frontrunner. But Netflix and the showdown's Saudi Arabian backers want the fight - which is pencilled in for November 20 - moved to New York. Joshua is prepared to back down if a series of demands are met.

‌



But no deal has been agreed - and Fury claims he is running out of patience. "There is still no deal done and it's getting quite tiring," he said. "I've been down to fight in every location that's been mentioned; England, Ireland, Vegas, New York, back to England, back to Ireland, back to New York.

‌



Tyson Fury makes major Anthony Joshua fight announcement READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua closer to Tyson Fury fight deal after key demand met READ MORE :

"I've said yes every time with zero stipulations. The facts are, I feel like you're being a coward. I feel like you don't want to fight and you're just conning everybody. I feel like you've been doing that for years. You've had many opportunities to fight me, but deep down you never really wanted it. So let's see if you're going to man up the final time.

"Let's f***ing fight. It's a boxing match; you've been banjoed before plenty of times. You've been knocked spark out a few times, so what? What's the worst that can happen? I'm going to f***ing chin you, 100 per cent, but it's nothing that hasn't been done before!"

Article continues below

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn revealed earlier this week that one of Joshua's key demands - payment of his purse for his win over Kristian Prenga in July - had been met. "We're all good from the last fight, and we're all moving forward amicably," he said. "We don't want to do the fight in the US, but we also understand it has to work for everybody.

“We've been banging our head against the wall on that for the last two months. We've set out our position, mainly in concern to the tax situation that will deplete his net purse by going to America, which can be rectified. There's nothing unreasonable in there. If they want it in the US, they'll sign it. If not, we'll be very happy, and we'll do it in the UK.

"We are speaking multiple times a day but we are running out of time if they want to do the fight on November 20. We will need to make a decision this week."

Sports.title: Argentina villain Leandro Paredes hints at international retirement after 10-game ban
Sports.content:
Argentina villain Leandro Paredes hints at international retirement after 10-game ban

Leandro Paredes was hit with a 10-game ban following his vile behaviour after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain and he has suggested that he may never represent his country again

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has hinted he could retire from international duty (Image: Getty Images)

Argentina’s Leandro Paredes has hinted that he could retire from international duty after being slapped with a 10-match ban. The Boca Juniors midfielder sparked an ugly brawl after the South American nation’s World Cup final defeat by Spain.

He shoved Spain star Gavi to the floor and faced three FIFA assault charges. After an investigation, FIFA handed him a 10-match ban and Paredes has now suggested that he might have made his last appearance for his country due that suspension, as well as Lionel Messi’s decision to hang up his boots for Argentina.

‌



“It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,” Paredes said. “Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision... It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

‌



“I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
