Sports.title: Austin Williams Tests Vito Mielnicki’s Contender Claims
Sports.content:
Gardzielik was dropped and lost every round on all three scorecards. Nmomah offered limited resistance before being stopped in the ninth. Huerta went the distance but lost 100-90, 100-90, and 99-91. Those victories showed Mielnicki can dominate carefully selected opposition. They did not demonstrate that he is prepared for a championship fight.

Top Rank moved Mielnicki methodically by matching him against fighters with attractive records but little recognition in the United States. The approach helped him collect regional belts and climb the sanctioning-body rankings without facing anyone near the top of the middleweight class.

The more revealing performances came against Khalil El Harraz and Connor Coyle. Mielnicki edged El Harraz by majority decision and then struggled to a majority draw with Coyle. The New York State Athletic Commission later changed the Coyle result to a no-contest after he tested positive for performance-enhancing drugs, but the ruling did not erase what happened during those 10 rounds.

Mielnicki believes beating Williams would answer criticism of rankings that place him No. 3 with the WBO, No. 7 with the WBA and WBC, and No. 9 with the IBF.

“I feel like having a name like him on my resume will silence a lotta that,” Mielnicki told Keith Idec of The Ring.

Williams (20-2, 13 KOs) is a considerable upgrade. The physically strong southpaw applies pressure and can make Mielnicki fight while moving backward, an area that the trio was not equipped to test. Mielnicki must show that his footwork and inside game hold up when an opponent closes the distance and refuses to remain at his preferred pace.

Still, beating Williams would not establish Mielnicki as one of the best at 160. Hamzah Sheeraz stopped Williams, and Carlos Adames defeated him decisively over 12 rounds. Williams occupies the middle of the first tier: capable enough to expose a protected contender, but well below the elite.

That makes him an appropriate screening test. A Mielnicki loss in his New Jersey backyard would make his lofty rankings difficult to defend. A convincing win would earn him the opportunity to face the leading middleweights, not prove he is ready to beat them.

Sports.title: Hearn Disputes Kremlev’s Bivol-Beterbiev Trilogy Offer Claim
Sports.content:
“It was never offered, by the way,” said Hearn during a media scrum reported by ProBox TV . “If there was an offer that was even remotely reasonable, the Callum Smith fight wouldn’t be happening. Dmitry would have vacated and fought Beterbiev.”

That version is difficult to reconcile with Kremlev’s account. The IBA president said negotiations had taken place with both camps and that Bivol was offered twice his previous purse. Kremlev also claimed Beterbiev was willing to box without taking a purse to help complete the trilogy.

The dispute may come down to the difference between vocal backing and an actionable contract. A public promise of enormous money is not the same as written terms containing a date, venue, broadcaster, payment schedule, guarantees, and regulatory responsibilities.

Beterbiev’s reported willingness to compete for free demonstrates his desire for the fight, but it does not provide a workable economic structure. His purse was only one part of the proposed event. Someone still had to guarantee Bivol’s money and cover the considerable production and promotional costs.

Mandatory obligations have also dismantled the undisputed championship created by their first two fights. Bivol relinquished the WBC belt rather than defend against David Benavidez, then satisfied his IBF requirement. Facing Smith under the WBO order would place another challenger between Bivol and the trilogy.

Smith provides a useful common opponent. Beterbiev stopped him in seven rounds in January 2024, overpowering the former super middleweight champion with sustained pressure. A clear Bivol victory would invite comparisons, although their contrasting styles make a direct measurement unreliable. Beterbiev broke Smith physically; Bivol would be more likely to dismantle him through distance, timing, and combinations.

Delay carries a heavier price for Beterbiev. He has not fought since losing the rematch in February 2025, while Bivol returned against Michael Eifert and is preparing for Smith. At 41, Beterbiev cannot recover lost time through another training camp.

If the trilogy is postponed until 2027, Beterbiev may have spent nearly two years outside the ring. The eventual fight would still sell, but it might no longer settle the rivalry under conditions resembling their first two meetings. What began as a 50-50 conclusion risks becoming a test of how much age and inactivity have taken from Beterbiev.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Admits Early Success Cost Him Against Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
“I felt a bit too comfortable maybe with the really early knockdown, then followed by another one in the third,” Wardley said during the kick-off press conference. “I thought this is near on a foregone conclusion. I’ve done it once, I’ve done it twice, I can get him out of there. “I was a victim of my own success in them early stages. I just got trigger-happy, got carried away with trying to launch that right hand. In the moments when I did have him hurt, I don’t actually think I jumped on him enough.”

The mistake was not simply failing to throw enough punches. Wardley stopped disguising the right hand and began loading up from too far away. Dubois steadied himself behind a stiff jab, controlled the distance, and forced him to expend more energy each time he attempted to close the space.

The challenger needs greater variety in London. Hooks to the ribs would give Dubois something else to consider behind his tight guard, while doubling the lead hook may create a cleaner route for Wardley’s power. Hunting for one spectacular shot only makes his attack easier to read.

Pacing will be just as important. An early knockdown does not require an immediate all-out assault, particularly in a fight scheduled for 12 rounds. Wardley must allow his successes to count on the scorecards without emptying his energy reserves in search of a dramatic finish.

The five-month turnaround adds another concern. Wardley absorbed sustained punishment before the 11th-round stoppage and has gone directly into another demanding camp without an interim bout. He dismissed questions about his condition, saying he had “absolutely zero excuses” for the defeat or the rematch.

Dubois carries the psychological advantage. He knows he can withstand Wardley’s heaviest punches, regain command with his jab, and break him down over the later rounds. The harder mental test for Wardley may arrive if he lands cleanly again and the champion refuses to fold.

The first fight established that Wardley can hurt Dubois. On October 17, he must show that early success will sharpen his decisions instead of distorting them.

Sports.title: Janibek Corners Hamzah Sheeraz Before WBO Deadline
Sports.content:
Sheeraz has already built a possible defense for refusing the fight. During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show, he called the WBO’s ruling a “joke” and criticized the organization for rewarding Janibek after his positive test for meldonium.

The clean-sport objection has merit. The WBO shortened Janibek’s suspension, allowed him to move directly into a mandatory position at 168 pounds, and selected him over Jacob Bank despite Janibek never fighting in the division. Bank had actively campaigned at super middleweight and petitioned for the same opportunity.

Still, Sheeraz’s moral position also provides a convenient exit. He can vacate while claiming he refused to cooperate with a sanctioning body order he considers disgraceful, rather than admitting that Janibek presents too much danger for too little money.

Surrendering the title would harm Sheeraz’s reputation. He won the vacant belt against 39-year-old Alem Begic and struggled through a majority verdict over Simon Zachenhuber in his first defense. Leaving before facing Janibek would support the Kazakh’s claim that Sheeraz was only a “champion by name.”

Facing Janibek carries the greater career risk. He is a precise southpaw counterpuncher with the power to punish the defensive lapses Sheeraz showed against Zachenhuber. A decisive loss would cost Sheeraz his belt and reduce his value for larger fights against Canelo Alvarez or Chris Eubank Jr.

The history makes an escape harder to disguise. Sheeraz withdrew from negotiations when the WBO ordered him to challenge Janibek at middleweight. After Sheeraz moved to 168 and became champion, Janibek followed him into the division.

Vacating can be presented as a principled business choice. Getting stopped by the opponent who pursued him through two weight classes would be far worse. Janibek has left Sheeraz to choose which consequence he is willing to accept.

Sports.title: Two Minutes in Tokyo: George Foreman Slaughters José Roman
Sports.content:
Roman had little chance of testing him. The Puerto Rican challenger stood 5-foot-10 and weighed between 196½ and 197 pounds, leaving him considerably smaller than the 6-foot-4, 219-pound champion. He had been outside the rankings when the fight was signed before being elevated to No. 9 by the WBA and WBC.

That placement gave the promotion official legitimacy, but it did not make Roman a genuine threat. Foreman was 38-0 with 35 knockouts and had just destroyed Frazier in two rounds to seize the championship. Roman brought a 43-7-1 or 44-7-1 record, depending on the source, with 21 knockouts.

Once the bell rang, even two minutes proved too long.

Foreman did not merely follow Roman and swing wildly. Under trainer Dick Sadler, he had learned to take broad lateral steps that closed escape routes. His lead hand served as more than a jab. He posted it against Roman, pushed him off balance, and turned him toward the right hand.

That rough leverage helped Foreman control opponents before the power punches landed. Some of it crossed into boxing’s gray area, particularly when he shoved or extended his lead arm, but Roman lacked the strength and composure to resist it.

The destruction of Frazier also followed Foreman into the ring. Roman knew that six knockdowns had reduced the previous champion to a helpless target. His tense movement and reluctance to commit gave Foreman little reason to respect anything coming back.

Foreman cut down the available space, drove Roman toward the ropes, and attacked his body. Roman fell along the ropes near the one-minute point, but referee Jay Edson initially treated it as a slip or loss of balance rather than a knockdown.

The decision became controversial when Foreman landed a right while Roman was sitting on the canvas. Roman’s manager, Bill Daly, and trainer, Al Braverman, jumped onto the apron demanding a disqualification. Edson ruled that Foreman had been following through and that the punch carried little force. Because the original fall was ruled a slip, Roman received neither a mandatory count nor additional recovery time.

The challenger rose, only to be dropped by a right hand. Roman made it up once more, but Foreman finished him with a right uppercut at exactly 2:00 of the opening round. Roman’s corner later called Foreman “the dirtiest fighter in the world,” while some members of the Tokyo crowd booed the abrupt ending.

Roman’s ranking exposed the business behind the defense. He was outside the WBA and WBC ratings when the fight was arranged, then elevated to No. 9 so the organizations could approve him as a challenger. The placement did not make him a mandatory contender or establish championship credentials. It allowed an overseas title defense to proceed against an opponent selected for limited risk.

Promoters advertised Foreman’s purse as $1 million, a figure that became attached to the fight in later records. Contemporary reporting placed his actual guarantee near $250,000, while other accounts and Foreman’s later recollections put his earnings in the $250,000 to $300,000 range. Roman received approximately $100,000.

Attendance reached roughly 7,500 to 8,000 in an arena capable of holding nearly twice that number. The midday Saturday scheduling and expensive tickets hurt local sales, leaving Japanese promoters braced for a financial loss despite televising the bout free to domestic viewers.

Foreman followed the Roman destruction by stopping Ken Norton in two rounds the next year. Across the Frazier, Roman, and Norton fights, he needed only five rounds to dispose of three heavyweights who had a combined 91 professional victories.

The two-minute result also concealed a flaw that Muhammad Ali later exploited. Foreman committed heavily to his power punches and expected resistance to collapse under the first sustained attack. Roman rewarded that approach by folding almost immediately.

Ali refused to provide the same response in Zaire the following year. He forced Foreman to keep punching after the quick finish failed to materialize, turning the champion’s aggression and confidence in his strength into an exhausting trap.

Foreman’s comeback decades later produced one of boxing’s greatest stories, capped by the heavyweight championship at age 45. Yet the older Foreman relied more on patience, positioning, and conservation. The 1973 version brought something more frightening: youth, crushing strength, and an appetite for immediate destruction.

Roman was never equipped to disprove it.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Says Crawford Resents His Boxing Takeover
Sports.content:
“I gave my honest opinion, saying that he left a lot on the table. That’s all I said. Crawford is the one that’s always coming up and slightly hating on me little by little. In the meantime, you’re retired. You should be in Turks and Caicos chilling on a yacht, enjoying your family. He’s desperate, bro,” said Ryan to Fight Hub TV. “Nobody knows him outside of boxing, so he’s doing everything he can to continue his name. He actually likes the attention. I used to think Crawford didn’t, but now I know he does. He realized nobody cares after you retire.”

Ryan also dismissed Crawford’s presence at Benn’s gym. “I feel like I’ll beat your ass, so what are you going to teach him?” he said.

Their bad blood highlights the fundamental difference between the two men. Crawford pursued championships, pound-for-pound recognition, and technical supremacy. Garcia measures his position through audience size, financial leverage, and the ability to command boxing’s most valuable dates.

Crawford built the greater traditional legacy, but Ryan attracts the larger mainstream audience. If Garcia defeats Benn and becomes boxing’s leading commercial figure, he will have achieved something Crawford never managed despite accomplishing far more inside the ring.

Working with Benn does not necessarily prove Garcia’s accusation that Crawford craves attention. It may represent a retired fighter transferring his knowledge to another contender. Garcia has turned that mentorship into an insult, reducing Benn to a pupil who cannot be saved even by one of boxing’s finest technicians.

That approach also keeps Benn’s abilities outside the discussion. By treating the fight as a proxy battle with Crawford, Garcia portrays him as little more than the vehicle for another man’s resentment.

The claim brings considerable risk. Garcia’s argument carries force only if he beats Benn. A loss would damage his attempt to place drawing power above championships while giving Crawford every reason to question both his boxing and his self-appointed status.

The message was simple: Crawford had his run and should either return to face someone such as Jaron Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr. or stay quiet in retirement.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Faces Duty as Oleksandr Usyk Exits
Sports.content:
The champion would naturally prefer a larger fight. Revenge against Dubois carries commercial value after Hrgovic’s stoppage loss to him in 2024, while a unification would pay considerably more than defending against Sanchez. The IBF mandate leaves little room for shopping around unless Sanchez accepts another step-aside agreement.

Dubois first has his own business to settle. He defends the WBO title against Fabio Wardley in their October 17 rematch at London’s O2 Arena. Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round of their May meeting, but the punishment he absorbed makes the return dangerous. Hrgovic cannot build his plans around Dubois retaining.

Oleksandr Usyk is operating outside that championship traffic. The former unified champion is targeting Deontay Wilder for a final fight in the United States in 2027. It offers Usyk one more famous name, but little clarity about the division’s best heavyweight.

Usyk struggled more than anticipated against boxing novice Rico Verhoeven in May. He trailed on one scorecard and was level on the other two before producing an 11th-round stoppage. Wilder also carries the wear of a long career and no longer releases his right hand with the conviction that once made him boxing’s most feared puncher. Their proposed fight sells history and name recognition rather than determining the division’s leader.

The active championship race now belongs to Hrgovic, Dubois, WBA champion Murat Gassiev, and WBC interim champion Agit Kabayel. Gassiev stopped Peter Kadiru in six rounds in July, while Kabayel demolished Damian Knyba in three rounds in January. A Gassiev-Kabayel unification would immediately reduce the number of competing titleholders.

Hrgovic wants access to those lucrative fights, but Sanchez remains positioned directly in front of him. Beating Itauma won Hrgovic the belt. Defeating his mandatory would prove that he can keep it.

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Waits for the Winner of Canelo-Mbilli
Sports.content:
Martinez was much more effective and landed the harder punches. Lester had the support of the Guatemalan people with a healthy attendance of 6,848 at the USC Galen Center. The interim WBC super middleweight champion is the only boxing champion of any kind for Guatemala; Martinez is held in high esteem, receiving the full support of his country. After the victory, he celebrated at Lafayette Park at the Festival Chapin with his fellow countrymen.

ProBox promoter Garry Jonas stated at the post-fight press conference they’re exploring the options of holding a Lester Martinez fight at a soccer stadium somewhere in Guatemala, hopefully for January of 2027. The energy and crowd at the Galen Center was electrifying as the crowd would erupt in cheers every time Lester would land a big punch.

Holding an event in Guatemala would definitely draw a crowd. Lester is becoming a bigger star with every fight, and if he’s able to secure a fight with the winner of the Canelo Alvarez-Christian Mbilli fight, he would only become that much bigger. Trainer Esau Dieguez said of the fight, “The truth is we would like to face the winner, but because of name recognition and what it would bring, we would like to fight Canelo. Being that we already fought Mbilli, but I expect Canelo to win. I think Canelo will win, I hope we can make the fight. I know the WBC may beat around the bush, but our hope is Lester will fight for the full world title.”

It was the fight against Mbilli that raised Lester’s profile and introduced him to the world. Although it was ruled a draw, there are many who believe Martinez should have been awarded the decision. Lester stood toe-to-toe with the power puncher, exchanging punch for punch with him. Martinez outlanded Mbilli 412 to 273 in total punches, outlanding him in 9 of 12 rounds (Compubox).

He tried securing the rematch with Christian, but the fight never materialized. Expecting a tough fight against the Canelo-Mbilli winner, Lester said, “I think for now I will relax, but I know what is coming will be more difficult, and we will prepare for it.”

Knowing that he will have to perform at his absolute best against whomever the winner may be. Lester has proven he has the skills to compete at the championship level, and he has the full support of an entire country with him in Guatemala; they want nothing more than to have their first full world champion.

Ghana News.title: BOSTenergies reports strong 2025 performance, pays first-ever dividend to government
Ghana News.content:
BOST Energies Limited Company (BOSTenergies) has reported strong financial and operational growth for the 2025 financial year, recording significant increases in revenue, profitability, assets and shareholder equity, while achieving a historic milestone with the payment of its first-ever dividend to the Government of Ghana.

The performance was announced at the Company's 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM) held today in Accra, where the shareholder, the Board of Directors, Management and other stakeholders reviewed the Company's performance for the 2025 financial year.

Strong Financial Performance

The 2025 financial year marked a defining period in BOSTenergies' transformation, with the Company recording substantial growth across key financial indicators.

The Company recorded:

GH¢3.81 billion in revenue, representing a 195% year-on-year growth;

GH¢683.96 million in Profit After Tax, reflecting a 72% year-on-year increase;

GH¢3.99 billion in total assets, representing 50% growth;

GH¢1.47 billion in shareholder equity, more than doubling over the period; and

A 28% reduction in administrative expenses, demonstrating the Company's continued focus on cost discipline and operational efficiency.

A major highlight of the year was the payment of BOSTenergies' first-ever dividend to the Government of Ghana since the Company's establishment 32 years ago.

The Company paid 5% of its net profit as dividend, amounting to GH¢34.2 million, marking a significant milestone in BOSTenergies' journey towards delivering greater value to Government.

The dividend payment reflects the Company's improved financial position and reinforces its commitment to prudent financial management, accountability and sustainable shareholder value creation.

Building Stronger and More Resilient BOSTenergies

The 2025 results were driven by the strength of the Company's commercial activities, disciplined financial management and continued focus on operational efficiency.

Beyond the financial results, the performance demonstrated the emergence of stronger and more resilient BOSTenergies, supported by a solid financial foundation to drive continued investment, operational excellence and sustainable growth.

Commenting on the performance, Managing Director of BOSTenergies, Mr Afetsi Awoonor, said:

“2025 was a defining year for BOSTenergies. We delivered strong financial growth, strengthened our balance sheet and achieved the significant milestone of declaring our first-ever dividend to the Government of Ghana. These achievements demonstrate what is possible when we combine commercial discipline, prudent financial management and operational efficiency.

Positioning BOSTenergies for the Future

Looking ahead, BOSTenergies will remain focused on strengthening its operations, driving efficiency, building resilience and creating lasting value for its shareholder and stakeholders.

The Company will continue to leverage its strategic infrastructure, commercial capabilities and evolving energy portfolio to support Ghana's energy security, while positioning itself to respond effectively to the changing energy landscape.

Mr Awoonor reaffirmed the Company's commitment to sustainable growth and its critical role in Ghana's downstream energy sector.

“As we look ahead, our focus remains clear: strengthening our operations, driving efficiency, building resilience and creating lasting value. We will continue to play our part in ensuring Ghana's energy security while positioning BOSTenergies for sustainable growth and long-term relevance.”

On his part, the Minister of Energy and Green Transition, Hon. Dr John Abdulai Jinpor praised the Board, Management and staff of BOSTenergies for delivering a masterclass performance in their financial growth and profitability, operational efficiency and portfolio growth of almost threefold. The Minister pledged his unflinching support to the Board and management and charged them to remain steadfast and build on the achievements attained.

The Director General of SIGA, Prof Michael Kpesah Whyte, welcomed the positive turnaround at BOSTenergies including its first dividend payment in its history and urged the Board and Management to remain on track to achieve bigger growth and deliver value to government.

The 2026 Annual General Meeting therefore marked an important milestone in BOSTenergies' journey, providing an opportunity to reflect on a year of strong performance while reaffirming the Company's commitment to financial sustainability, operational excellence, shareholder value and Ghana's energy security.

Ghana News.title: Carlos Queiroz reappointed as Black Stars head coach
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has reached an agreement with Carlos Queiroz for the Portuguese coach to continue as head coach of the Black Stars.

The announcement comes a few weeks after Queiroz’s previous mandate, which included leading Ghana at the just-concluded FIFA World Cup, came to an end.

According to the GFA, discussions between the coach, the Association and the Ministry of Sports and Recreation resulted in an agreement for Queiroz to take up a new coaching mandate.

His new tenure will commence with the upcoming international window.

The GFA said Queiroz’s extensive international experience, technical expertise and knowledge of the Black Stars made him the preferred choice to lead the team into the next phase of its programme.

“The GFA believes Queiroz’s extensive international experience, technical expertise and knowledge of the Black Stars position him strongly to lead the team into this next chapter,” the Association said in a statement on Wednesday, September 2.

The football governing body did not disclose the duration or specific terms of the new mandate.

It said further details about Queiroz’s new assignment and the Black Stars’ upcoming programme would be announced in due course.

The coach will now turn his attention to preparing the team for its next international engagements as the GFA seeks to build what it described as a successful new phase for Ghana on the international stage.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t targets TVET transformation with US$300m World Bank facility
Ghana News.content:
The government has secured a US$300 million World Bank facility to support the transformation of Ghana’s secondary education and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector.

The funding, secured under the Secondary Education Transformation for Access, Relevant and Results for Jobs (STAR-J) Project, is expected to expand secondary education and TVET infrastructure, improve the quality and relevance of training, and support efforts to end the double-track system by 2027.

Speaking on behalf of the Minister of Education at a TVET stakeholders’ engagement dialogue, Technical Advisor to the Minister, Prof. George K.T. Oduro, said the government is also providing US$31 million in counterpart funding, bringing the total investment under the programme to US$331 million.

“STAR-J will expand secondary education and TVET infrastructure, improve quality, strengthen relevance and support the government’s efforts to end the double-track system by 2027.”

The engagement, held under the theme, “Partnership for TVET Transformation: The Role of Industry in Workforce Development in Ghana,” brought together government, industry and other stakeholders to deliberate on ways to align technical and vocational training with the needs of the economy.

Director-General of the Ghana TVET Service, Engr. Dr. Eric Kofi Adzroe, said the government is working to bridge the gap between the skills produced locally and those required in more advanced economies.

He said Ghana must strengthen its systems while learning from countries that have successfully developed their TVET sectors.

“Let’s just take it slowly. Let’s learn lessons from the developed world—how they are doing it, what they have done so far.”

He also disclosed that the government is establishing a TVET Fund to help address gaps in equipment and infrastructure and strengthen the connection between training institutions and industry.

Meanwhile, Chairman of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Dr. Nii Moi Thompson, called for greater use of digital platforms to create employment opportunities for Ghana’s youth.

He cited data showing that Ghana ranks poorly in the use of ICT for business and work, with only 28.5 percent of the population using ICT for such purposes.

According to him, while the figures highlight challenges in digital productivity, they also point to opportunities that policymakers can leverage to create jobs and develop relevant skills.

“These are both bad and good statistics. Bad because they show that we spend way too much time on non-productive social media activities, but they are good because they point us to areas of potential growth that must attract the attention of policymakers.”

Dr. Thompson further expressed concern over the growing desire among young Ghanaians to seek opportunities abroad.

He cited a recent Afrobarometer survey indicating that 72 per cent of Ghanaian youth want to immigrate, with more than half citing the search for jobs as a major reason.

“We can no longer just grow our economy. Therefore, we must grow hope, and growing hope means creating employment opportunities.”

He urged policymakers to create opportunities that will give young people a reason to remain in Ghana and contribute to the country’s development.

The Ghana TVET Service says it is also placing greater emphasis on soft skills, attitudes and work ethics as part of efforts to make TVET graduates more employable and responsive to industry needs.

The Service says stronger collaboration with industry will be critical to ensuring that training programmes reflect the changing demands of the labour market and equip young people with the practical skills needed to secure sustainable employment.

Ghana News.title: Flying into Ghana with more than 2 phones may face commercial import charges – GRA
Ghana News.content:
The Commissioner of the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), Aaron Kanors, has cautioned travellers arriving in Ghana against carrying multiple mobile phones on behalf of other people, warning that excessive quantities could be treated as commercial imports.

He said individuals travelling into the country are expected to carry only a limited number of phones for personal use, while bringing in several devices could attract customs treatment as commercial goods.

“Travelers should not bring more than two phones into the country; anything beyond that will be considered commercial importation at the Airport” - GRA Customs Commissioner Aaron Kanor#UTVGhana pic.twitter.com/Eu1SAdZIKt — UTV Ghana (@utvghana) September 2, 2026

“When you carry all those 7 phones, and you arrive, it will amount to commercial. Because as an individual, you are entitled to one.

So we implore that when you are coming home, you do not collect people's things. If you collect them and they are beyond two… one individual, you can only carry two. One for yourself and maybe one for your wife. Beyond that, it amounts to commercial. "

Mr Kanors said the practice of travellers carrying several phones belonging to other people could result in the items being considered commercial quantities.

He explained that the high value of smartphones, particularly premium brands such as Apple’s iPhone and Samsung devices, makes them an important source of customs revenue.

"Because all these phones are expensive. Look at iPhone, Samsung, they are very expensive phones. And that is where we can get our revenue.”

The GRA is therefore urging Ghanaians returning home to be mindful of the number of phones and other goods they carry into the country on behalf of others to avoid potential customs liabilities.

Ghana News.title: Education Ministry warns private schools against use of unapproved textbooks
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Education has warned private schools against compelling parents to purchase unapproved textbooks, describing the practice as an exploitation of families for commercial gain.

The warning comes as the Ministry, through the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA), undertakes a comprehensive review of the Basic School Curriculum from Kindergarten One (KG1) to Primary Six.

Press Secretary and Spokesperson for the Ministry of Education, Hasmin Mohammed, said the curriculum review process was still ongoing and that the revised curriculum had not yet been approved for implementation.

He stressed that until the process is completed, both public and private schools are required to continue using the existing approved curriculum and NaCCA-approved textbooks.

“The Ministry of Education, through the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA), is undertaking a comprehensive revision of the Basic School Curriculum from KG1 to Primary 6. That process is ongoing. The revised curriculum has not yet been approved for implementation,” he said.

According to him, the government will procure the necessary textbooks and Teaching and Learning Materials (TLMs) to support the implementation of the revised curriculum when it receives approval.

However, Mr Mohammed expressed concern about what he described as an emerging practice in some private schools, where parents are allegedly being pressured to buy textbooks developed by individual writers or in collaboration with schools without approval from NaCCA.

He said some of the materials were being sold at exorbitant prices, placing unnecessary financial burdens on parents.

“Education must not become a marketplace for exploiting parents,” he stated.

The Ministry's spokesperson called on parents and Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) to speak up against proprietors of private schools who impose unapproved learning materials on families for their commercial interests.

He noted that NaCCA had been empowered by Parliament to enforce compliance and sanction schools found to be using textbooks that had not received approval from the Council.

“NaCCA has been empowered by Parliament to enforce compliance and take action against schools using unapproved textbooks. The Council is already in the field monitoring schools and will sanction institutions found to be in breach of the law,” Mr Mohammed said.

He urged the public to support efforts by the government and NaCCA to ensure that private schools comply with approved textbook requirements.

Mr Mohammed maintained that parents should not be made to pay high prices for textbooks that have not been approved by NaCCA, alleging that some school proprietors were bypassing approved materials in pursuit of commercial interests.

He said the Ministry would continue working to protect parents from exploitation while ensuring that schools use learning materials that meet the required national standards.

Ghana News.title: Travelers with multiple new devices returning to Ghana to pay additional charges – Customs Commissioner
Ghana News.content:
Travelers returning to Ghana with multiple new devices including mobile phones and other electronic gadgets may be compelled to pay commercial duties on such products at the airport during arrival processes.

Briefing journalists after a tour of the Airport, Commissioner of Customs at the Ghana Revenue Authority, Aaron Kanor, said more than two mobile devices could amount to commercial use.

The Commissioner also disclosed plans to fully automate passenger profiling at the country’s airports during arrivals.

He noted that this is part of international customs as such items are required to be declared by the owners.

“In Ghana, because of our culture, when one is traveling, Amma gives you one phone, Kofi gives you another and all the days born phones, they all give you phones. When you carry all those seven phones and you arrive, it will amount to what? Commercial.

“This is because as an individual, you are entitled to one or maybe two, considering that the other is for your wife”.

“So, we implore that when you are coming home, you do not collect people's things. If you collect them and they are beyond two, one is allowed to carry two”, he added.

“One for yourself and maybe one for your wife. Beyond that, it amounts to commercial because all these phones are expensive”, he mentioned.

Furthermore, he said, “If you look at iPhone, Samsung, they are very expensive. That is where we can get our revenue”.

Meanwhile, the Customs Division of the GRA is in the process to fully automate passenger profiling at the country’s airports during arrivals.

This is part of the transformation of the GRA and to help curb delays at the ports as a result of customs physical checks.

Ghana News.title: John Boadu: A lifetime of party service, experience and grassroots leadership
Ghana News.content:
For decades, John Boadu has occupied some of the most important organisational positions within Ghana’s New Patriotic Party (NPP), building a political career that has taken him from the grassroots to the highest levels of the party’s national structure.

His journey is one marked not only by positions held, but also by the experiences gathered along the way experiences that have exposed him to electoral victories, political setbacks, internal party challenges and the continuous task of keeping a large political organisation together.

As the NPP considers its future leadership, Boadu’s record places him among the experienced figures whose understanding of the party’s organisational structure is difficult to overlook.

His political experience stretches across several layers of the party. He has served as Youth Organiser, National Organiser, Acting General Secretary and General Secretary, among other responsibilities. These positions have given him exposure to the practical workings of the party, from grassroots mobilisation and polling-station structures to constituency, regional and national administration.

For a political organisation whose electoral fortunes depend heavily on the effectiveness of its grassroots structures, such experience can be significant.

Boadu’s years in party organisation have also brought him into contact with polling-station executives, constituency leaders, regional executives, national officers, party activists and government officials during periods when the NPP has been in power.

That broad network of relationships is an important part of his political profile.

Politics, however, is not simply about occupying an office. It is also about relationships, communication and the ability to work with people who may not always share the same opinions.

Throughout his political career, Boadu has operated within an environment where disagreements, competing ambitions and differing interpretations of the party’s direction are inevitable. His experience therefore includes navigating the human side of political organisation, engaging individuals and groups across different levels of the party.

That experience has been particularly relevant to his interactions with the grassroots.

The polling station executive remains one of the most important actors in Ghanaian electoral politics. It is at the polling-station level that national political strategies are ultimately translated into votes. Candidates may make speeches at national rallies, but the actual work of mobilising voters, monitoring polling stations and maintaining contact with communities is largely carried out by people at the grassroots.

Boadu’s long association with party organisation has therefore provided him with considerable familiarity with this structure.

His relationship with the youth is another feature of his political profile.

Having served as a Youth Organiser, Boadu has had direct experience working with younger party members and understanding their role in political mobilisation. The youth constitute a significant component of every political organisation, but they also represent one of the groups most interested in questions of employment, economic opportunity, political participation and leadership succession.

His experience has consequently placed him in a position to understand the importance of bringing young people into the party’s organisational and decision-making processes rather than treating them merely as campaign foot soldiers.

Perhaps one of the most significant aspects of Boadu’s political journey is that it has not been confined to one particular phase of the NPP’s history.

He has experienced the party in opposition and has also participated in periods when the NPP controlled government. He has therefore witnessed the contrasting demands that come with political power and opposition.

When a party is in government, expectations from its supporters and grassroots members can be enormous. Constituency and polling-station activists expect communication, recognition and responsiveness, while government officials must simultaneously deal with the responsibilities of governance.

In opposition, the priorities change. Organisation, unity, mobilisation and rebuilding become particularly important.

Boadu’s experience across these different political environments has contributed to his understanding of the relationship between the party organisation and government.

Yet his record should also be viewed within the broader history of the NPP. Like every senior political figure, his career has been associated with both achievements and difficult moments. The party has enjoyed major electoral victories during periods in which he held senior organisational responsibilities, but it has also suffered electoral defeats.

Those contrasting experiences can provide valuable lessons.

Victory can create confidence, while defeat can expose organisational weaknesses that may otherwise remain hidden. A leader who has experienced both is inevitably confronted with questions about what worked, what failed and what must change.

As the NPP looks toward the future, these questions are particularly important.

The challenge before the party is not simply to select individuals for positions. It is to determine what kind of organisational leadership is required to strengthen its structures, rebuild confidence, improve communication and reconnect effectively with members at every level.

That conversation inevitably brings attention to individuals with long institutional experience.

John Boadu’s political profile is therefore rooted in several decades of party service, organisational responsibility and relationships across the NPP’s structures.

His experience from the youth wing to national administration, from grassroots mobilisation to senior party leadership, gives him an understanding of the organisation that has been developed over many years.

Ultimately, the assessment of any candidate for national party leadership must go beyond slogans and promises. It requires consideration of experience, organisational competence, temperament, relationships, understanding of the grassroots and the ability to work with different constituencies within the party.

For John Boadu, the record provides a substantial basis for that assessment.

His political journey represents a long chapter in the organisational history of the NPP, a journey shaped by service, responsibility, electoral campaigns, leadership challenges, relationships and lessons from both success and defeat.

As the party debates its next chapter, that experience will remain an important part of the conversation about the leadership and direction of the NPP.

Ghana News.title: Ghana to host 16th African Economic Summit as Friends of Africa brings Global Investment Dialogue to Accra
Ghana News.content:
From boardrooms to start-up pitches, Ghana is preparing to become the meeting point for investors, governments, entrepreneurs and businesses from Africa and North America as the Friends of Africa Economic Summit makes its Ghanaian debut with an ambitious mission: “Turning partnerships and ideas into sustainable investment opportunities.”

Ghana is set to host the 16th African Economic Summit, marking a major milestone in the Friends of Africa (FOA) initiative as the organisation brings 15 years of experience hosting economic

summits in North America to the African continent.

The two-day Friends of Africa Economic Summit 2026 is scheduled for September 17–18, 2026, at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City in Accra, under the theme, “Building Sustainable Futures: Scaling Investment Partnerships in Ghana.”

The summit is expected to bring together business leaders, government representatives, investors, entrepreneurs, founders and professionals for discussions and networking focused on strengthening investment partnerships and creating practical opportunities for economic growth.

According to the organisers, the Ghana edition represents an effort to share the experience gained from 15 years of hosting the African Economic Summit in North America with African counterparts, beginning with Ghana.

The programme will begin with informal Friends of Africa sessions from September 16–17, including one-on-one meetings with founders. A private reception for speakers and sponsors is also scheduled for September 17.

The main programme on September 18 will feature a full-day combination of business, government and investment discussions, including plenary sessions, expert panels, fireside conversations, government-to-government and business-to-business meetings, exhibitions and networking opportunities.

One of the major attractions will be a start-up pitch competition featuring 40 start-ups presenting their value propositions before investors and funding groups in the hope of competing for seed capital.

The organisers say the summit will also provide a marketplace where selected Canadian companies seeking partnerships in Ghana can connect with professionals and businesses.

The discussions are expected to focus on critical areas including funding, partnerships and infrastructure development opportunities, while also providing opportunities for knowledge sharing and business-to-business engagement.

Beyond the formal business sessions, the summit will showcase Ghanaian food, music and entrepreneurial talent, adding a cultural dimension to the economic and investment discussions.

Friends of Africa is also inviting organisations to participate as sponsors, offering several sponsorship categories ranging from US$3,000 for FOA Supporters to US$20,000 for Platinum Sponsors.

The Platinum package includes prominent branding, speaking opportunities, VIP access, marketplace tables, advertising in the FOA Magazine, social media promotion and recognition in the summit's impact report.

Gold Sponsors, at US$10,000, will receive branding opportunities around the pitch competition and opportunities to engage with seed-capital winners, while Silver and Bronze sponsors will receive varying levels of visibility, speaking, networking and marketplace opportunities.

The organisation said sponsorship support would help strengthen the FOA platform and facilitate the summit's broader objectives of connecting businesses, investors and governments.

The summit is being led in Ghana by Prof. Odoi Yemoh, Chair of the African Economic Summit Committee, Ghana 2026, alongside Nardos Sebro, Executive Lead for Partnerships and Sponsors at Friends of Africa-Global.

With Ghana increasingly seeking to position itself as a destination for investment, entrepreneurship and international business partnerships, the summit could provide an important platform for turning conversations into concrete commercial relationships.

At its core, however, the Friends of Africa Economic Summit is presenting a broader proposition: Africa's economic future will require partnerships that move beyond dialogue and translate ideas, capital and innovation into sustainable opportunities.

Organizations interested in participating or sponsoring the summit are encouraged to register early and join this important global conversation on building stronger investment partnerships and expanding opportunities for African businesses to contact Friends of Africa-Global through foaglobal@friendsofafrica.ca or visit the Ghanaian-Canadian Chamber of Commerce for registration and further information.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: The long-term implications of Pete Hegseth’s US military purges
World.content:
Earlier this week, Daniel Driscoll, the secretary of the United States Army, resigned from his post after he reportedly tried to directly appeal to US President Donald Trump about how changes in the military’s leadership were having an impact on the institution’s readiness for war.

Driscoll, a law school colleague of US Vice President JD Vance, was appointed last February to his position, the highest civilian role in the Army below the secretary of defense, Pete Hegseth. He was particularly involved, experts say, in planning how to transform the Army so it could take part in modern wars that seemed to increasingly rely less on ground forces and more on assets like drones and missiles.

His resignation is the latest in a list of top officials who have been fired or asked to resign under Hegseth, including three- and four-star generals and members of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, a group of top-ranking military officers who meet to directly advise the US president. Among them have been Black and female leaders, demographics the Trump administration has said were unfairly promoted in recent times because of “diversity, equity, and inclusion” initiatives he is now seeking to undo.

Technically, officials like Driscoll serve at the pleasure of the president, said Kelly Grieco, senior fellow at the Stimson Center think tank. So Hegseth, having been appointed by Trump, has the power to remove them. But for civilian leaders, as well as the rest of the military who are not told exactly why these personnel changes happen, “the sheer number of firings, and promotions that have been blocked, raises the question of whether there is a hollowing out of the senior levels of the military.”



Ending ‘wokeness’

Hegseth was an infantry officer in the Army National Guard who went on to become a television personality on the conservative US news channel Fox News before being tapped for the military portfolio in Trump’s cabinet. Hegseth had been particularly outspoken about modern changes in the military that he claimed had weakened it, including policies that led to the inclusion and promotion of women and LGBTQ personnel. These are other minority groups, Hegseth has said, have been promoted in the military based on their demographics and not based on their performance, as they should have been judged.

“Hegseth came into the Pentagon with a specific set of priorities,” said Jennifer Kavanagh, a senior fellow at Defense Priorities, “including a focus on increasing what he calls ‘lethality’ and getting rid of what he calls ‘woke’ ideology, which he and Trump think are running rampant through the Pentagon.”

Under Hegseth, the Trump administration began using the “Department of War” instead of the “Department of Defense”, and the military has toned down, and in some cases erased, memorials and other public acknowledgments of minorities and women who were pioneers in the institution. Earlier this year, Hegseth announced the military would start annual testosterone screening for its soldiers who are aged 30 and over, as part of an initiative to ensure they “have the biological foundation required to sustain the fight”.

Fired, or forced to retire early

The result, experts say, has been the unravelling of a merit-based system of promotions that defines a military with about a trillion-dollar budget and more than 1.3 million active duty personnel.

“It is far past time for President Trump to recognize the lasting harm that Pete Hegseth is inflicting on the Department of Defense,” Senator Jack Reed, a former Army officer himself, said in a statement in response to news of Driscoll’s resignation this week. “Secretary Hegseth is cultivating a culture where dissent is punished and competence is secondary to personal allegiance.”

Members of the Joint Chiefs of Staff who have represented the Army, Navy, and Air Force have all been fired, resigned, or replaced under Hegseth.

General Charles Q Brown, Jr., a Black fighter pilot who served as the Air Force’s chief of staff and later became the chairman of the Joint Chiefs, was fired last February and replaced with a white man. Admiral Lisa Franchetti, a white woman who also served on the Joint Chiefs of Staff as chief of naval operations, was also fired that month, replaced by a white man. General Randy A George, chief of staff of the Army, was fired in April of this year. General David Allvin, the Air Force chief of staff, retired early last year.



Hegseth has also removed or forced out top civilians working under him. Navy Secretary John Phelan resigned in April, and Driscoll’s last day was Wednesday.

Heads of intelligence services too have left. Lieutenant-General Jeffrey Kruse, head of the Defense Intelligence Agency, was fired last year after his agency reported US air strikes on Iran’s nuclear facilities had not been effective.

Other high-ranking personnel who have left under Hegseth include: General Chris Donahue, US Army commander Europe and Africa; General David Hodne, US Army commander of transformation and training command; General James Mingus, US Army vice chief of staff; Lieutenant-General Joseph McGee, director for strategy, plans and policy at the Joint Chiefs of Staff; Vice Admiral Shoshana Chatfield, US Navy representative to NATO; Rear Admiral Milton Sands, commander of Naval Special Warfare Command.

The sidelining of top-ranking women and minorities, experts say, will make others below them question whether they should be devoting decades more of their lives to an institution that could get rid of them because of their identity.

“If you’re in the military and you’re watching these changes, even if you’re not at the senior levels, you would have to be wondering what message it is sending to the rank and file?” Grieco said.

Overruling advice

There are pressing operational consequences, as well, for all this churn at the Pentagon, experts say.

There are longer-term strategic considerations of losing leadership, said Kavanagh.

The war in Iran has shown how crucial fleets of drones and missiles will be in any future conflict, she said, and top leaders like Driscoll understood the need to pivot their forces in a new direction, a task that becomes much more difficult if the person in charge of this kind of long-term thinking is constantly being swapped out with someone else.

“This is what the chiefs of staff, the secretaries of services, are supposed to do,” Kavanagh said. “They are not dealing with operational warfighting; they are not dealing with what’s going on in Iran every day, for example. They are dealing with big-picture issues of force modernisation, and every time there’s a new leader, they might come in with a new vision.”
