He said in the meantime there were signs that building and construction were starting to recover, and that should result in more apprenticeships and workplace training.

The Manufacturing and Engineering Industry Skills Board said manufacturing companies were intending to increase apprentice numbers.

"Apprenticeship numbers have generally been subdued for a few years now, as we've come down off a post-Covid high, and business confidence has been hit by the extended war in the Gulf," it said.

"However, our manufacturing and engineering industries have seen continuing signs of recovery and growth over the past year, and many companies now face skills shortages and are consequently looking to take on more apprentices."

World.title: 'We've lost half our deposit': About 4000 first-home buyers owe more than their homes worth
World.content:
Is there any point in KiwiSaver if I'm on a total remuneration package? No Stupid Questions with Susan Edmunds Download MP3 10m

Rising interest rates are not welcome news for most borrowers, but they hit especially hard for those who are paying off a home loan on a house that is now worth less than they paid for it.

Cotality chief economist Kelvin Davidson said, assuming all first-home buyers had a 20 percent deposit at the time they purchased, there were still about 3600 households nationwide who now owed more than the value of their homes.

Most would be people who had bought during the peak of the market, in late 2021 and early 2022. Prices are still down about 17 percent since that point, and more than 20 percent in Auckland and Wellington. Some parts of the country, such as Canterbury and Otago, have since returned to the prior peaks.

The true number in negative equity is likely to be higher than 3600 because many bought with a deposit much smaller than 20 percent. Cotality said about 29,000 first-home buyers bought properties during the 18-month peak of the market and a large proportion of them would now still be worth less than they paid.

Money correspondent Susan Edmunds on interest rate rise Morning Report Download MP3 2m

Some recent buyers have posted anonymously on social media in recent weeks, sharing the human implications of the downturn.

One said they were separating from a partner and worried that their townhouse would not sell because next door was vacant and had not sold. "Our CV is down by $100,000 from our purchase price. Either way we will be in debt with mortgage repayments even if the house sells."

Another who said they had bought a house in 2023 had seen their house value drop $80,000, even though they missed the peak.

"When you add the $35,000 agent fee to sell, we've lost half our deposit."

Another said they had been left jealous of renters. "I bought at the peak in 2021 and the house has dropped at least $200,000 easily. It's taken years to accept this is one financial mistake I've made which won't kill me but still hurts."

Some buyers talked about being stuck in townhouses and apartments longer than they intended to, because they had listened to advice that they did not need to buy a "forever home" first up.

Cotality chief economist Kelvin Davidson. SUPPLIED

Davidson his data assumed that they had not paid off much of the mortgage yet, which would be normal for a new borrower with a table loan. A large part of early repayments is interest and only a small amount goes to principal.

"It can't be great for the mindset to be in negative equity, but it's not necessarily a huge problem if people keep servicing the debt, which the majority are, there are hardly any non-performing loans at present. The bank won't come knocking solely because of negative equity."

[audio[ https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/morningreport/audio/2019050280/what-falling-house-prices-mean-for-the-ocr-and-the-economy

Kiwibank chief economist Jarrod Kerr said it could be tough going for some people. He said he bought his first house in 2007, which then lost value and did not recover for years. There was a mental element to falling prices, he said.

"With interest rates going up on top of what is being labelled a cost of living crisis, it's unhelpful, it really is. It's not what we should be doing right now, in my opinion."

Bruce Patten, chief executive at New Zealand Financial Services Group, said negative equity was primarily a problem when people needed or wanted to move.

New Zealand Financial Services Group chief executive Bruce Patten. Supplied / NZFSG

"Our recommendation to them is, sit tight for a few more years, until the market starts moving again. So far, touch wood, we haven't had a situation similar to that during the GFC, when there were lots of mortgagee sales with negative equity, leaving people with personal loans after their properties sold and nothing to show for it.

"The main advice is to speak to your adviser if you are struggling. We can help negotiate interest-only payments or repayment holidays in some cases but do your best to ride this point in time out."

Campbell Hastie, of Hastie Mortgages, said he advised people to keep paying their mortgages and try not to think about it. He said he would look at borrowers' equity positions when they came to refix mortgages because people who had bought with less than a 20 percent deposit were usually also paying a low equity premium on top of their interest rates, too.

"The fact of whether your equity position is improving or not in a sense sort of doesn't matter so long as your loan is going down.

Bernard Hickey on why OCR rise will hit those already suffering Morning Report Download MP3 7m

"That's what a principal and interest loan is… so long as you're making your minimum commitment there as long as the bank is concerned, they are not going to squawk at you."

While Kerr said falling house prices could make people more reluctant to invest, such as business people seeking borrowing secured against their home, Otago University economist Murat Ungor said the number was likely too small to make a large difference.

"For those 3600 households, this is real and it is painful. Negative equity is a balance-sheet problem, not a cash-flow one, as long as they keep servicing the mortgage. The bank is not calling the loan provided they keep paying. But it does trap people: they cannot easily sell to move for a better job, and they cannot use their home as collateral to start a business. So there will be individual stories of lost opportunity. But as a drag on national investment or the wider economy? No. This is a personal finance story, not an economic one."

World.title: Times remain tough for the building sector, but firms are adapting to the uncertainty, survey shows
World.content:
The latest Master Builders State of the Sector survey, which polls the mood of member companies and their customers, showed a slight improvement in firms' confidence in their pipeline.

Of those surveyed, 68 percent described their potential forward work as strong or steady, up from 64 percent last year. And fewer Master Builders described their pipeline as being in dire shape compared to last year.

Master Builders chief executive Ankit Sharma said the downturn had been slower and deeper than expected.

"What we are seeing across the sector both residential and commercial, businesses are more resilient, they are managing their cashflow a lot better, based on the data than what we saw four or five years back," he said.

"And they are also spending more time to engage with their customers to try to convert their pipeline into committed work."

As for challenges facing the sector right now, Sharma said cost pressures and problems with consenting had again surfaced.

"Once you get a four, five, or six week delay in consenting that just adds more in terms of managing the costs of delay.

"The biggest change we could have is more consistency across consenting authorities."

While outside building firms' control, weaker consumer demand remained a challenge with 87 percent of Master Builders listing it as a top concern.

Sharma said signs of economic recovery at the end of last year flowed through into 2026 with an uplift in the forward-looking pipeline, but that was thrown off track by the Iran conflict and oil price shock.

"What we are seeing is probably in the last two months there's some normality in the way people are thinking about what's happening with the Iran conflict - it's not a short-term conflict and probably will continue for a period of time, and all prices have been more stable than what we were all anticipating," he said.

World.title: Edith Cavell Bridge to stay closed after Milford Sound quakes
World.content:
Earthquakes renew focus on Milford Sound risks Morning Report Download MP3 6m

Fallen rocks have been removed from the road after last night's earthquakes in the South Island, but a major bridge will remain closed for inspection.

A 5.5-magnitude earthquake hit 40 kilometres northeast of Milford Sound at 6:16pm on Wednesday. That was followed by a 5.6 quake, and three more light to weak aftershocks.

Edith Cavell Bridge would stay closed until engineers had inspected the structure, the Queenstown Lakes District Council said on Thursday.

The bridge crosses the Shotover River in Arthurs Point, about 15 minutes from Queenstown.

"We hope to provide an update around 8.30am pending the outcome of an inspection. In the meantime, traffic from Arthurs Point should detour via Malaghans Road and through Dalefield."

Crews were also working to open one lane of Glenorchy-Queenstown Road.

"The team are aiming to open one lane of Glenorchy-Queenstown Road (between One Mile Roundabout and Sunshine Bay turn-off) from 2pm this afternoon. The lane heading into Queenstown will remain closed until at least Thursday next week while repair work is completed following a recent slip - traffic can still detour over Fernhill Road."

The Queenstown Lakes District Council said minor rockfall on SH6 through the Kawarau Gorge had now been cleared.

More information on tsunami risk being gathered

The tsunami risk at Piopiotahi/ Milford Sound has been known for some time but new science and modelling is underway to understand it better, DOC's Southern, South Island director Aaron Fleming says.

He was talking to Morning Report after Southland's mayor Rob Scott told the programme the tragedy in Nepal should prompt practical preparation for the threat of a tsunami at Piopiotahi /Milford Sound.

DOC now had a communications strategy so that information could be shared with people before they visited the area, Fleming said.

Milford Sound in Fiordland. 123rf

DOC was working with Emergency Management Southland, NEMA and councils as well as businesses operating in the region.

It was important that people understood their options for staying safe if a tsunami was triggered in Milford Sound were limited, he said.

In the next few months modelling would take place to understand the type of wave it would create, its size and its impact.

"That will certainly help us hone our skills in terms of the response and how we can better mitigate the risk."

Fleming said Milford Sound was the eighth wonder of the world and "a visitor magnet" and DOC wanted to encourage people to enjoy it.

During the earthquake that occurred in the area in July people went along the road away from the scene and were able to get to higher ground.

However, he stressed the timeframe to leave was very short.

"The modelling we are doing ...will give us more details around the length of time people will have because it's not a lot of time. But the best thing you can do is if it's long or strong, get to that higher ground."

World.title: Snow resorts wind up business early after warmest winter on record
World.content:
Australian ski resorts are winding up operations early in 2026 after the warmest winter on record.

Along with mild temperatures, winter also brought frequent rain to the high country, preventing a seasonal snowpack from establishing across lower alpine elevations.

This year also marks three very lean years in the past four, continuing the long-term decline in snowfall across the Australian Alps, which is proving to be one of the most tangible signs of our warming climate.

Ski fields above freezing most of winter

This year's snow season was a challenge from the start.

June was unseasonably warm and wet, and when it was not raining, it was mostly too warm for snowmaking at ski resorts.

Heavy rain in late August caused a major melting event and a swelling of the Perisher Creek. (Supplied: SMSkier)

A remarkable statistic for early winter was the Perisher Valley weather station measured 301 millimetres of precipitation from June 1 to July 2, of which only 25mm fell at a temperature below 0 degrees Celsius.

A modest dump of snow finally arrived in July, but the month was generally mild and occasionally rainy; although a snow base developed on higher slopes, a full cover across lower alpine regions never formed.

Last month brought no relief, with further rain and above-average temperatures — during the final days of the month, alpine maximums even climbed above 10C, including a new all-time winter record of 14.4C at Perisher on Saturday, August 29.

Three warmer-than-normal months meant the average winter temperatures across the high country were easily the highest on record, and by a fair margin.

The longest-running BOM station in the Australian alpine region is Cabramurra, where this winter's mean of 4.0C was well above the long-term average of 1.8C and nearly half a degree above the previous record in 2023.

Across the border, the Mount Buller station has been operational since 1985 and also exceeded the previous record by nearly half a degree, coming in at 1.9C versus a long-term average of 0.1C.

Snow depth in 2026 is historically low

Before: Pictures of Frostbite Kiosk at Thredbo on August 30, 2025, versus August 30, 2026. . . After: (Supplied) . . Instructions: Use left and right arrow keys to control image transition Before and after images SLIDE Pictures of Frostbite Kiosk at Thredbo on August 30, 2025, versus August 30, 2026. / (Supplied)

In a typical year, snow accumulates through winter and peaks in August or early September.

However, this year, discounting the improbable arrival of a major polar storm this spring, snow peaked two weeks earlier than average and was at historically low levels, which heavily restricted the amount of open terrain for skiing.

The table below shows peak snow depth in 2026 compared to average; however, there are a few caveats when analysing snow data in Australia*.

What is evident this season is that, for higher elevations, it was the worst season for natural snow since 2006, while for lower regions it was the worst on record.

Despite the setbacks, CEO of Snow Resorts Australia Josh Elliott was confident the industry had the infrastructure to mitigate poor seasons.

"While conditions and available terrain have differed between resorts, continued investment in snowmaking and snow management has meant that skiing, snowboarding and snowplay have been available in NSW, Victoria and the ACT since the June long weekend," he said.

Winter finished with almost no snow cover on many alpine slopes and an early end to the season for most of the terrain. (Supplied: Perisher)

But even extensive snow curation eventually lost out to the elements, and two of the lower resorts, Mount Selwyn and Mount Baw Baw, already shut down operations for the season a fortnight ago.

Mount Hotham is also due for a premature finish this Sunday, and with more heavy rain ahead this weekend, it is hard to see the other major resorts lasting until the traditional closing weekend in early October.

The downhill slide continues

In isolation, a winter without much snow is nothing new in Australia — 1973 and 1982 were both very lean years — but it is the sharp downward trend over recent decades that is concerning.

And unsurprisingly, the marginal lower alpine areas are most vulnerable to a warming climate, since more winter precipitation is now falling as rain, and above-freezing temperatures are melting the snow cover between storms.

Between 1955 and 2000, the peak annual snow depth at Three-Mile Dam, at an elevation of 1,460 metres, averaged 55 centimetres, but during the past 25 years that figure has fallen to 34cm, a reduction of 38 per cent.

A few hundred metres higher, Mount Buller's drop during the corresponding period is 21 per cent, from 117cm to 93cm, while for Spencers Creek at 1,830m, the decline is 13 per cent from 205cm to 178cm.

In other words, the winter snowline is clearly rising, and projections from several studies this century show that by 2050, maximum snow depth at major resorts, relative to the late 20th century, may decline by more than 50 per cent even under a low emissions scenario.

However, Mr Elliott said Australian resorts were leveraging against future climates.

"While those projections may be relevant to understanding changes in the natural alpine environment, they are not forecasts of future skiable terrain, resort operating periods or the visitor experience," he said.

"Snowmaking has been a core component of the Australian snow experience for more than 35 years. New technology, including All-Weather Snowmaking Systems, now allows resorts with these systems to produce snow in ambient temperatures of up to +20C."

*Victorian statistics are sufficiently robust with daily natural snow depth readings taken by resorts; however, Mount Hotham did not report during the COVID-19 winters of 2020 and 2021. In NSW, Perisher and Thredbo quote snow depth data from Snowy Hydro at Spencers Creek, normally measured weekly or fortnightly. Snowy Hydro also takes readings at Deep Creek and Three-Mile Dam, however these datasets suffer from inconsistent measurement intervals, with intervals between readings of up to three weeks.

World.title: Tiger Woods loses driving licence for five years after plea deal
World.content:
Golfing champion Tiger Woods has pleaded no contest to a reckless driving charge following a rollover crash in March near his home in Florida where he initially was accused of driving under the influence.

Woods appeared in a courtroom in Martin County where he agreed to the reduced charge.

A judge ordered that his driver’s licence be suspended for five years.

Woods, 50, said little during the hearing and beforehand sat at the defence table, looking back at the courtroom gallery.

He arrived at the courthouse with his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, President Donald Trump’s former daughter-in-law.

She sat behind him during the hearing. Woods left the courthouse without addressing reporters.

Tiger Woods stands by his overturned vehicle following a crash in Florida. (AP: Jason Oteri)

He also pleaded no contest to refusing to submit to testing and was fined court costs, according to court documents.

A no-contest plea is not an admission of guilt, but means the accused will offer no defence.

The plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal justice system.

Woods was arrested after his SUV clipped a truck and rolled over on its side on a beachside residential road on Jupiter Island.

A sheriff’s report said deputies found two pain pills in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment. He did a Breathalyzer test, which came out negative, but refused to take a urine test.

He had pleaded not guilty to the original DUI charge.

Neither Woods nor the person in the other vehicle were injured in the crash, according to officials.

But his Land Rover caused $US5,000 ($7,000) in damage to the truck, according to a police report. Woods had told a deputy that he was looking down at his phone and changing the radio station when he hit the truck.

Woods is among the most influential figures in golf, but his career has been derailed by multiple back and knee surgeries, car crashes and dependence on pain medication.

Woods has been involved in four crashes over the years.

He took a leave from the golf tour after the 2009 crash and again after the latest crash and has yet to return to tournament play.

He left the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient treatment facility, according to court records.

Woods made his first public appearance since returning from treatment on June 23 when he introduced the PGA Tour’s plans to revamp its schedule for 2028.

Woods remained as chairman of the tour’s Future Competition Committee after his arrest. He did not take questions during that appearance.

AP

World.title: Ciraldo calls out NRL over delayed rule-change communication
World.content:
Cameron Ciraldo wants rule changes for 2027 to be communicated to clubs well in advance of the season's start date as Canterbury prepares to become the latest crash-test dummies in trials for the NRL's kick-off experiment.

With the Bulldogs and Thursday's opponents Brisbane both out of finals contention, the NRL has again opted to stress-test changes to the kick-off rules, where teams conceding a try can opt to kick or receive from the restart.

The concept was widely panned by players in Melbourne's win over Brisbane, and Ciraldo claimed on Wednesday he only learned his team would be guinea pigs in their regular-season game via email.

Beach sprinting was just the start of Damien Cook's NRL story It's been a long time since Damien Cook was known merely as a beach sprint champion, but ahead of the champion hooker's final NRL game, all the old stories are being told one last time.

Ciraldo would have a right to feel aggrieved by the NRL's constant tinkering, given his side were firmly entrenched in the top four last year.

The Dogs slipped back in the pack when the NRL changed the six-again threshold from the 40-metre line to the 20-metre mark weeks out from the season starting.

Canterbury has righted the ship since officials have eased off on calling six-agains.

And while Ciraldo won't solely attribute his club's early-season form slump to the changes, he would prefer clearer communication so clubs can plan their conditioning and roster management accordingly.

"If you look at our form at the start of the year you can blame that, but I think there's a lot of factors that went into our results at the start of the year," Ciraldo said.

"We'll look to address those over the next few weeks.

The Bulldogs have corrected their form of late after referees eased off on the six-again calls. (Getty Images: Brendon Thorne )

"As the rules came back to what they were last year, we sort of found our rhythm a little bit more, and were able to get back to our style of footy.

"I think it coincides with a number of other things as well.

"I think everyone would like to know what the rule changes are to start the pre-season and not find out about them during the trial period."

Ciraldo said Canterbury had little time to put the trialled kick-off interpretations into practice this week.

"I don't check my emails that often, so someone had to tell me," Ciraldo said.

Canterbury's clash with Brisbane will be the last for Bronson Xerri (Melbourne) and Josh Curran (Perth) before they move on to new clubs in 2027.

Ciraldo paid tribute to the pair for being key parts of the Dogs' revival, and confirmed Sean O'Sullivan had agreed to a contract at Belmore for 2027, despite interest from the Super League.

AAP

World.title: AFL boss backflips by scrapping controversial 'Opening Round' experiment
World.content:
The AFL has scrapped the Opening Round experiment after three seasons and will return to a traditional nine-game first week.

League boss Andrew Dillon today confirmed the demise of the much-criticised concept that featured four games played exclusively in Queensland and New South Wales between only a selection of eight clubs.

Designed to build a foothold in rugby league heartland, it instead drew criticism given the fixturing created a staggered start and early-season byes.

Defending it in March, Dillon said Opening Round was "key" to growing the sport north of Victoria, citing record attendances and membership rises.

Australia and England will play a one-off Test next year at the MCG to celebrate 150 years of Test cricket, pushing the AFL season back. (Getty Images: Robbie Stephenson/PA Images)

"What we've found in the last couple of years is that focus on NSW and Queensland is helping to grow awareness in NSW and Queensland and at the same time it hasn't taken away from our round one," Dillon said at the time.

But, with the season to begin a week later next year due to the MCG hosting the 150th anniversary cricket Test between Australia and England, it has been taken out with the trash.

"We have been working through alternative options to deliver the start of the AFL season," Dillon said in a statement.

"After important feedback from fans and stakeholders, and consultation with clubs and broadcasters, round one will see the return of a traditional nine-game round played across the country."

The first round will be played from Wednesday or Thursday, March 17 or 18, just days after the final day of the historic Ashes Test.

The 24-round home-and-away season will conclude on Sunday, August 30, with the five-week finals series beginning with two wildcard finals in the first week of September.

The grand final will be held on Saturday, October 2 and Gather Round in South Australia is locked in for April 8-11.

AAP

World.title: Police speak with four men over Sydney Swans scandal
World.content:
Victoria Police detectives have spoken with four Sydney men as part of their sexual assault investigation linked to the Sydney Swans.

In a statement, police confirmed they travelled to NSW this week.

Sexual Crimes Squad detectives spoke with a 26-year-old Randwick man, a 30-year-old Maroubra man, a 25-year-old Randwick man and a 25-year-old Paddington man.

Investigators say the interview process with the four men has now concluded.

The allegations relate to events at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel where it is understood players were joined by several adult entertainers in the early hours of August 17.

Three women subsequently made a report to police.

No-one has been arrested and no charges have been laid.

Authorities say they also spoke to, or will speak with, three men also believed to be in the hotel room, who are being treated solely as witnesses at this time.

The club stood down five players — vice captain Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordan, Riley Bice and Nick Blakey — for breaching club standards for drinking and bringing women to the hotel in the hours after the team's round 23 clash against Essendon.

Police now believe they have identified all parties who were in the room at the time of the alleged incident.

The investigation into the alleged incident remains ongoing, and Victoria Police said it does not expect to provide any further updates for about eight weeks.

Detectives believe they have identified everyone who was in the hotel room at the time of the alleged incident. (ABC News: Danielle Bonica)

The club released a statement acknowledging the update on Wednesday afternoon.

"The wellbeing of those impacted remains of paramount importance," the Swans said.

"The club again extends its sincere apologies to our members and fans, sponsors and the wider community, along with all of our staff and players across both the women's and men's programs, for the distress and disappointment this matter has caused."

Two separate law firms have been engaged to represent three women considering civil action over the alleged incident.

Their lawyers have previously alleged the women are suffering severe stress and anxiety and may pursue damages.

World.title: Clarkson sacked as Kangaroos hunt 'coach for the modern game'
World.content:
North Melbourne says "gaping holes" within Alastair Clarkson's game plan led to the club parting ways with the veteran senior coach.

Clarkson was contracted with the club until 2027, but the Kangaroos opted to end his tenure early.

Kangaroos president Sonja Hood and head of football Todd Viney both pointed to key game plan issues when questioned on the reasons behind the decision to not proceed with Clarkson into the final year of his deal.

"I think if there was one thing that Clarko did was he tried too hard in trying to fix that, and then therefore what happens is we get into more meetings, more information, and the players at the end of the day become a little bit confused, and we don't get the cohesion that we need to win more games," Viney said.

"There's still parts of our game plan that we haven't been able to improve in the four years, and that's some stuff that we need to get right when we talk to the next coach to bring us in line with where the modern game is right at the moment."

Viney also conceded that Clarkson had been run down by the investigation into racism at Hawthorn under his tenure.

"I'm not sure the scars have fully healed, to this point. He's gone through enormous trauma," he said.

"I'm not sure of the exact impact, but I know it's had an effect. He's been through a lot and he's managed it well and coached us well, but it's definitely had an effect.

" He's not the same bubbly person that I knew early days. "

Despite former Kangaroos stars-turned-coaches Adam Simpson and John Longmire both being on the market, Hood said North Melbourne will run a full process to find its next coach.

Hood added that assistants already at the club who worked under Clarkson are also welcome to throw their hats in the ring for the full-time role.

When questioned over what type of coach the Kangaroos are after, Hood said: "a coach who can coach for the modern game".

Clarkson was blindsided by the club's decision to not proceed with him into 2027, with Hood saying he was "upset" by the call.

Despite Clarkson being Hood's star hire four years ago, she envisages continuing in her role as president, while Viney also said he was prepared to remain at North Melbourne.

Former Swans premiership coach John Longmire (pictured) has been linked with the Kangaroos vacancy, but will need to go through a process if he wants the job. (Getty Images: Morgan Hancock)

Clarkson released a statement in response to his exit via his manager James Henderson.

"My time as coach of the North Melbourne Football Club has come to an end," he said.

"We set out to stabilise the club and lay the foundations for a return to playing deep in September.

"The challenge was a difficult one that I embraced with my whole being.

"My family and I have been privileged to be involved in AFL football for over 40 years, but it is now time for a new chapter."

The Kangaroos will begin their coach search next week, and Hood said there is no timeline on when an appointment should be made official, despite the trade period taking place next month.

Hood said the Kangaroos were in a better position now than when Clarkson took over, but the club wanted more success over the next four years.

"We asked Alastair to give our club stability and strength and help return us to the top of the AFL ladder," she said.

"Four years later, we have created an environment where our staff and players want to be at our club. This is a testament to the culture Alastair has helped create and the belief that he has built in this group.

"Although we have clearly made progress and won more games, we won't shy away from our desire to want more from this talented group.

"We are incredibly grateful to Alastair for the work he's done over the last four years and we wish him all the very best for his next chapter."

Live Moment Look back at North Melbourne president Sonja Hood and football boss Todd Viney's press conference after Alastair Clarkson was relieved of his duties as Kangaroos coach. What was going to happen next year? Did the North Board refuse a contract extension prior to the 2027 season? Did the want Clarkson to coach for his future? - Roos Member From what Hood said, they determined that they weren't going to extend Clarkson beyond 2027, therefore believed that it would be unfair to expect him to coach next season. Is it time for Simpson or Longmire? I think it's the right thing to do. He has laid a foundation but it needs a new voice to get that bit more. I prefer Simmo to Horse and think he could really push this group forward. - Nathan Hood wasn't prepared to say they're the preferred candidate, but both of their reactions will be interesting. The stuff about a modern coach makes me think they'll go for a highly-credentialled assistant. Should the players be blamed? Why get rid of a 4 time premiership coach with 1 more year left. Makes no sense. Maybe players should be held more accountable. - Davo It is interesting, Davo, that the players often seem to skirt responsibility with this kind of stuff. I guess it's easier to remove one employee than multiple. At the end of the day, this is a players' league. Show more

Under Clarkson, North won 20 of its 82 AFL matches, including nine this season. Clarkson took over the Kangaroos after the club had collected back-to-back wooden spoons in 2022 and 2021, while also finishing second-last in 2020.

North has not made the finals in a decade, when the club made consecutive preliminary finals in 2014 and 2015 and an elimination final in 2016 under Brad Scott.

The 2026 season was North's best under Clarkson, and most successful since 2019, with the Kangaroos finishing 14th on the ladder with nine wins.

World.title: Ferrari's Schumacher-inspired livery, F1 leader to cop penalty in Italy
World.content:
Ferrari will be celebrating the legacy of Michael Schumacher this weekend at its home race, with a special livery dedicated to the seven-time Formula 1 world champion.

This year marks 30 years since Schumacher joined the Scuderia, and 20 years since his final F1 victory in the 2006 Chinese Grand Prix.

Piastri searching for answers as teammate re-enters F1 title picture Oscar Piastri's "disappointing" end to the Dutch Grand Prix leaves the Australian and his McLaren team searching for answers, while his teammate has roared back into the Formula 1 title picture.

With Schumacher at the wheel, Ferrari rose to the top of F1 after years spent without championships.

Ferrari's constructors' championship win in 1999 ended a 16-year wait in the teams' competition, while Schumacher's drivers' championship triumph in 2000 made him the first Ferrari race to become world champion since Jody Scheckter in 1979.

Schumacher won five of his seven drivers' championships with Ferrari, from 2000-2004.

This weekend at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza, a race Schumacher won five times with Ferrari, the Scuderia has a one-off livery which pays tribute to the F1 champion.

Among the features are seven stars on the nose of the car, representing Schumacher's world titles, and drivers Lewis Hamilton — the sport's other seven-time world champion — and Charles Leclerc will wear racing suits that also feature the seven stars and Schumacher's logo.

F1 championship leader to take grid penalty at Monza

Kimi Antonelli has celebrated his 20th birthday as the Formula 1 drivers' championship leader, and heads into his home grand prix with a significant 59-point advantage over his two nearest rivals.

F1 drivers' championship leader Kimi Antonelli is set to start the Italian Grand Prix from the back of the grid. (Reiters: Benoit Tessier)

But the youngest-ever leader of the F1 championship heads into this weekend's race at Monza knowing he has work to do to be near the front of the grid.

Mercedes announced during the previous race weekend in the Netherlands that Antonelli will take an engine penalty this weekend.

F1 teams have an allocation of power unit components they can use in a season. When a driver is fitted with a power unit component that exceeds the allocation, they are handed a penalty at the first event that new part is used.

Mercedes has had multiple power unit issues this year, with Antonelli failing to finish in Barcelona and teammate George Russell suffering issues in Canada and Belgium.

Despite the Italian Grand Prix being Antonelli's home race, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said now was the right time to do it for the championship leader.

"Our calculations say that that's the best track to take it," Wolff said.

"Obviously, algorithms don't take their nationality into consideration. We're here to fight for a championship and not get the most PR. So yeah, that's what we're going to do."

Monza, known as the Temple of Speed, is expected to be a strong track for Mercedes, which is likely why it is taking the penalty now.

With long straights, there should be plenty of opportunities for Antonelli to pass with his impressive Mercedes power unit.

Monza has been the scene of impressive drives through the field in recent years.

Pierre Gasly won from 10th on the grid driving for AlphaTauri (now Racing Bulls). Max Verstappen won in 2022 after taking a five-place grid penalty, while Lewis Hamilton charged from the last row on the grid to place fifth.

Last year, Isack Hadjar started in the pit lane for Racing Bulls and was able to finish 10th.

ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix from 9pm AEST on Sunday, September 6.

World.title: Bledisloe Cup quadruple-header announced as sevens added to ticket
World.content:
Australia's sevens teams will share the stage in a scheduling first, with the Wallabies and Wallaroos creating a Bledisloe Cup quadruple-header in Sydney.

The Stadium Australia Test against the All Blacks on October 17 already had a support act secured, with the Wallaroos due to host Scotland for the first time in their WXV Global Series clash.

Kick-off times for Bledisloe Cup in Sydney Wallaroos v Scotland, 12pm

Australian sevens men v Fiji, 2:05pm

Australian sevens women v New Zealand, 2.25pm

Wallabies v New Zealand, 3:45pm All times in AEDT

Now two more fixtures will be added to the ticket, with Australia's world champion sevens women to face rivals New Zealand and the men up against two-time Olympic gold medallists Fiji.

"This is an historic moment for Australian rugby, with all four of our Teams In Gold competing on the same pitch, on the same day, on an unmissable occasion," Rugby Australia chief executive Phil Waugh told AAP.

"The day will showcase the very best of rugby with our elite male and female players across the XVs and Sevens formats taking on famous rivals from around the world in an unprecedented line-up of international rugby.

"We look forward to celebrating this extraordinary occasion with our great Australian rugby community and we thank our friends from New Zealand Rugby, Fiji Rugby Union and Scottish Rugby for helping make this day a reality."

The Wallaroos will begin the action before the men's and women's sevens outfits take the field, followed by the Wallabies, who will complete the four-course menu with a late afternoon kick-off at the venue set to host next year's World Cup final.

AAP

Tech.title: Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model ‘works harder’ but might cost more
Tech.content:
is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, arriving just a few weeks after its predecessor. The company claims the new model “works harder” than Gemini 3.7 Flash by performing more reasoning steps on complex tasks and “calling tools iteratively.” It has the same introductory pricing as 3.7 Flash, $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, but could still end up costing users more. Google warns that “the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels.” Developers can keep using Gemini 3.7 Flash if they want to minimize token usage.

Gemini 3.8 Flash’s launch was followed by some early impressions online. Artificial Analysis highlighted the model’s pricing, saying Gemini 3.8 Flash is “the cheapest we’ve measured at this level of intelligence. This is up ~40% from Gemini 3.7 Flash despite unchanged per-token pricing, driven by a 30% increase in output tokens per task and more turns on agentic evaluations.”

Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis compared Gemini 3.8 Flash to Anthropic’s models, saying it offers “Opus 5 coding quality but at a fraction of the cost and super fast,” adding, “This is going to be so awesome for things like making remotion videos.”

Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash offers “significant improvements” for software engineering and autonomous AI agents. It outperforms its predecessor and other frontier models on the DeepSWE v1.1 software engineering benchmark, including Anthropic’s Fable 5, which got an upgrade earlier this week that also promises stronger performance at a lower price, by cutting the price to use cached data.

Google’s new model also outperformed its competitors on the Vals Finance Agent V2 benchmark and Harvey’s Legal Agent benchmark. However, the new model also “ships with safeguards against misuse in the domains of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cyber offense.”

Google also released Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber alongside its new Fairwind Program, which is limited to governments and “trusted partners.” The program, whose 650 members include CrowdStrike and the Center for Internet Security, offers access to 3.8 Flash Cyber and Google’s CodeMender agent, which Google says can help “autonomously find and fix vulnerabilities, protecting critical infrastructure, public services, and national security.” Gemini 3.8 Flash is available now for consumers with a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, as well as developers and enterprise users.
